lessons.title: The Many Ways I Support Lives

activities.prompt: How does one river quietly help so many people live and thrive?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A River Helps Everyone
activities.body: Rivers are like kind friends who help us every day. Since ancient times, people have built homes near rivers. The Godavari gives water to many towns and villages around it. We drink, cook and wash with its water. It helps fields grow food and helps factories make things. Its water travels through pipes and canals and is shared by many. Ecotourism lets us enjoy nature without harming it.
keyPoints: People have built homes near rivers since ancient times.
The Godavari gives water for drinking, cooking, washing, farming and factories.
River water travels through pipes and canals and is shared by many.
Ecotourism means enjoying nature without harming it.
activities.explanation: One river can touch many lives in one day.

activities.prompt: A new town is being built far away from any river. The builder says, 'We can build anywhere. Water is not a problem.' Do you agree? Why do towns often come up near rivers?
steps: People need water every day to drink, cook and wash, so a town cannot work without it.
A river gives water to houses, schools and fields around it, so a town near a river gets water easily.
The river water can be carried in pipes and canals, so it can reach every home and farm.
So the builder is wrong: towns grow near rivers because rivers support many lives and livelihoods.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Long ago, why did many people build their homes near rivers?
options: Because rivers were quiet at night
Because rivers had no animals
Because rivers gave them water
activities.explanation: Water is what we need most, so homes grew close to rivers.

activities.prompt: The Godavari gives water to many towns and villages around it.
activities.explanation: Yes! Many people depend on the Godavari for their water.

activities.prompt: Match each way a river helps with what makes it happen.
activities.explanation: The same river water helps farmers, workers and nature lovers.

activities.prompt: Put the journey of river water in the correct order.
items: Water flows in the river
Water is carried in pipes and canals
Water reaches houses, schools and fields
People drink, cook, wash and grow food
activities.explanation: Water travels from the river through pipes and canals before it reaches you.

activities.prompt: Meena lives near the Godavari. Her family grows food, and a nearby factory makes things. How does the river support them both?
options: It gives water for the fields and the factory
It gives them free toys every day
It stops all rain from falling
activities.explanation: River water helps crops grow and helps factories make things, so it supports many livelihoods.

activities.prompt: The Chenab rail bridge is the highest railway ______ bridge in the world.
activities.hint: Think of the curved shape, like a rainbow.
activities.explanation: Well done! The Chenab rail bridge is the highest railway arch bridge in the world.

activities.prompt: Two villages are near the same river. One village is right next to it. The other is far away, but pipes carry water to it. Both villages get water every day. Why does the far village also get water?
options: Rain fills its tanks, so pipes are not needed at all.
Pipes and canals carry river water to far places.
The far village dug wells that never go dry.
Trucks bring river water to the far village daily.

why.Rain fills its tanks, so pipes are not n: This assumes rain is enough, but the fact says pipes carry the river water.
why.The far village dug wells that never go: Wells are not mentioned; the water that reaches people comes from the river.
why.Trucks bring river water to the far vill: Trucks are not how the river water travels; pipes and canals carry it.

activities.explanation: Right: river water is carried in pipes and canals, so it reaches places far from the river.

activities.prompt: A farmer's field is near the Godavari. There was very little rain this year. Still, his plants grow well and he gets a good crop. Why did his plants grow?
options: River water reached his field through canals.
Plants do not need water when it is hot.
Little rain makes plants grow faster and bigger.
His field got water from a factory nearby.

This is a wrong idea about plants; all plants need water to grow.
why.Little rain makes plants grow faster and: This is a common mistake; less rain means less water, not better growth.
why.His field got water from a factory nearb: Factories use river water to make things, not to water crop fields.

activities.explanation: Right: the river helps people grow food, and its water reaches fields through canals.

activities.prompt: Ravi says, 'The river only helps people who drink its water.' His sister points to a factory by the river and to green fields near it. What is wrong with Ravi's claim?
options: He forgot the river also helps cooking and washing.
He forgot the river helps farms and factories too.
He forgot that rivers flow only during the rainy season.
He forgot that river water is too dirty to drink.

why.He forgot the river also helps cooking a: That is true but it is still only about using water at home, not the main flaw.
why.He forgot that rivers flow only during t: Rivers giving water all year is not the mistake in his claim.
why.He forgot that river water is too dirty: The facts say people drink the river water, so this is not the flaw.

activities.explanation: Right: the river helps grow food, make things in factories and support many livelihoods, not just drinking.

activities.prompt: Four friends visit a forest. They watch birds, take photos and learn about trees. They carry back all their rubbish and do not harm anything. What is this kind of visit called?
options: Ecotourism, because they enjoy nature without harming it.
Ecotourism, because they took many photos of birds.
A picnic, because they carried their rubbish back.
A school trip, because they learned about the trees.

why.Ecotourism, because they took many photo: Taking photos alone is not the reason; the key is enjoying nature without harming it.
why.A picnic, because they carried their rub: A picnic is not the word for visiting nature to learn and watch birds.
why.A school trip, because they learned abou: Learning is part of it, but a school trip is not the word being taught here.

activities.explanation: Right: ecotourism means enjoying nature, watching animals or birds and learning, without harming the environment.

activities.prompt: One river gives water to five towns through pipes. Four towns use only a little water each. The fifth town leaves its taps open all day and wastes a lot. What will happen to the other four towns?
options: They will get more water because taps stay open.
They will get less water because water is shared.
Nothing will change; each town makes its own water.
They will get sea water instead of river water.

why.They will get more water because taps st: This is backwards; one town wasting cannot give more to the others.
why.Nothing will change; each town makes its: Towns do not make their own river water; they all share the same river.
why.They will get sea water instead of river: Sea water is not part of this; the towns share the river's water.

activities.explanation: Right: the river's water is shared by many, so wasting it leaves less for others.

activities.prompt: Meera says the Chenab rail bridge is the highest railway arch bridge in the world. Arjun says, 'A bridge in my town is taller than my house, so it is the highest in the world.' What is the flaw in Arjun's thinking?
options: He compared the bridge with a house, not with all railway arch bridges.
He forgot that bridges are only built over rivers and valleys.
He forgot that tall bridges cannot carry heavy trains.
He counted bridges in his town, not bridges in his school.

why.He forgot that bridges are only built ov: Where bridges are built does not decide which one is highest.
why.He forgot that tall bridges cannot carry: The Chenab rail bridge carries trains, so this idea is wrong.
why.He counted bridges in his town, not brid: Comparing with a school makes no sense; the comparison must be with all railway arch bridges.

activities.explanation: Right: 'highest in the world' means comparing with every railway arch bridge, not with a house.

lessons.title: Dams — Storing My Water, Changing My Flow

activities.prompt: Where does the water in your tap come from?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What Does a Dam Do?
activities.body: Have you ever wondered where tap water comes from? A dam is like a giant wall that blocks a river's flow. The blocked water gathers in a big water body called a reservoir. More than 900 dams store the water of the Godavari river. This stored water helps many people, even in dry seasons.
keyPoints: A dam is like a giant wall that blocks a river.
The stored water gathers in a large water body called a reservoir.
More than 900 dams store Godavari's water for many people.
activities.explanation: A dam stops the river so its water can be saved and shared.

activities.prompt: It has not rained for many weeks. But when Riya opens the tap at home, water still comes out. Her little brother asks, 'Where is the water coming from if there is no rain?' Riya wants to reason it out.
steps: The tap water must come from somewhere, because taps do not make water themselves.
Long ago, when there was rain, dams blocked the river and stored the water in a reservoir.
The stored water was kept safe, so people can use it even in this dry season.
So the water in Riya's tap comes from water a dam stored when it rained.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Stored Water at Work
activities.body: Stored water does many jobs. We drink it, use it to grow crops, and make electricity from it. When you open a tap, it is hard to imagine the water's long journey. Dams also flood land where animals and people once lived. So use water wisely, and never waste a drop.
keyPoints: Stored water is used to drink, grow crops and make electricity.
Building dams floods land, so some people must leave their homes.
It is important to use water wisely and never waste it.
activities.explanation: Every drop of tap water has travelled a long way to reach you.

activities.prompt: A dam is most like which of these?
options: A giant boat
A giant wall
A giant bridge
A giant tent
activities.explanation: A dam is like a giant wall that blocks the river's flow. Well spotted!

activities.prompt: More than ______ dams store the water of the Godavari river.
activities.hint: Think of the big number you read in the lesson.
activities.explanation: More than 900 dams store Godavari's water. That is a lot of dams!

activities.prompt: Why do dams store water for people?
options: So rivers can flow faster
So fish can swim deeper
So people can use it in dry seasons
So the water can get warmer
activities.explanation: Dams store water so people can use it even during dry seasons. Great thinking!

activities.prompt: Match each use of stored water with its example.
activities.explanation: Stored water helps us drink, grow crops and make electricity.

activities.prompt: When a dam is built, what hard thing happens to many families?
options: They must leave their homes and shift elsewhere
They get a new school nearby
They receive free electricity forever
activities.explanation: Dams flood land where people lived, so many families have to shift elsewhere. It is a real sacrifice.

activities.prompt: Put the journey of tap water in the correct order.
items: A giant dam wall blocks the river's flow
The water gathers in a big reservoir
You open a tap at home and water flows out
activities.explanation: The dam blocks the river, water gathers in the reservoir, then it reaches your tap. Now you know the journey!

activities.prompt: It has not rained for many weeks. Meena opens her tap. Water still comes out. Dams on the river stored water long ago. Why does water still come out?
options: The dam saved water, so people can use it in dry seasons.
The rain is falling inside the pipes right now.
The river flows very fast even without any rain.
The tap makes fresh water by itself every day.

why.The rain is falling inside the pipes rig: Wrong. Rain does not fall inside pipes; the water was stored earlier.
why.The river flows very fast even without a: Wrong. Without rain the river is low; the stored water is what helps.
why.The tap makes fresh water by itself ever: Wrong. Taps do not make water; they only let stored water out.

activities.explanation: Right. Dams store water so people can use it even in dry seasons.

activities.prompt: A giant wall will be built across the river near Aman's village. The wall will flood the land around it. What will happen to Aman's family?
options: They will have to leave their home and shift elsewhere.
Their home will stay dry and safe in the water.
The river will move far away from their village.
The dam will send a tap with water to them.

why.Their home will stay dry and safe in the: Wrong. The land will flood, so the home will not stay dry.
why.The river will move far away from their: Wrong. The wall blocks the river; the river does not move away.
why.The dam will send a tap with water to th: Wrong. A dam stores water in a reservoir; it does not give taps.

activities.explanation: Right. Dams flood land, so many people must leave and shift elsewhere.

activities.prompt: Dev says, 'Water comes from taps, so wasting it is fine.' Water travels a long journey before it reaches a tap. What is wrong with Dev's claim?
options: Tap water has a long journey, so we must not waste it.
Taps make new water, so wasting water is always fine.
Wasting water is fine only in the dry season.
Only dams waste water, and taps never waste any.

why.Taps make new water, so wasting water is: Wrong. Taps do not make water; they only release stored water.
why.Wasting water is fine only in the dry se: Wrong. Water is precious in every season, not just the dry one.
why.Only dams waste water, and taps never wa: Wrong. Dams store water to help people; wasting happens when we misuse it.

activities.explanation: Right. It is hard to imagine the water's journey, so we must use water wisely.

activities.prompt: Gauri says, 'Every island must be in the sea.' Majuli is the world's largest river island. It is formed by the Brahmaputra river. What is wrong with Gauri's claim?
options: Some islands form in rivers, like Majuli in the Brahmaputra.
Majuli is really in the sea, so Gauri is right.
Islands can only ever form inside the deep sea.
Majuli is not an island because rivers are small.

why.Majuli is really in the sea, so Gauri is: Wrong. Majuli is formed by a river, not by the sea.
why.Islands can only ever form inside the de: Wrong. Majuli shows that islands can form in rivers too.
why.Majuli is not an island because rivers a: Wrong. Majuli is an island, and the Brahmaputra is a river that formed it.

activities.explanation: Right. Majuli is a river island formed by the Brahmaputra, so islands need not be in the sea.

activities.prompt: The Godavari river has more than 900 dams on it. The dams store its water in reservoirs. Many people need this water. Why do people build so many dams on one river?
options: To store enough water for many people to use.
To stop all the fish from swimming in it.
To make the river go dry in the summer.
To build a big island like Majuli on it.

why.To stop all the fish from swimming in it: Wrong. Dams are built to store water for people, not to stop fish.
Wrong. Dams store water so it can be used in dry seasons, not to dry the river.
Wrong. Islands like Majuli are formed by rivers, not built by dams.

activities.explanation: Right. Stored water helps many people to drink, grow crops and make electricity.

lessons.sceneCaption: A dam is like a giant wall that blocks a river and stores water in a large reservoir.

lessons.title: What Pollutes Me and Why it Matters

activities.prompt: What sneaky things hide in a river even when it looks clean?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A River Speaks: What Pollutes Me?
activities.body: Hello! I am a river. Many people and factories live near my banks. Their waste, plastic and dirty water flow into me. Sometimes I do not smell or look clean. Fish, turtles and birds have nowhere else to go, so they slowly begin to disappear. I wish people would keep me clean and free from waste.
keyPoints: People and factories near the banks pollute the river with waste, plastic and dirty water.
Sometimes the river does not smell or look clean.
Fish, turtles and birds are slowly beginning to disappear.
The river wishes people would keep it clean and free from waste.
activities.explanation: The river gives so much to us. Keeping it clean keeps everyone healthy and happy.

activities.prompt: A boy looks at the river near his home. The water looks clear and pretty. His friend says it is safe to drink. Is the friend right?
steps: The water looks clean, but looks can trick us, because harmful things like chemicals can hide in water.
Dirty soapy water and chemicals mix in and cannot be seen, so a clean look does not mean clean water.
If people drink or use this water, the hidden harmful things could make them sick.
So the friend is wrong, because even clear river water may carry things that hurt living beings.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Hidden Dangers and a Way to Help
activities.body: Careful! Harmful things like chemicals or dirty soapy water can hide in rivers. Even clean-looking water may carry things that hurt living beings. So what can we do? One important way is to create less waste by using eco-friendly products. The river wishes people would keep it clean and free from waste.
keyPoints: Chemicals and dirty soapy water can hide in rivers.
Clean-looking water may still hurt living beings.
Using eco-friendly products creates less waste and helps the river.
activities.explanation: You cannot always see pollution, so the smartest way is to make less waste in the first place.

activities.prompt: What pollutes a river when many people and factories live near its banks?
options: Clean rain and fresh air
Waste, plastic and dirty water
Fish, turtles and birds
Fresh water from the hills
activities.explanation: Waste, plastic and dirty water from the banks flow into the river and pollute it.

activities.prompt: If river water looks clean, it is always safe for living beings.
activities.explanation: Even when water looks clean, it may carry things that hurt living beings. Harmful things can hide in rivers.

activities.prompt: Fish, turtles and birds have nowhere else to go, so they slowly begin to ______.
activities.hint: Think about what happens when a home is spoilt.
activities.explanation: The river is their only home. When it is polluted, these animals slowly begin to disappear.

activities.prompt: How do fertilisers from farms hurt a river?
options: They make plants and organisms grow very fast
They make the river water taste sweet
They help fish swim much faster
They wash all the plastic away
activities.explanation: Fertilisers get washed into the water. They make plants and other organisms grow very fast, which slowly chokes all life inside the river.

activities.prompt: Match each cause with what it does to the river.
activities.explanation: Each of these harms the river in its own way. Together they choke the life inside it.

activities.prompt: Using eco-friendly products is one important way to create less waste and help the river.
activities.explanation: Well done! Creating less waste with eco-friendly products is an important way to keep the river clean.

activities.prompt: Put these events in the correct order to show how fertilisers choke a river.
items: Fertilisers used to grow crops get washed into the water
Plants and other organisms grow very fast
The fast growth slowly chokes all life inside the river
Fish, turtles and birds slowly begin to disappear
activities.explanation: First fertilisers wash in, then growth speeds up, then life is choked, and finally animals begin to disappear. You spotted the whole chain!

activities.prompt: Riya fills a bottle with river water. It looks clear and has no smell. She says it is safe to drink. What is the flaw in her claim?
options: Clear water is safe only if the bottle is new and shut.
Harmful things like chemicals can hide even in clear water.
River water is always safe because rivers clean themselves.
She must smell it again, as smell alone shows safety.

why.Clear water is safe only if the bottle i: This thinks the bottle matters, not what is inside the water.
why.River water is always safe because river: This believes rivers can make all water safe, which is not so.
why.She must smell it again, as smell alone: This thinks smell alone can show hidden harmful things.

activities.explanation: Right. Even when water looks clean, it may carry things that hurt living beings.

activities.prompt: Over many years, a polluted river keeps getting dirtier. What will happen to the fish, turtles and birds living there?
options: They will find new homes in the same dirty river.
They will slowly begin to disappear because they have nowhere else to go.
They will grow used to the dirt and become stronger.
They will move into the factories and live near the pipes.

why.They will find new homes in the same dir: This thinks new homes can be found inside the same river.
why.They will grow used to the dirt and beco: This thinks animals can simply adapt to any amount of dirt.
why.They will move into the factories and li: This thinks factories are safe homes for wild animals.

activities.explanation: Right. Fish, turtles and birds have nowhere else to go, so they are slowly beginning to disappear.

lessons.title: When a River Floods, Runs Dry and Saving Water

activities.prompt: What happens when a river grows too big or disappears?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Gentle River and the Powerful River
activities.body: Most of the time, a river flows gently and helps life grow. But the river never forgets that it is powerful. When there is too much rain, the river expands. It becomes faster, deeper and bigger. Then it overflows its banks and floods large areas. That is when the river shows its power.
keyPoints: Most of the time, the river flows gently and helps life grow.
Too much rain makes the river faster, deeper and bigger.
Then the river overflows its banks and floods large areas.
activities.explanation: A river can be gentle and powerful at the same time.

activities.prompt: Ravi's village has many trees near the river. Meena's village cut down all its trees. One night, heavy rain falls on both villages. Which village will have more trouble from the river?
steps: Heavy rain makes the river bigger, faster and deeper, so it may overflow.
In Ravi's village, trees slow the rainwater down and the soil soaks it up.
In Meena's village, no trees means water runs off the land very fast.
So Meena's village gets more flooding, because trees were not there to slow the water.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: When the River Runs Dry
activities.body: A river can also run dry. This causes great problems for people. Families may have to leave their homes and move to places where water is available. The Godavari is perennial, so it flows across the year and can look after everyone along its way. We can all help by saving water in small ways every day.
keyPoints: A dry river causes great problems for people.
Families may move to places where water is available.
The Godavari flows across the year, so it can look after everyone.
We can save water by doing small things every day.
activities.explanation: A river that flows all year is a friend to everyone along its banks.

activities.prompt: There is too much rain for many days. What happens to the river?
options: It becomes faster, deeper and bigger
It becomes slower, shallower and smaller
It stops flowing completely
It becomes salty and warm
activities.explanation: Too much rain makes the river expand, so it grows faster, deeper and bigger.

activities.prompt: Most of the time, the river flows gently and helps life grow.
activities.explanation: The river is usually gentle and kind to the plants, animals and people near it.

activities.prompt: Floodwater covers Meera's village. Why do her family and the animals leave their homes?
options: To stay safe from the expanding waters
To find more rain for their fields
To make the river flow gently again
To help the soil soak up water
activities.explanation: Expanding waters flood houses, fields and roads, so people and animals move away to stay safe.

activities.prompt: Trees slow down rainwater and help the soil ______ up water.
activities.hint: Think of a sponge drinking water.
activities.explanation: Tree roots and soil work like a sponge, holding the rainwater gently.

activities.prompt: Match each idea with what it means.
activities.explanation: Floods and dry rivers both trouble people, but saving water every day helps us all.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to show how a flood happens.
items: Too much rain falls
The river becomes faster, deeper and bigger
Water overflows the banks
Floods cover houses, fields and roads
People and animals leave to stay safe
activities.explanation: Heavy rain makes the river grow until it spills over, and then people move to safety.

activities.prompt: The river is flowing gently today. Boats move on it and plants grow near it. Then it rains very hard for many days. What will the river most likely do?
options: It will stay gentle and small like before.
It will become bigger, faster and deeper.
It will dry up and stop flowing.
It will flow backwards away from the fields.

why.It will stay gentle and small like befor: This forgets that too much rain changes the river.
This mixes up flooding with a river running dry.
why.It will flow backwards away from the fie: Rivers do not flow backwards when it rains.

activities.explanation: Right: too much rain makes the river expand and overflow.

activities.prompt: A river floods and water covers houses, fields and roads. A family lives near the river. Why should they leave their home for some days?
options: Because the flood water has made their home unsafe.
Because they want to go on a holiday trip.
Because the river always dries up in the rainy time.
Because trees near their house drink all the flood water.

why.Because they want to go on a holiday tri: A flood is not a holiday; it is dangerous.
why.Because the river always dries up in the: Floods happen when there is too much water, not too little.
why.Because trees near their house drink all: Trees help with flooding, but they do not empty a flooded house.

activities.explanation: Right: expanding waters flood houses, so people leave to stay safe.

activities.prompt: Two hills are next to a river. Hill A has many trees. On Hill B, all the trees were cut down. The same heavy rain falls on both hills. What will happen on Hill B?
options: Water will soak into the soil faster than on Hill A.
Water will run off the land faster and cause flooding.
Water will stay on the hill and never reach the river.
Water will turn gentle because the soil is bare.

why.Water will soak into the soil faster tha: This is backwards; trees help soil soak up water, not bare soil.
why.Water will stay on the hill and never re: Runoff water does flow down and can reach the river.
why.Water will turn gentle because the soil: Bare land makes water faster, not gentler.

activities.explanation: Right: no trees means water runs off faster and causes flooding.

activities.context: Meena lives in a village near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra. One rainy day, she sees a tiny stream beginning its journey down from the high Western Ghats. She follows it on her way to school and notices it getting wider and stronger. Her grandmother tells her that this little stream is the start of a very long journey that ends at the sea.
activities.prompt: Meena follows the stream for many weeks and sees rain falling and other streams flowing into it. What will most likely happen to the stream as she keeps following it?
options: It will become wider and stronger
It will become narrower and weaker
It will stop flowing altogether
It will turn back towards the hills

why.It will become narrower and weaker: This is the opposite of what happens when water is added.
why.It will stop flowing altogether: Rivers keep flowing; nothing in the case suggests it would dry up.
why.It will turn back towards the hills: Rivers flow downhill towards the sea, not backwards to where they began.

activities.explanation: Correct: joining streams and rainwater make a river grow wider and stronger as it moves.

activities.context: Meena lives in a village near Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra. One rainy day, she sees a tiny stream beginning its journey down from the high Western Ghats. She follows it on her way to school and notices it getting wider and stronger. Her grandmother tells her that this little stream is the start of a very long journey that ends at the sea.
activities.prompt: Meena wants to find where the stream's journey finally ends. What should she do to find out?
options: Follow the direction of the flow towards the Bay of Bengal
Walk uphill back to the moonlit forest
Dig a new channel to the sea herself
Wait for the stream to flow back to her village

why.Walk uphill back to the moonlit forest: The journey goes away from the hills, not back up into them.
why.Dig a new channel to the sea herself: The river already has its own path to the sea; no digging is needed.
why.Wait for the stream to flow back to her: Rivers do not reverse direction; they keep moving forward.

activities.explanation: Correct: rivers flow from the mountains to the sea, so following the flow leads to where it joins the sea.

activities.prompt: Explain why the Godavari becomes wider and stronger on its journey from Trimbakeshwar to the sea.
activities.answer: The Godavari starts as a small stream at Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats. As it flows, rainwater and many other streams join it. These joining streams, called tributaries, add more and more water. Because of this extra water, the river becomes wider and stronger as it travels towards the Bay of Bengal.
points: Starts as a small stream at Trimbakeshwar
Rainwater and other streams join it
Joining streams are called tributaries
Extra water makes it wider and stronger
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: During Godavari Pushkaram, Meera's family travels to the river, which flows all year and is called Dakshina Ganga because it is sacred and flows through southern India. On the way, they pass rich forests full of wildlife like the tiger, barking deer and Indian golden gecko, and see famed red sandalwood trees. Meera learns the river finally reaches the sea, spreads into many small streams and forms a delta at the Coringa Mangrove Forests, where its journey ends.
activities.prompt: A small stream near Meera's village flows only when it rains, and it dries up completely in summer. What will most likely happen to the fish and other creatures living in that stream during summer?
options: They will have to move to another water body that still has water, or they will die.
They will be safe because the stream flows all year like the Godavari.
They will turn the dry stream bed into a delta.
They will move into the red sandalwood trees nearby.

why.They will be safe because the stream flo: Wrong: only a perennial river like the Godavari flows all year; this stream is seasonal.
why.They will turn the dry stream bed into a: Wrong: a delta forms where a river meets the sea, not in a dry village stream.
why.They will move into the red sandalwood t: Wrong: trees are not a water home for fish and water creatures.

activities.explanation: Correct: a seasonal river dries without rain, so freshwater creatures must shift or perish.

activities.context: During Godavari Pushkaram, Meera's family travels to the river, which flows all year and is called Dakshina Ganga because it is sacred and flows through southern India. On the way, they pass rich forests full of wildlife like the tiger, barking deer and Indian golden gecko, and see famed red sandalwood trees. Meera learns the river finally reaches the sea, spreads into many small streams and forms a delta at the Coringa Mangrove Forests, where its journey ends.
activities.prompt: On a boat ride near the coast, the boatman points out many small streams of water spreading out. Why has the river split like this at this spot?
options: Because pilgrims take a holy dip here during Pushkaram.
Because the river has reached the sea, the end of its journey, and spreads out.
Because tigers and barking deer come here to drink.
Because red sandalwood trees grow on the banks here.

why.Because pilgrims take a holy dip here du: Wrong: the holy dip happens during Pushkaram, but it does not cause the river to split.
why.Because tigers and barking deer come her: Wrong: wildlife lives in the forests along the river, not where it splits at the sea.
why.Because red sandalwood trees grow on the: Wrong: red sandalwood trees grow in the forests, not at the river's end.

activities.explanation: Correct: when the river reaches the sea it spreads into many small streams and forms a delta.

activities.prompt: How does the Godavari's journey end? Explain what happens when the river reaches the sea.
activities.answer: When the Godavari reaches the sea, it spreads into many small streams and forms a delta. This place is called the Coringa Mangrove Forests, and the river's journey ends there. Being a freshwater source, the river is home to many plants and animals along its whole route.
points: River spreads into many small streams at the sea.
A delta is formed.
Names the Coringa Mangrove Forests.
States that the journey ends there.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Ravi's town stands on the banks of the Godavari. Water from the river reaches every house and school through pipes, and flows along canals to the fields where farmers raise crops. A factory by the river uses water too. Last month, a group of visitors came to walk along the banks, watch birds and learn about the plants there, taking care not to disturb anything. Ravi noticed that farmers, factory workers, shopkeepers and the bird-watching guide all seemed to depend on the same river in different ways.
activities.prompt: Ravi asks his grandfather why the town's first settlers chose this spot long ago. What is the best reason?
options: The river gave them a steady supply of water for daily life right where they lived
The river made the land cooler than any other place in the region
The river kept wild animals away from their homes at night
The river made it easy to build tall houses on its banks

why.The river made the land cooler than any: Coolness is not a reason given for settling near rivers.
why.The river kept wild animals away from th: Keeping animals away is not a benefit rivers provide.
why.The river made it easy to build tall hou: Rivers do not help in building tall houses.

activities.explanation: Correct: settlements have always come up near water because it serves everyday needs.

activities.context: Ravi's town stands on the banks of the Godavari. Water from the river reaches every house and school through pipes, and flows along canals to the fields where farmers raise crops. A factory by the river uses water too. Last month, a group of visitors came to walk along the banks, watch birds and learn about the plants there, taking care not to disturb anything. Ravi noticed that farmers, factory workers, shopkeepers and the bird-watching guide all seemed to depend on the same river in different ways.
activities.prompt: One summer, the factory draws much more water than usual. What is Ravi most likely to see further down the canals?
options: Farmers at the end of the canal getting less water for their fields
The river immediately becoming deeper and wider
More birds arriving because the fields get wetter
The pipes in the houses starting to carry more water

why.The river immediately becoming deeper an: Taking more water cannot make a river deeper or wider.
why.More birds arriving because the fields g: Less water for fields would not attract more birds.
why.The pipes in the houses starting to carr: House pipes would not get extra water when supply is stretched.

activities.explanation: Correct: river water is shared by many, so extra use by one user leaves less for others.

activities.context: Ravi's town stands on the banks of the Godavari. Water from the river reaches every house and school through pipes, and flows along canals to the fields where farmers raise crops. A factory by the river uses water too. Last month, a group of visitors came to walk along the banks, watch birds and learn about the plants there, taking care not to disturb anything. Ravi noticed that farmers, factory workers, shopkeepers and the bird-watching guide all seemed to depend on the same river in different ways.
activities.prompt: One visitor wants to get closer to the birds for better photographs. What should the guide advise her to do?
options: Watch quietly from a distance so the place stays peaceful and unharmed
Move right up to the birds so the photos come out clear
Play bird calls loudly to make the birds come nearer
Pick up a few plants as souvenirs of the visit

why.Move right up to the birds so the photos: Getting too close would disturb the birds and harm the place.
why.Play bird calls loudly to make the birds: Loud calls would disturb the birds, not help them.
why.Pick up a few plants as souvenirs of the: Taking plants away damages the natural place.

activities.explanation: Correct: enjoying and learning about nature without harming it is the right way to visit such places.

activities.prompt: Explain why, since ancient times, people have preferred to build their homes near rivers or water bodies.
activities.answer: People need water every day for drinking, cooking and washing, and rivers provide it easily. Living nearby also lets them water their crops and carry water to their homes through pipes. That is why settlements have always come up close to rivers and other water bodies.
points: Mentions daily needs: drinking, cooking, washing
Mentions water for growing crops
Links nearness of the river to easy supply of water
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meena's village lies near the Godavari river. A new dam has been built there, and a huge reservoir now spreads behind its giant wall. Some families from the low-lying fields had to shift to a hillside settlement. In the hot, dry months, Meena's family still gets water from the tap to drink and to grow their crops, and the nearby power line hums with electricity made from the stored water.
activities.prompt: Why did some families from the low-lying fields have to move to the hillside settlement?
options: Water rising behind the dam spread over the ground where their houses stood
The hillside settlement had better schools for their children
They wanted to live closer to the reservoir for fishing
The government gave them free houses on the hillside

why.The hillside settlement had better schoo: Schools are not mentioned anywhere in the facts, so this reason cannot be supported.
why.They wanted to live closer to the reserv: Fishing is not one of the uses of stored water given, and wanting to move is different from having to move.
why.The government gave them free houses on: Free houses are not part of the facts; the reason people shift is the flooding of their land.

activities.explanation: Correct: land that gets flooded when a dam is built can no longer be lived on, so people must shift elsewhere.

activities.context: Meena's village lies near the Godavari river. A new dam has been built there, and a huge reservoir now spreads behind its giant wall. Some families from the low-lying fields had to shift to a hillside settlement. In the hot, dry months, Meena's family still gets water from the tap to drink and to grow their crops, and the nearby power line hums with electricity made from the stored water.
activities.prompt: What would most likely happen in the dry months if the dam wall had never been built on the Godavari near Meena's village?
options: The river would flow faster than ever before
There would be more electricity in the power lines
Meena's family would find it hard to get water for drinking and crops
The low-lying families would have to shift to the hillside

why.The river would flow faster than ever be: A dam blocks and slows the flow; without it there is no reason for the river to flow faster.
why.There would be more electricity in the p: Electricity is made from stored water, so removing the dam would reduce it, not increase it.
why.The low-lying families would have to shi: People shift because dams flood their homes; with no dam there would be no flooding to force them out.

activities.explanation: Correct: without stored water kept back by the dam, the dry season would leave people short of water to drink and to grow crops.

activities.context: Meena's village lies near the Godavari river. A new dam has been built there, and a huge reservoir now spreads behind its giant wall. Some families from the low-lying fields had to shift to a hillside settlement. In the hot, dry months, Meena's family still gets water from the tap to drink and to grow their crops, and the nearby power line hums with electricity made from the stored water.
activities.prompt: Meena sees her little brother leave the tap running while he plays. What should she do, and why?
options: Leave it open, because the reservoir behind the dam is very large
Close the tap and remind him that reaching their home took a long journey and many sacrifices
Close the tap only during the dry months, and leave it open in the rainy season
Leave it open, because the dam makes electricity from the water anyway

why.Leave it open, because the reservoir beh: A large reservoir does not make wasting water right; the lesson is to use water wisely and never waste it.
why.Close the tap only during the dry months: Water must be used wisely at all times, not only when it is scarce.
why.Leave it open, because the dam makes ele: Making electricity is not a reason to waste water; the tap water should still be used carefully.

activities.explanation: Correct: water should never be wasted, and remembering its journey and the sacrifices behind it helps us value every drop.

activities.prompt: Explain why people have to leave their homes when a dam is built on a river.
activities.answer: A dam is like a giant wall that blocks a river's flow, so water collects behind it in a large reservoir. This reservoir floods land that was once home to animals and people. Since their homes and land go under water, many people have to leave and shift elsewhere.
points: A dam blocks the river's flow like a giant wall
Water collects in a large water body called a reservoir
The reservoir floods land that was once home to animals and people
So many people must leave their homes and shift elsewhere
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: The town of Sundarpur grew quickly. Many new houses and factories were built close to the riverbank. Every day, waste, plastic bags and dirty water flowed into the river. Soon the river began to smell bad and did not look clean. The fish, turtles and birds living there had nowhere else to go, and people still used the river water every day.
activities.prompt: If the number of factories and houses near the riverbank keeps increasing, what is most likely to happen to the river?
options: The river will become cleaner because more people will look after it
The pollution will increase because more waste and dirty water will flow into it
The fish and turtles will move to the factories and live there
The river water will turn sweet and safe to drink

why.The river will become cleaner because mo: Wrong: more people usually means more waste, not better care, unless they act specially
why.The fish and turtles will move to the fa: Wrong: animals cannot live in factories; they are losing their home, not finding a new one
why.The river water will turn sweet and safe: Wrong: pollution makes water dirty and unsafe, never sweet or safe to drink

activities.explanation: Correct: more houses and factories mean more waste, plastic and dirty water entering the river

activities.context: The town of Sundarpur grew quickly. Many new houses and factories were built close to the riverbank. Every day, waste, plastic bags and dirty water flowed into the river. Soon the river began to smell bad and did not look clean. The fish, turtles and birds living there had nowhere else to go, and people still used the river water every day.
activities.prompt: A family living near the river keeps getting stomach problems. What is the most likely reason, and what should they do?
options: The river water may carry harmful things even though it looks clean, so they should stop using it untreated
The river is too noisy, so they should move away from it
The fish are eating all the plants, so they should feed the fish more
The weather near the river is cold, so they should wear warm clothes

why.The river is too noisy, so they should m: Wrong: noise does not cause stomach problems; the case is about the water they use
why.The fish are eating all the plants, so t: Wrong: fish eating plants does not make people sick; this misses the dirty water problem
why.The weather near the river is cold, so t: Wrong: cold weather does not cause stomach problems from using river water

activities.explanation: Correct: even clean-looking water may carry harmful things, so using it can make people sick

activities.prompt: How does the use of fertilisers on nearby farms harm the life inside the river?
activities.answer: Fertilisers used to grow crops get washed into the river water. Once inside, they make plants and other organisms grow very fast. This fast growth slowly chokes all life inside the river, so fish, turtles and other living things struggle to survive and may slowly begin to disappear.
points: Fertilisers from crops get washed into the water
They make plants and other organisms grow very fast
This fast growth slowly chokes all life inside the river
Living things like fish and turtles may slowly disappear
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Ravi lives in a village beside a river. Most of the time the river flows gently and the fields stay green. This year, days of very heavy rain fell, and the trees on the nearby hills had been cut down. The river grew faster, deeper and bigger, spilled over its banks, and covered houses, fields and roads. Ravi's family and the village cattle had to go away for a while.
activities.prompt: Why did rainwater reach Ravi's village so quickly and cause such a big flood?
options: The trees on the hills had been cut down, so water rushed off the land instead of soaking in
The river had become weak and could not hold the rainwater gently
The rain only fell during the night, so nobody could stop it
The fields soaked up too much water and pushed it into the river

why.The river had become weak and could not: Wrong: the river was not weak; it grew bigger and more powerful with the heavy rain
why.The rain only fell during the night, so: Wrong: the time of day or night the rain fell does not change how the land handles the water
why.The fields soaked up too much water and: Wrong: soaking water into the soil is helpful; it is the lack of trees, not the fields, that made water run off

activities.explanation: Correct: with no trees, rainwater is not slowed down or soaked into the soil, so it runs off fast and floods

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Journey of a River

activities.prompt: Where does the journey of the Godavari begin?
options: At the Bay of Bengal
At the Coringa Mangrove Forests
At Trimbakeshwar in Maharashtra
On Majuli island in Assam
activities.explanation: The Godavari starts high in the Western Ghats at Trimbakeshwar. The sea comes much later, at the end of its long journey.

activities.prompt: The Godavari flows only during the rainy season.
activities.explanation: The Godavari flows all year, so it is a perennial river. Seasonal rivers are the ones that need rain to flow.

activities.prompt: Small streams that join a big river are called ______.
activities.hint: These little helpers make the river wider and stronger.
activities.explanation: Tributaries bring rainwater and more water to the river. That is how a small stream grows into a mighty river.

activities.prompt: Match each river word with its meaning.
pairs: a small stream that joins a river
many small streams where a river meets the sea
a river that flows all year
the large water body behind a dam
activities.explanation: These four words tell the story of a river: streams join it, it flows all year, and dams store its water before it spreads into a delta.

activities.prompt: Why is the Godavari called Dakshina Ganga?
options: Because it is the longest river in India
Because it flows through southern India and is sacred
Because it flows only during Godavari Pushkaram
Because it begins near the Bay of Bengal
activities.explanation: Dakshina means south. The Godavari flows through southern India and is sacred, so people call it the Ganga of the South.

activities.prompt: Dams store water but never cause any problems for people or animals.
activities.explanation: Dams are helpful, but they flood land that was once home to animals and people. Many families have to shift elsewhere.

activities.prompt: More than ______ dams store the water of the Godavari.
activities.hint: It is a number bigger than eight hundred.
activities.explanation: That is a lot of dams! They store water so people can use it even during dry seasons.

activities.prompt: What happens when fertilisers from fields get washed into a river?
options: They make plants and other organisms grow very fast
They make the river cleaner and fresher
They have no effect on life in the river
They make the river flow backwards
activities.explanation: The fast growth of plants and organisms slowly chokes all life inside the river. Even clean-looking water can hide harmful things.

activities.prompt: Put the events of a flood in the correct order.
items: Too much rain falls
The river becomes faster, deeper and bigger
It overflows its banks
Houses, fields and roads are flooded
People and animals leave their homes to stay safe
activities.explanation: Heavy rain makes the river swell until it spills over its banks. That is why people and animals must move to safety.

boss.sceneCaption: The kund at Triyambakeshwar, considered to be origin of river Godavari.

chapters.title: Health and Well-being
chapters.summary: In this chapter: food spoilage and microbes; why food spoils and how to preserve it; more preservation and good microbes; my food, my pride and seasonal fruits.

lessons.title: Food Spoilage and Microbes

activities.prompt: Why did Disha's forgotten uttapam grow colourful patches and smell so bad?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Mystery of the Smelly Lunch Box
activities.body: Disha forgot her lunch box in school. Inside was uttapam from three days ago. When she opened it, a foul smell came out. The uttapam had coloured patches too. Aditya said the patches were mould. Mould and other microbes are tiny living things that grew on the food and changed it.
keyPoints: Food left for days can get a foul smell and coloured patches.
The coloured patches were mould.
Microbes are tiny living things that grow on food and change it.
activities.explanation: Tiny living things called microbes changed Disha's uttapam over three days.

activities.prompt: Disha forgot her lunch box in school on Friday. When she opened it, a bad smell came out. Why did the uttapam change?
steps: Microbes are everywhere, so some were already on the uttapam.
Microbes are tiny living things, so they grew on the food.
Growing microbes changed the food, so the taste and smell changed.
So the foul smell came from microbes that changed the uttapam.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Not All Microbes Are Bad
activities.body: Here is a happy surprise! Some microbes help us make curd. Some microbes help digest our food inside our body. Microbes live in soil, water, air, plants, animals and inside us. They are everywhere! But when microbes grow on food for days, they change its taste and smell.
keyPoints: Some microbes help us make curd.
Some microbes help us digest our food.
Microbes live in soil, water, air, plants, animals and inside us.
activities.explanation: Microbes can be our helpers as well as food spoilers.

activities.prompt: What food did Disha find left in her forgotten lunch box?
options: Uttapam
Curd
Rice
Bread
activities.explanation: Well done! Disha had left uttapam in her lunch box three days ago.

activities.prompt: Microbes are so tiny that we need a ______ to see them.
activities.hint: It is a tool that makes very tiny things look big.
activities.explanation: Great! A microscope makes tiny things look big enough for our eyes to see.

activities.prompt: Why did Disha's uttapam give out a foul smell?
options: Microbes changed the smell of the food
The lunch box was new
The uttapam was too fresh
The box was kept in the sun
activities.explanation: Microbes grew on the uttapam and changed its taste and smell.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what it means in the lesson.
pairs: A colony of thousands of microbes
We need it to see microbes
A sign that microbes changed the food
activities.explanation: Each match shows how microbes change food or help us.

activities.prompt: Which of these shows microbes helping us?
options: Helping to make curd
Making a foul smell
Growing coloured patches
Changing the taste of uttapam
activities.explanation: Some friendly microbes help us make curd and digest our food.

activities.prompt: Put the story of Disha's lunch box in the right order.
items: Disha forgot her lunch box in school
The uttapam sat in the box for three days
Disha opened the box and a foul smell came out
She saw coloured patches of mould on the uttapam
activities.explanation: First the box was forgotten, then time passed, then came the smell, then the mould.

activities.prompt: Meera says microbes are not on her clean table. Her friend says they are. Who is right, and why?
options: Meera, because clean things have no microbes on them
The friend, because microbes are everywhere around us
Meera, because microbes only live inside lunch boxes
The friend, because microbes only live in dirty water

why.Meera, because clean things have no micr: Thinks clean means no microbes at all.
why.Meera, because microbes only live inside: Thinks microbes only grow on spoiled food.
why.The friend, because microbes only live i: Thinks microbes live only in one dirty place.

activities.explanation: Right: microbes are everywhere, even on clean tables.

activities.prompt: Some microbes help us make curd. Other microbes spoiled Disha's uttapam. What does this show about microbes?
options: All microbes change food in a bad way
Only microbes in milk can ever change food
Microbes can change food in helpful or harmful ways
Microbes only change food when it is inside a box

why.All microbes change food in a bad way: Thinks every microbe is harmful to food.
why.Only microbes in milk can ever change fo: Thinks only one special microbe can change food.
why.Microbes only change food when it is ins: Thinks the lunch box caused the change, not microbes.

activities.explanation: Right: some microbes help us, some spoil food.

activities.prompt: Anu left chapati in her box. Two days later it smells bad. She looks with her eyes only. What will she see?
options: She will see the microbes moving on the chapati
She will see nothing, but she can smell the change
She will see nothing and smell nothing at all
She will see curd forming on the chapati

why.She will see the microbes moving on the: Thinks eyes alone can see single microbes.
why.She will see nothing and smell nothing a: Forgets that microbes change the smell of food.
why.She will see curd forming on the chapati: Mixes up curd making with food spoiling.

activities.explanation: Right: microbes are too tiny to see, but the smell change is clear.

activities.prompt: A boy says: 'I touched the mould patch, so I saw a microbe.' What is wrong with his claim?
options: Nothing is wrong, mould is one single microbe
The patch is a colony, so he saw many microbes together
He is wrong because microbes live only inside our body
He is wrong because microbes never grow on food

why.Nothing is wrong, mould is one single mi: Thinks the whole patch is one living thing.
why.He is wrong because microbes live only i: Thinks microbes cannot live on food or objects.
why.He is wrong because microbes never grow: Thinks microbes cannot grow on food at all.

activities.explanation: Right: the patch is thousands of microbes living as a colony.

lessons.sceneAlt: A pizza covered with patches of mould, showing how food spoils when microbes grow on it.
lessons.sceneCaption: Mould growing on food makes it spoil and smell bad, just like Disha's uttapam.

sceneCredit.text: Moldy pizza 1 2024-05-14 by Fastily, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
sceneCredit.creator: Fastily

lessons.title: Why Food Spoils and How to Preserve It

activities.prompt: Why did the bread on the balcony get patches while the pickle stayed tasty?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Why does food go bad?
activities.body: Disha saw a slice of bread on the balcony grow coloured patches. Tiny living things called microbes had grown on it. Microbes need three things: moisture, air and the right temperature. But her family's pickle, made two months ago, was still tasty because oil covered it. If we take away even one thing microbes need, we can stop them. That is how we keep food safe.
keyPoints: Microbes are tiny living things that spoil food.
Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow.
Remove any one of these three, and microbes stop growing.
Oil on pickles keeps out air, so the pickle stays good.
activities.explanation: Food spoils when microbes grow on it, and we can stop them by taking away what they need.

activities.prompt: Disha saw coloured patches on a slice of bread left on the balcony. Why did the patches come?
steps: The bread has moisture, and microbes need moisture to grow.
The balcony has open air, and microbes need air too.
The balcony is warm, so microbes had the right temperature.
Microbes had all three things they need, so they grew and made the patches.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Disha's family made pickles two months ago. Why are they still delicious?
options: They were kept in a matka.
They were covered with oil.
They were dried in the Sun.
activities.explanation: Well done! Oil keeps out air, so microbes cannot grow on the pickle.

activities.prompt: Chillies are dried in the Sun to remove ______ from them.
activities.hint: Think of the water in fresh chillies.
activities.explanation: Great thinking! Without moisture, microbes cannot grow on the chillies.

activities.prompt: Mum puts milk in the fridge so it does not spoil. How does the fridge help?
options: It makes the temperature too cold for microbes.
It adds salt to the milk.
It removes all the moisture from milk.
activities.explanation: Correct! The fridge makes it too cold for microbes to grow, so the milk lasts longer.

activities.prompt: Match each method with what it does.
pairs: Makes it too cold for microbes
activities.explanation: Each method stops microbes in its own way. You matched them all!

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to show how oil keeps a pickle safe.
items: Microbes need air to grow
The pickle is covered with oil
The oil keeps out the air
The microbes cannot grow
The pickle stays delicious
activities.explanation: Perfect order! Blocking the air with oil stops the microbes, so the pickle stays good.

activities.prompt: Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature. What happens if we remove just ONE of these?
options: The microbes grow even faster.
We can stop the microbes.
The microbes only need more food.
activities.explanation: Well done! Even one missing need is enough to stop microbes, and that is how preserving works.

activities.prompt: Ravi puts one bread slice on the table. He puts another slice in the fridge. The room is warm. The fridge is very cold. Which slice gets patches first?
options: The slice on the table
The slice in the fridge
Both get patches at the same time
Neither slice will ever get patches

why.The slice in the fridge: The child thinks cold helps microbes, but cold slows them down.
why.Both get patches at the same time: The child thinks both places are the same for microbes, but they are not.
why.Neither slice will ever get patches: The child thinks bread never spoils, but microbes can grow anywhere food is.

activities.explanation: Right. The table is warm, so microbes grow fast there.

activities.prompt: Meera wants to show that moisture helps microbes grow. She has two slices of the same bread. Which test is fair?
options: One dry and one wet slice, both in the same warm place
One dry slice in the fridge and one wet slice in the Sun
One dry slice in a dark box and one wet slice in the Sun
One small dry slice and one big wet slice on the same table

why.One dry slice in the fridge and one wet: Two things change here, temperature and moisture, so it is not fair.
why.One dry slice in a dark box and one wet: Two things change here, light and moisture, so it is not fair.
why.One small dry slice and one big wet slic: The size changed too, so the test is not fair.

activities.explanation: Right. Only moisture is different, so the test is fair.

activities.prompt: Amit dried mango slices in the Sun. He says, 'The Sun took away the air, so microbes cannot grow.' What is wrong with his claim?
options: Drying in the Sun takes away moisture, not air
The Sun takes away moisture and adds more air
Microbes do not need air to grow
Mango slices have no water inside them

why.The Sun takes away moisture and adds mor: The child mixed up what the Sun removes and what it does.
why.Microbes do not need air to grow: The child forgot that microbes need air to grow.
why.Mango slices have no water inside them: The child forgot that mango has water inside it.

activities.explanation: Right. The Sun removes the water, and that is what stops microbes.

activities.prompt: Mother leaves a wet chapati and a dry papad on the same plate overnight. The kitchen is warm. Which one spoils first?
options: The wet chapati, because it has moisture
The dry papad, because dry food spoils faster
Both spoil at the same time
Neither spoils, because the plate is clean

why.The dry papad, because dry food spoils f: The child thinks dry food spoils faster, but dryness stops microbes.
why.Both spoil at the same time: The child thinks both are the same, but one is wet and one is dry.
why.Neither spoils, because the plate is cle: The child thinks a clean plate stops microbes, but microbes come from the air.

activities.explanation: Right. The chapati has moisture, so microbes grow on it first.

activities.prompt: Water in a clay matka stays cool. A cook keeps cooked rice in a cool corner. She does not keep it near the hot stove. Why does the cool corner help?
options: Cool places slow down microbes
Cool places give the food more air
Hot stoves put moisture into the food
Cool places add salt to the food

why.Cool places give the food more air: The child thinks cool means more air, but coolness changes temperature.
why.Hot stoves put moisture into the food: The child thinks heat adds water, but heat helps microbes grow.
why.Cool places add salt to the food: The child thinks coolness changes taste, but it changes microbe growth.

activities.explanation: Right. Microbes grow slowly when the temperature is cold.

lessons.sceneCaption: Red peppers being laid out to dry in the sun in the summer in Seoul, South Korea.

lessons.title: More Preservation and Good Microbes

activities.prompt: How do wasps keep their food fresh without a fridge?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Keeping Food Safe and Tummy Friends
activities.body: Food can be kept safe in many ways. In factories, food is sealed in air tight cans so microbes cannot reach it. Nature knew this trick first! Hunting wasps preserve food for their babies. Some microbes are our friends. Microbes in the air help idli batter rise. Microbes in curd join the good microbes in your stomach and help digestion.
keyPoints: Air tight cans keep microbes away from food.
Hunting wasps preserved food long before humans did.
Microbes in the air make idli batter rise.
Microbes in curd help your stomach digest food.
activities.explanation: Not all microbes are bad. Some keep food safe, and some keep your tummy happy!

activities.prompt: Amma fills a jar with mango pickle. Then she presses the lid down very, very tightly. Riya asks, 'Why close it so tightly?' Can you reason it out?
steps: Tiny microbes float around in the air, so an open jar lets them land on the pickle.
Microbes on food can spoil it, so Amma wants to keep them away from the pickle.
A tight lid blocks the air, so the microbes cannot get inside the jar.
So the tight lid keeps microbes away, and the pickle stays good for many days.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why is food sealed in air tight cans in factories?
options: To keep microbes away from the food
To make the food taste sweeter
To give the food a shiny look
activities.explanation: Air tight cans and packaging keep microbes away, so the food stays safe to eat.

activities.prompt: Hunting wasps preserve food for their ______.
activities.hint: It means the young babies of the wasp.
activities.explanation: Hunting wasps are careful parents. They preserve food so their larvae can eat it.

activities.prompt: What makes idli batter rise?
options: Microbes in the air
Ice from the fridge
Sugar mixed in water
activities.explanation: Microbes floating in the air get into the batter and help it rise. Good microbes at work!

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what it does.
activities.explanation: Great matching! You can see how preservation and good microbes both help us every day.

activities.prompt: Why does curd help your stomach when it is upset?
options: Microbes in curd join good microbes and help digestion
Curd washes the stomach with cold water
Curd makes the stomach stop working for a while
activities.explanation: Small microbes in curd join the good microbes already in your stomach. Together they help digestion.

activities.prompt: Aditya Anna ate food at a fair and got an upset stomach. Put the steps of getting better in order.
items: Have an upset stomach after eating fair food
Try curd or buttermilk to help digestion
If the problem is severe, consult a doctor
Take the medicines the doctor gives
activities.explanation: First try the gentle home help like curd. If the problem is severe, a doctor and medicines are needed.

activities.prompt: Ravi says, 'Only humans know how to preserve food.' His sister shows him a solitary hunting wasp. The wasp preserves food for its larvae. What is the flaw in Ravi's claim?
options: Wasps also preserve food, so humans are not the only ones
Ravi is right because wasps only hunt and never store food
Ravi is right because larvae cannot eat preserved food
The claim is wrong only because wasps are very small insects

why.Ravi is right because wasps only hunt an: This child forgot that hunting wasps preserve food for their larvae.
why.Ravi is right because larvae cannot eat: This child made up a new rule; the fact says wasps do preserve food.
why.The claim is wrong only because wasps ar: This child thinks size matters, but small wasps still preserve food.

activities.explanation: Right. Insects like hunting wasps preserved food long before humans did.

activities.prompt: Arun eats chips and fizzy drinks every day. He eats very fast too. Sameer eats slow, home-cooked meals. Who is more likely to get indigestion, and why?
options: Sameer, because home-cooked food always takes longer to digest
Arun, because bad eating habits can lead to indigestion
Both equally, because every child gets indigestion every day
Neither, because indigestion comes only from fair food

why.Sameer, because home-cooked food always: This child blames home food, but slow healthy eating helps digestion.
why.Both equally, because every child gets i: This child thinks indigestion is automatic, but habits make a difference.
why.Neither, because indigestion comes only: This child thinks only fair food causes it, but habits matter too.

activities.explanation: Right. Bad eating habits like Arun's can lead to indigestion.

activities.prompt: Ria's stomach pain is very bad. Curd and buttermilk are not helping her. What should her family do now?
options: Give her more and more curd until the pain stops
Consult a doctor, because the problem may need medicines
Tell her to run and play so the pain runs away too
Wait for many days without doing anything new at all

why.Give her more and more curd until the pa: This child thinks more curd always works, but severe problems need more.
why.Tell her to run and play so the pain run: This child thinks playing cures pain, but a bad stomach needs a doctor.
why.Wait for many days without doing anythin: This child thinks waiting helps, but severe problems should not be ignored.

activities.explanation: Right. For a severe problem, consult a doctor and take medicines.

lessons.sceneCaption: A potter wasp is hunting a caterpillar of a leaf roller moth, catching prey for its larvae.

lessons.title: My Food, My Pride and Seasonal Fruits

activities.prompt: Why does waiting for a fruit make it taste even better?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Food from Our Families and Fields
activities.body: Families pass food ways from grandparents to parents to children. Thatha goes to the vegetable market every day for fresh fruits and vegetables. Appa once brought home lychees. Lychee is a seasonal fruit, so the family had to wait for it. Fruits taste best in their season, and waiting makes the joy bigger.
keyPoints: Food practices pass from one generation to the next.
Thatha buys fresh fruits and vegetables at the market daily.
Lychee is seasonal, so we wait for it.
Fruits taste best in their season.
activities.explanation: Fresh, seasonal food brings families together with joy.

activities.prompt: Meera sees lychees in the market in December. Her friend says, 'Buy them now, they will be sweet!' Should Meera buy them?
steps: Lychee is a seasonal fruit, so it does not grow in every month of the year.
Fruits taste best when they are eaten in their season, so out-of-season lychees will not taste as good.
Waiting for the right season is hard, but waiting increases the joy when the fruit finally comes.
So Meera should wait for lychee season, because the fruit will taste best and feel more special then.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why are local mangoes fresh?
options: They did not have to travel far.
They are kept in a fridge.
They are the biggest fruits.
activities.explanation: Local mangoes stay fresh because they did not have to travel far.

activities.prompt: Lychee is a ______ fruit, so we need to wait for it.
activities.hint: It comes only at a certain time of year.
activities.explanation: Yes! A seasonal fruit comes only at its own time of year.

activities.prompt: Match each thing to what you learned about it.
activities.explanation: Great matching! Each one has its own special place in the lesson.

activities.prompt: When do fruits taste best?
options: When eaten in their season
When eaten before their season
When kept for many months
activities.explanation: Fruits taste best in their season, and waiting makes the joy grow.

activities.prompt: Put the story events in the right order.
items: Thatha buys fresh fruits and vegetables at the market
Appa buys lychees on his way home
The family waits, as lychee is seasonal
Everyone peels and shares the fruits
Everyone feels joy eating the delicious fruits
activities.explanation: Lovely! You remembered the story from market to happy sharing.

activities.prompt: What happens when we wait for a seasonal fruit?
options: The joy of eating it grows
The fruit loses its taste
The fruit never ripens
activities.explanation: Waiting increases the joy, and the fruit tastes best in its season.

activities.prompt: Appa buys mangoes from a farm near his town. Ravi buys mangoes from a farm very far away. Both mangoes reach the market on the same day. Whose mangoes are more likely to be fresh, and why?
options: Ravi's, because faraway farms grow bigger mangoes
Appa's, because near mangoes did not travel far
Ravi's, because travel makes mangoes sweeter
Both are the same, because all mangoes are alike

why.Ravi's, because faraway farms grow bigge: Wrong: size is not the reason; the fact talks about travel, not size.
why.Ravi's, because travel makes mangoes swe: Wrong: travel does not make fruit sweeter; long travel makes fruit less fresh.
why.Both are the same, because all mangoes a: Wrong: how far fruit travels changes how fresh it is.

activities.explanation: Right: local mangoes are fresh because they did not have to travel far.

activities.prompt: Ravi wants to eat his favourite seasonal fruit today, but it is not the season for it. His sister says, 'Just wait a few months!' What will most likely happen if Ravi waits?
options: He will enjoy the fruit more when the season comes
He will enjoy the fruit less when the season comes
The fruit will taste the same in any month
The fruit will never come to the market again

why.He will enjoy the fruit less when the se: Wrong: waiting makes the joy bigger, not smaller.
why.The fruit will taste the same in any mon: Wrong: fruits taste best in their season, not the same all year.
why.The fruit will never come to the market: Wrong: seasonal fruits come back every year in their season.

activities.explanation: Right: waiting for a seasonal fruit increases the joy of eating it.

activities.prompt: In a village in the Northeast, a family builds a new house and cooks dinner. They use one plant for both jobs. Which claim about this plant is fair to make?
options: Bamboo is useful for building and for cooking
Bamboo is useful only for making houses
Bamboo is useful only for cooking curries
Bamboo is not useful for houses or food

why.Bamboo is useful only for making houses: Wrong: bamboo is also used in cooking, not only for houses.
why.Bamboo is useful only for cooking currie: Wrong: bamboo is also used for houses, not only for curries.
why.Bamboo is not useful for houses or food: Wrong: bamboo is useful for both jobs.

activities.explanation: Right: in the Northeast, bamboo is used in making houses and in cooking.

activities.prompt: Anu's uncle says, 'I ate lychees in a month when they were not in season. So seasonal fruits taste the same in every month.' What is the flaw in his claim?
options: He forgot that fruits taste best in their season
He forgot that lychees grow in every month
He forgot that only children can taste well
He forgot that markets stay open all year

why.He forgot that lychees grow in every mon: Wrong: lychee is seasonal, so it does not grow in every month.
why.He forgot that only children can taste w: Wrong: tasting well is not about being a child.
why.He forgot that markets stay open all yea: Wrong: markets being open does not decide how fruit tastes.

activities.explanation: Right: fruits taste best in their season, so out-of-season fruit is not the best test.
