lessons.title: Chewing, Teeth, Oral Hygiene and Choking

activities.prompt: Why do we have different kinds of teeth in our mouth?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: What Happens When You Eat?
activities.body: When you eat, chew each piece properly until it turns soft and mushy. Your mouth has different teeth for different jobs: incisors cut, canines tear, premolars crush and molars grind. Chewing well also releases saliva, which helps digest your food. After eating, rinse your mouth and brush your teeth regularly to keep them healthy. And always eat slowly, so you do not choke.
keyPoints: Chew each item properly until it breaks into small, soft pieces.
Incisors cut, canines tear, premolars crush and molars grind.
Chewing releases saliva, which helps digest food.
Rinse after eating, brush regularly, and eat slowly to avoid choking.
activities.explanation: Good chewing and clean teeth keep your tummy and your smile happy.

activities.prompt: Ravi eats his chapati in two big bites and swallows fast. His friend Meera chews each bite many times. Why does Meera's tummy feel better after lunch?
steps: Meera chews till the food becomes small and mushy, so her body can handle it easily.
Her chewing also makes saliva come out, and saliva helps digest the food.
Ravi swallows big pieces fast, so his body has to work harder on them.
So chewing slowly and properly helps the food digest well and keeps the tummy comfortable.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which teeth do you use to CUT food, like biting into an apple?
options: Molars
Incisors
Premolars
activities.explanation: Incisors are the front teeth made for cutting food.

activities.prompt: Chewing properly releases ______, which helps digest your food.
activities.hint: It is a juice made in your mouth when you chew.
activities.explanation: Saliva mixes with your food as you chew and helps digestion begin.

activities.prompt: Match each type of tooth to its job.
activities.explanation: Each tooth has its own special job in breaking down food.

activities.prompt: Why should you chew each piece of food until it is soft and mushy?
options: It makes food taste sweeter
It helps your mouth make saliva to digest food
It helps you finish eating faster
activities.explanation: Chewing well releases saliva, and saliva helps digest the food.

activities.prompt: Ravi's tooth has been aching for two days. What may he need to do?
options: See a dentist for help or a check-up
Chew only on the other side of his mouth
Rinse his mouth once and ignore the ache
activities.explanation: When teeth ache, a dentist is the right person to visit. A cavity is a hole in a tooth, and a dentist can check for one.

activities.prompt: Put these steps of eating a meal in the correct order.
items: Take a bite of food
Chew it properly till it is soft and mushy
Swallow the food
Rinse your mouth after eating
activities.explanation: Chew well before swallowing, and always rinse your mouth when you finish eating.

activities.prompt: An apple slice is hard. Your front teeth bite a piece off. Your back teeth then crush it. Why do you need both kinds of teeth for one apple?
options: Because front teeth cut the piece and back teeth grind it small.
Because front teeth are stronger and back teeth are weaker.
Because the apple tastes better when both teeth are used.
Because using both kinds of teeth makes chewing faster only.

why.Because front teeth are stronger and bac: Wrong: it is not about strength; each tooth has its own special job.
why.Because the apple tastes better when bot: Wrong: taste does not change; the teeth do different jobs on the food.
why.Because using both kinds of teeth makes: Wrong: speed is not the reason; the reason is the different jobs of teeth.

activities.explanation: Right: incisors cut and molars grind, so the apple needs both jobs done.

activities.prompt: A boy says, 'I can skip rinsing my mouth after eating sweets. Nothing happens if I do it just once.' What is wrong with his claim?
options: Rinsing washes food away, so skipping it can harm the teeth.
Rinsing only makes the mouth smell nice, nothing more.
Rinsing is needed only after drinking milk, not after sweets.
Rinsing works only when a dentist tells you to do it.

why.Rinsing only makes the mouth smell nice,: Wrong: rinsing is not just for smell; it is part of keeping teeth healthy.
why.Rinsing is needed only after drinking mi: Wrong: rinsing matters after eating, not only after one special drink.
why.Rinsing works only when a dentist tells: Wrong: you do not need permission; rinsing after eating is a good habit always.

activities.explanation: Right: oral hygiene matters, and rinsing after eating keeps the mouth clean.

activities.prompt: Two children eat the same food. One chews each bite till it is mush. One swallows big pieces fast. Who is more likely to choke, and why?
options: The fast eater, because big pieces can get stuck and block the throat.
The slow chewer, because chewing makes food too soft to swallow.
Both equally, because choking depends only on the type of food.
Neither, because choking happens only when drinking water quickly.

why.The slow chewer, because chewing makes f: Wrong: soft mushy food is easier to swallow, not harder.
why.Both equally, because choking depends on: Wrong: how you eat changes the risk, not just the food itself.
why.Neither, because choking happens only wh: Wrong: choking is about food going the wrong way, not about water.

activities.explanation: Right: eating slowly and chewing well helps avoid choking on big pieces.

activities.prompt: A girl feels a sharp pain in one tooth every time she eats. Her friend says, 'Wait, it will fix itself.' What should the girl really do, and why?
options: See a dentist, because an aching tooth needs a check-up.
Chew only on the other side, so the bad tooth gets rest.
Brush that tooth many times a day until the pain stops.
Rinse the mouth more often, since rinsing cures tooth pain.

why.Chew only on the other side, so the bad: Wrong: resting the tooth does not fix the problem inside it.
why.Brush that tooth many times a day until: Wrong: brushing more cannot fix a tooth that already hurts.
why.Rinse the mouth more often, since rinsin: Wrong: rinsing keeps the mouth clean but does not cure a painful tooth.

activities.explanation: Right: an aching tooth is a sign that a dentist may need to see it.

activities.prompt: A boy says, 'All my teeth do the same job, so it does not matter which tooth I use.' Is he right? Why or why not?
options: No, because different teeth are made for different jobs on food.
Yes, because every tooth can cut, tear, crush and grind equally.
No, because teeth only work when food is soft and mushy.
Yes, because the tongue does the chewing, not the teeth.

why.Yes, because every tooth can cut, tear,: Wrong: no single tooth does every job; each type has its own use.
why.No, because teeth only work when food is: Wrong: teeth work on food before it turns mushy; chewing makes it mushy.
why.Yes, because the tongue does the chewing: Wrong: the tongue helps move food, but the teeth do the chewing.

activities.explanation: Right: teeth have different uses, like cutting, tearing, crushing and grinding.

activities.prompt: A dentist finds a small hole in a child's tooth. The child asks how it happened. Which answer shows the child really understood?
options: The hole is a cavity, so the teeth were not kept clean enough.
The hole is a cavity, so the child was born with it.
The hole is a cavity, so the child chewed food too slowly.
The hole is a cavity, so the child used too many teeth to chew.

why.The hole is a cavity, so the child was b: Wrong: cavities are not something you are born with; care of teeth matters.
why.The hole is a cavity, so the child chewe: Wrong: chewing slowly is good for digestion; it does not make holes.
why.The hole is a cavity, so the child used: Wrong: using teeth for chewing is normal and does not make holes.

activities.explanation: Right: a cavity is a hole in the tooth, and good oral hygiene helps prevent it.

lessons.title: Final Discovery and Good Microbes

activities.prompt: Can some tiny creatures be our kitchen friends and helpers?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Mystery is Solved!
activities.body: Detective Disha has found the answer at last. The food mystery is solved! Some microbes spoil our food, but some microbes help us. Good microbes help us make food items like fermented rice. They also help us digest the food we eat. So we should eat right, preserve and store food right, chew well, and thank the good microbes.
keyPoints: Some microbes spoil food, but some microbes help us.
Good microbes help us make food and digest it.
Eat right, store food right, chew well, and thank the good microbes.
activities.explanation: Microbes can be friends or foes, and now you know how to tell them apart.

activities.prompt: Anu finds old rice in the kitchen. It smells sour. Grandmother says, 'Do not throw it. I will make pakhala.' Anu is confused. How can sour rice be bad and good?
steps: Some microbes land on food and spoil it, so sour food can be bad.
But some microbes help us make food items like pakhala, so sour can be good too.
The difference is which microbes are at work, not the sour smell itself.
So Anu learns that some microbes spoil food while some help us.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Which of these is a way GOOD microbes help us?
options: They spoil our food
They help us make food items
They hide in the kitchen
They make rice dry
activities.explanation: Good microbes help us make food items. Spoiling food is what the unhelpful microbes do.

activities.prompt: Fermented rice is called ______ in many parts of India.
activities.hint: It starts with the letter p.
activities.explanation: Fermented rice has names like pakhala and kanji in different parts of India.

activities.prompt: Match each idea with what we should do about it.
activities.explanation: Storing food right stops spoilage, and chewing well helps the good microbes digest your food.

activities.prompt: Put the last steps of Detective Disha's food story in order.
items: The food mystery was finally solved
We should eat right, preserve and store right
We should chew well and thank the good microbes
Detective Disha closed her notebook with a smile
activities.explanation: First the mystery was solved, then came the good food habits, and at last Disha closed her notebook with a smile.

activities.prompt: You have eaten your lunch. What do the good microbes do next to help you?
options: They help you digest the food
They spoil the food in your plate
They turn the food into pakhala
They close your notebook
activities.explanation: Good microbes help us digest our food, so chew well and thank them!

activities.prompt: Ravi leaves cooked rice outside for two days. It smells bad. Amma keeps another bowl inside the fridge. What will happen to the rice in the fridge?
options: It will stay good for a longer time.
It will also spoil in the same way.
It will turn into pakhala overnight.
It will become sweet and tasty.

Wrong. Thinks all food spoils no matter where it is kept.
Wrong. Thinks any rice left alone becomes pakhala.
Wrong. Thinks the fridge changes the taste of food.

activities.explanation: Right. Storing food right stops the spoil microbes from acting.

activities.prompt: Meera says all microbes are bad because they spoil food. But her idli and her pakhala are both made with microbes. What is the flaw in Meera's claim?
options: Idli and pakhala are not real food.
Some microbes help us make food items.
Microbes only live inside rice grains.
Spoiled food can sometimes taste nice.

Wrong. Thinks the foods do not count as food.
Wrong. Thinks microbes live only in one place.
Wrong. Thinks taste decides if microbes are good or bad.

activities.explanation: Right. Some microbes spoil food but some help us make food.

activities.prompt: Sanjay eats very fast. He swallows big pieces without chewing well. Good microbes in his body help digest food. What problem will Sanjay have?
options: His food will be harder to digest.
His food will turn into pakhala.
His good microbes will run away.
His body will become very cool.

Wrong. Mixes up digestion with fermenting rice.
Wrong. Thinks microbes leave the body when we eat fast.
Wrong. Mixes up cooling from pakhala with digestion.

activities.explanation: Right. Big pieces are hard, so chewing well helps digestion.

lessons.sceneAlt: A pizza covered with patches of mould, showing how food spoils when microbes grow on it.
lessons.sceneCaption: Mould growing on food makes it spoil and smell bad, just like Disha's uttapam.

activities.context: Ravi left his lunch box in his school bag over the weekend. Inside, there was uttapam from three days ago. When he opened the box at home, a foul smell came out, and the uttapam had coloured patches on it. His friend Meera, who had seen Disha's forgotten lunch box in school last Friday, said the patches looked just like the mould on Disha's uttapam.
activities.prompt: Why did Ravi's uttapam develop a foul smell after the weekend?
options: Because the lunch box was kept inside a bag instead of on a shelf
Because tiny living things grew on it and changed it while it was left for days
Because uttapam always smells bad when it becomes cold
Because the school bag was dark inside

why.Because the lunch box was kept inside a: Wrong: the box being in a bag is not the cause; food left anywhere for days can spoil.
why.Because uttapam always smells bad when i: Wrong: cold uttapam does not smell foul; the smell came from the change after days.
why.Because the school bag was dark inside: Wrong: darkness inside the bag is not the reason for the smell.

activities.explanation: Correct: microbes grew on the food over the days and changed its smell.

activities.context: Ravi left his lunch box in his school bag over the weekend. Inside, there was uttapam from three days ago. When he opened the box at home, a foul smell came out, and the uttapam had coloured patches on it. His friend Meera, who had seen Disha's forgotten lunch box in school last Friday, said the patches looked just like the mould on Disha's uttapam.
activities.prompt: If Ravi looks at the coloured patches on his uttapam without any instrument, what will he most likely find?
options: He will see each microbe clearly because the patches are made of microbes
He will not be able to see the microbes, only the patches they have formed
He will see nothing at all, because microbes cannot form patches
He will see the microbes moving away from the patches

why.He will see each microbe clearly because: Wrong: single microbes are too tiny to see without a microscope.
why.He will see nothing at all, because micr: Wrong: patches can be seen, as in Disha's and Ravi's uttapam.
why.He will see the microbes moving away fro: Wrong: microbes cannot be seen moving, since they are too tiny to see.

activities.explanation: Correct: the patches are visible, but the microbes making them up are too tiny to see without a microscope.

activities.prompt: Explain why the uttapam in Disha's lunch box developed coloured patches and a foul smell after she forgot it in school.
activities.answer: Microbes are tiny living things found all around us, in air, water, soil and on plants. When Disha left her uttapam for days, microbes grew on it and changed it. They changed its taste and smell, giving it a foul smell, and grew into mould, which appeared as coloured patches.
points: Microbes are tiny living things found everywhere, including air and around us
Microbes grew on the uttapam while it was left for days
Microbes changed the taste and smell, causing the foul smell
The coloured patches were mould, made of a colony of thousands of microbes
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Disha found a slice of bread left on the balcony covered with coloured patches. In the same kitchen, her grandmother showed her pickles made two months ago that were still delicious, because they were covered with a layer of oil. Grandmother was also drying chillies in the Sun and keeping drinking water in a clay matka.
activities.prompt: Why did the pickles stay good for two months while the bread got coloured patches?
options: The oil on the pickles kept air away, but the bread on the balcony had moisture and air that microbes need
The pickles were older, so their microbes had already finished growing
The bread was made of wheat, which microbes like more than pickles
The balcony sunlight made the bread grow patches, while the kitchen light protected the pickles

why.The pickles were older, so their microbe: Wrong: microbes do not stop growing just because time has passed; the pickles stayed good because of the oil
why.The bread was made of wheat, which micro: Wrong: the lesson does not say microbes prefer wheat; the bread spoiled because of the conditions around it
why.The balcony sunlight made the bread grow: Wrong: sunlight did not cause the patches; the patches came from microbes growing on the bread

activities.explanation: Correct: microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature, and oil keeps air out, so the pickles were protected while the bread was not

activities.context: Disha found a slice of bread left on the balcony covered with coloured patches. In the same kitchen, her grandmother showed her pickles made two months ago that were still delicious, because they were covered with a layer of oil. Grandmother was also drying chillies in the Sun and keeping drinking water in a clay matka.
activities.prompt: Disha wants to keep a fresh slice of bread safe to eat for a few days. What should she do?
options: Sprinkle water on it so it stays soft
Keep it in the fridge, where it is too cold for microbes to grow
Leave it on the balcony again so the Sun can see it
Cover it with a wet cloth to keep dust away

why.Sprinkle water on it so it stays soft: Wrong: adding water gives microbes the moisture they need, so the bread would spoil faster
why.Leave it on the balcony again so the Sun: Wrong: the balcony did not protect the first slice; leaving it there would let microbes grow again
why.Cover it with a wet cloth to keep dust a: Wrong: a wet cloth adds moisture, which is exactly what microbes need to grow

activities.explanation: Correct: a cold temperature slows down microbes, so the bread stays good longer

activities.context: Disha found a slice of bread left on the balcony covered with coloured patches. In the same kitchen, her grandmother showed her pickles made two months ago that were still delicious, because they were covered with a layer of oil. Grandmother was also drying chillies in the Sun and keeping drinking water in a clay matka.
activities.prompt: Disha washes some chillies and shuts them in a closed, damp box instead of drying them in the Sun. What is most likely to happen?
options: The chillies will become hotter than before
The chillies will turn into pickles on their own
The chillies may spoil, because the moisture inside the box lets microbes grow
The chillies will stay fresh, because a closed box keeps out all air

why.The chillies will become hotter than bef: Wrong: keeping chillies wet does not change how spicy they are
why.The chillies will turn into pickles on t: Wrong: pickles need to be covered with oil; a damp box does not make pickles
why.The chillies will stay fresh, because a: Wrong: a closed damp box does not keep out air, and even without air, the moisture still lets microbes grow

activities.explanation: Correct: without removing the moisture, microbes can grow, so the chillies are likely to spoil

activities.prompt: Explain why the pickles made two months ago were still delicious.
activities.answer: Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow. The pickles were covered with oil, and oil keeps out air. Since air could not reach the pickles, one thing microbes need was removed, so microbes could not grow and the pickles did not spoil.
points: Microbes need moisture, air and the right temperature to grow
Oil keeps out air
Removing any one need stops microbes
So microbes could not grow and the pickles stayed good
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Aditya Anna ate puffed rice and a sweet from a stall at a village fair. By evening he had an upset stomach. His grandmother said bad eating habits like eating stale food from open stalls can cause indigestion. She churned curd into buttermilk and gave it to him. At home that morning, Aditya had also watched idli batter rising on its own, and he remembered seeing sealed cans in a food factory on a school trip.
activities.prompt: Aditya's grandmother gives him buttermilk instead of a fizzy drink. What is she hoping will happen inside his stomach?
options: The microbes from the buttermilk will join the microbes already there and settle his digestion
The buttermilk will wash all microbes, good and bad, out of his stomach
The buttermilk will cool his stomach so the bad food becomes fresh again
The buttermilk will stop him feeling hungry until the fair food is digested

why.The buttermilk will wash all microbes, g: Wrong: washing out all microbes would remove the helpful ones too
why.The buttermilk will cool his stomach so: Wrong: food that has gone bad cannot become fresh again by cooling
why.The buttermilk will stop him feeling hun: Wrong: the aim is to fix digestion, not to hide hunger

activities.explanation: Correct: good microbes in curd/buttermilk team up with the stomach's good microbes to help digestion

activities.context: Aditya Anna ate puffed rice and a sweet from a stall at a village fair. By evening he had an upset stomach. His grandmother said bad eating habits like eating stale food from open stalls can cause indigestion. She churned curd into buttermilk and gave it to him. At home that morning, Aditya had also watched idli batter rising on its own, and he remembered seeing sealed cans in a food factory on a school trip.
activities.prompt: The stall at the fair kept its sweets in an open tray, while the factory Aditya visited seals its food in airtight cans. What is the most likely result of the difference?
options: Microbes from the air can settle on the open sweets, so they spoil faster than the sealed cans
The open sweets stay fresh longer because air keeps them dry
The sealed cans spoil faster because microbes grow better without air
Both spoil at exactly the same rate because packaging makes no difference

why.The open sweets stay fresh longer becaus: Wrong: open air is exactly what carries microbes to the food
why.The sealed cans spoil faster because mic: Wrong: the whole point of airtight sealing is to keep microbes out
why.Both spoil at exactly the same rate beca: Wrong: packaging is used precisely because it does make a difference

activities.explanation: Correct: airtight packaging keeps microbes away, so open food is more exposed and spoils sooner

activities.prompt: Explain why Aditya Anna's grandmother gave him buttermilk when he had an upset stomach after eating food at the fair.
activities.answer: Eating food from the fair, or bad eating habits, can cause indigestion. Curd or buttermilk made from it contains small good microbes. When Aditya drinks it, these microbes join the good microbes already in his stomach and together they help digestion, so his upset stomach gets better.
points: Links the fair food or bad eating habits to indigestion
Says curd or buttermilk contains good microbes
Says these microbes join the good microbes in the stomach
Concludes that this helps digestion and eases the upset stomach
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Disha is making a detective case diary on 'My Food, My Pride'. Every morning, her thatha walks to the vegetable market and brings home fresh fruits and vegetables. One evening, Appa came home carrying a bag of lychees. Disha remembered that lychee is a seasonal fruit, so the family had been waiting for it. Everyone sat together, peeled the fruits and shared them, feeling great joy. Disha wrote in her diary that fruits taste best in their season.
activities.prompt: Next month, Disha asks Appa to buy lychees again from the market. What will most likely happen?
options: Appa will easily find plenty of lychees at the market
Appa may not find lychees because their season will be over
Appa will buy bamboo shoots instead of lychees
Appa will stop going to the vegetable market

why.Appa will easily find plenty of lychees: Wrong: lychees are seasonal, so they are not available all year
why.Appa will buy bamboo shoots instead of l: Wrong: nothing in the case suggests Appa would switch to bamboo shoots
why.Appa will stop going to the vegetable ma: Wrong: Thatha goes to the market daily, so the family would not stop going

activities.explanation: Correct: since lychee is a seasonal fruit, it cannot be bought once the season ends

activities.context: Disha is making a detective case diary on 'My Food, My Pride'. Every morning, her thatha walks to the vegetable market and brings home fresh fruits and vegetables. One evening, Appa came home carrying a bag of lychees. Disha remembered that lychee is a seasonal fruit, so the family had been waiting for it. Everyone sat together, peeled the fruits and shared them, feeling great joy. Disha wrote in her diary that fruits taste best in their season.
activities.prompt: Why did everyone in Disha's family feel such great joy while eating the lychees?
options: Because the lychees had travelled a long way to reach them
Because they had waited for the fruit to come in its season
Because Disha wrote about them in her detective diary
Because Thatha bought them at a very low price

why.Because the lychees had travelled a long: Wrong: the joy came from waiting, not from the fruit travelling far
why.Because Disha wrote about them in her de: Wrong: writing in the diary came after, it did not cause the joy
why.Because Thatha bought them at a very low: Wrong: no price is mentioned in the case at all

activities.explanation: Correct: waiting for a seasonal fruit increases the joy of eating it

activities.context: Disha is making a detective case diary on 'My Food, My Pride'. Every morning, her thatha walks to the vegetable market and brings home fresh fruits and vegetables. One evening, Appa came home carrying a bag of lychees. Disha remembered that lychee is a seasonal fruit, so the family had been waiting for it. Everyone sat together, peeled the fruits and shared them, feeling great joy. Disha wrote in her diary that fruits taste best in their season.
activities.prompt: If Thatha bought mangoes grown by local farmers nearby, what could Disha conclude about them?
options: They would be fresh because they did not have to travel far
They would need to be peeled before eating
They would taste best only if stored for many months
They would be available in every season of the year

why.They would need to be peeled before eati: Wrong: peeling is about how fruits are eaten, not about being local
why.They would taste best only if stored for: Wrong: fruits taste best in season, not after long storage
why.They would be available in every season: Wrong: being local does not make a fruit available all year round

activities.explanation: Correct: local fruits stay fresh since they do not travel far

activities.prompt: Explain why Disha's family had to wait for lychees, and how waiting changed the way they enjoyed the fruit.
activities.answer: Lychee is a seasonal fruit, so it is not available throughout the year and the family had to wait for its season. Because they waited, everyone felt great joy when they finally peeled and shared the delicious fruits together. This shows that fruits taste best in their season and waiting increases the joy.
points: Lychee is a seasonal fruit
Seasonal fruits cannot be got at any time of the year
The family peeled and shared the fruits with joy
Waiting increases the joy of eating
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera was in a hurry during lunch break, so she took big bites of her chapati and swallowed them almost without chewing. She also forgot to rinse her mouth after eating. That evening, one of her back teeth started aching, and her mother noticed a small hole in that tooth.
activities.prompt: Why did Meera's back tooth most likely start aching?
options: Because she ate her food too slowly
Because she has a cavity in that tooth
Because she chewed the chapati too well
Because she rinsed her mouth after eating

why.Because she ate her food too slowly: Eating slowly is good for you, so it would not cause pain.
why.Because she chewed the chapati too well: Chewing properly is good for teeth and digestion, not a cause of pain.
why.Because she rinsed her mouth after eatin: Rinsing after eating is a good habit that protects teeth, not harms them.

activities.explanation: A hole in a tooth is a cavity, and an aching tooth can mean she needs a dentist.

activities.context: Meera was in a hurry during lunch break, so she took big bites of her chapati and swallowed them almost without chewing. She also forgot to rinse her mouth after eating. That evening, one of her back teeth started aching, and her mother noticed a small hole in that tooth.
activities.prompt: What could happen to Meera if she keeps swallowing big bites without chewing?
options: Her teeth will become sharper
Her mouth will make more saliva than needed
She could choke on her food
Her molars will change into canines

why.Her teeth will become sharper: Teeth do not change their shape by how fast you eat.
why.Her mouth will make more saliva than nee: Swallowing quickly without chewing does not help digestion.
why.Her molars will change into canines: Each tooth keeps its own job; teeth do not turn into other types.

activities.explanation: Food should be eaten slowly and chewed well, or it can get stuck and cause choking.

activities.prompt: Explain why we have different types of teeth in our mouth.
activities.answer: We have different types of teeth because different types of teeth have different uses. Incisors cut food, canines tear it, premolars crush it and molars grind it. Together they break food into smaller pieces and mush so it can be chewed properly and digested well.
points: Mentions that different teeth have different uses
Names incisors for cutting and canines for tearing
Names premolars for crushing and molars for grinding
Links chewing to breaking food into smaller pieces
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Detective Disha visited her friend Meera, whose grandmother had kept a bowl of rice covered overnight. In the morning, the rice smelled sour but everyone ate it happily. Grandmother called it pakhala. Meera wondered why the rice did not make anyone ill. Disha opened her notebook, thought about microbes, and finally the food mystery was solved with a smile.
activities.prompt: Meera's cousin leaves a bowl of cooked rice uncovered on a warm night. What will most likely happen to it by morning?
options: The helpful microbes in it will make it tastier
Some microbes will spoil it and it may become unsafe to eat
The rice will stay exactly the same forever
The rice will digest itself before anyone eats it

why.The helpful microbes in it will make it: Helpful microbes make food, they do not improve any rice left out
why.The rice will stay exactly the same fore: Food left out does not stay unchanged; microbes act on it
why.The rice will digest itself before anyon: Rice cannot digest itself; digestion happens inside our body

activities.explanation: Some microbes spoil food, so uncovered rice in the heat goes bad

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Health and Well-being

activities.prompt: Disha opened her old lunch box and a foul smell came out. What had changed the uttapam?
options: The Sun dried it up
Microbes grew on it
Sugar melted into it
Cold air froze it
activities.explanation: Microbes are tiny living things that grew on the food and changed it. They can change the taste and smell of food.

activities.prompt: Mould is a colony of thousands of microbes.
activities.explanation: Yes! Each coloured patch is a whole colony of tiny microbes living together.

activities.prompt: The pickle made two months ago was still delicious because it was covered with ______.
activities.hint: Think of the shiny layer floating on top of a pickle jar.
activities.explanation: Oil keeps out air, and microbes need air to grow. Well done, detective!

activities.prompt: Match each type of tooth to its job.
activities.explanation: Different teeth have different uses. That is why chewing breaks food into small pieces and mush.

activities.prompt: Put the events of Disha's food mystery in the order they happened.
items: Disha found her forgotten lunch box
A foul smell came out when she opened it
The uttapam had coloured patches
Aditya said the patches were mould
activities.explanation: First she found the box, then came the smell, then the patches, and finally Aditya solved the puzzle. Great sequencing!

activities.prompt: Lychee is available in the market all year round.
activities.explanation: Lychee is a seasonal fruit, so we need to wait for it. Waiting for it increases the joy!

activities.prompt: A cavity is a ______ in the tooth.
activities.hint: It is a small opening that a dentist may need to look at.
activities.explanation: A cavity is a hole in the tooth. Rinse after eating and brush regularly to keep your teeth safe.

activities.prompt: Aditya Anna had an upset stomach after eating food at a fair. What can help him feel better?
options: Eating more fair food
Skipping all meals for a week
Drinking very cold water
Curd or buttermilk
activities.explanation: Curd or buttermilk made from it can be given for an upset stomach. Small microbes in curd join the good microbes in your stomach to help digestion.

activities.prompt: Match each way of keeping food or drink good to how it works.
pairs: Oil on top of a pickle
activities.explanation: Each method takes away one thing microbes need. You have mastered the ways we preserve and store right!

boss.sceneAlt: A pizza covered with patches of mould, showing how food spoils when microbes grow on it.
boss.sceneCaption: Mould growing on food makes it spoil and smell bad, just like Disha's uttapam.

chapters.title: Our School — A Happy Place
chapters.summary: In this chapter: green school and a happy place; be a school explorer; waste management and segregation; let us be cool and dripping water.

lessons.title: Green School and a Happy Place

activities.prompt: Why does Mohit call his school his happy place?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: School: Our Happy Place
activities.body: Mohit loves school because he meets friends, plays games and learns new things. He calls school his happy place. School is where we feel safe and cared for. Aasha wants her school to be a green school. A green school saves water, manages waste, uses electricity carefully and plants more trees.
keyPoints: School is a happy place where we learn and feel safe.
A green school saves water and electricity and manages waste.
A green school plants more trees to make the campus green.
activities.explanation: School helps us learn, play and feel cared for, so we can help make it green and clean.

activities.prompt: Aasha's school plants trees, but children leave taps running and throw waste around. She says her school is a green school now. Is she right?
steps: A green school must do more than one thing, so trees alone are not enough.
A green school saves water, so running taps show a part is missing.
A green school manages waste, so waste on the ground shows another part is missing.
So Aasha is not right yet, because her school must also save water and manage waste.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why does Mohit love school?
options: Because he meets friends and learns new things
Because he gets long holidays there
Because he can sleep in class
activities.explanation: Mohit loves school for friends, games and learning new things. Well done!

activities.prompt: A green school makes the campus green by planting more ______.
activities.hint: Think of what grows tall and gives shade.
activities.explanation: Planting more trees makes the campus green. Great thinking!

activities.prompt: Which of these does a green school do?
options: It wastes water every day
It saves water and manages waste
It throws waste on the ground
activities.explanation: A green school manages waste, saves water and uses electricity carefully.

activities.prompt: Match each idea with what it means.
activities.explanation: Each friend has a special idea about school. You matched them all!

activities.prompt: Every child has the ______ to study in a clean and safe environment.
activities.hint: It is something every child should have.
activities.explanation: Every child has the right to a clean and safe place to study.

activities.prompt: Aasha says: put these steps in order to make a green school.
items: Look closely at the school
Decide what to do
Plant more trees
Save water and electricity
activities.explanation: First look closely, then decide, then act. Aasha's plan works step by step!

activities.prompt: A school plants many new trees. But children throw waste all over the ground. What will happen to the school campus?
options: It will look green and clean.
It will not look fully clean and green.
The trees will grow faster than ever.
The waste will turn into water.

Wrong: thinks planting trees alone makes a school green.
Wrong: thinks trees can grow well in a dirty campus.
Wrong: thinks waste changes into water by itself.

activities.explanation: Right: a green school also manages waste, so waste spoils it.

activities.prompt: Two classes want to save water. Class A fixes its leaking tap and counts the water used each day. Class B only says it will save water. Which class can really show it saved water?
options: Class B, because saying it is enough.
Class A, because it fixed the tap and counted the water.
Both classes, because both want to save water.
Neither class, because water cannot be counted.

Wrong: thinks wanting something is the same as doing it.
why.Both classes, because both want to save: Wrong: thinks a wish alone proves the water was saved.
why.Neither class, because water cannot be c: Wrong: thinks water use cannot be measured at all.

activities.explanation: Right: fixing the tap and counting shows real saving of water.

activities.prompt: Riya says her school is a green school. The school has many trees. But taps are left running all day. What is wrong with Riya's claim?
options: Trees cannot grow in a school.
A green school must also save water carefully.
Taps should never be used in a school.
Riya should plant even more trees first.

Wrong: thinks trees do not belong in schools.
Wrong: thinks green schools use no water at all.
Wrong: thinks more trees can fix wasted water.

activities.explanation: Right: a green school saves water, so running taps break the claim.

activities.prompt: Every child has a right to study in a clean and safe place. A school's toilets are very dirty. Why must the school clean them?
options: So the school can charge children more money.
So children can study in a clean and safe place.
So the school can buy more new toilets.
So children can stay away from school.

why.So the school can charge children more m: Wrong: thinks cleaning is done to collect money.
Wrong: thinks the answer is buying new things, not cleaning.
Wrong: thinks dirty toilets are a reason to skip school.

activities.explanation: Right: clean toilets keep the school healthy for every child.

lessons.sceneAlt: A green school campus in Chennai where children learn about farming among trees and plants.
lessons.sceneCaption: An urban green campus of Hive Montessori School Chennai integrating farm learning with Montessori education.

lessons.title: Be a School Explorer

activities.prompt: What secrets could your school be hiding, right where you walk every day?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet the School Explorer Teams
activities.body: You can join a School Explorer Team with your friends. Each team picks a fun name for itself. Before you set off, your team must decide what it will observe. Some teams watch lights and fans, some watch water, some watch traffic at the gate, and some watch litter. Good explorers always plan first, then look carefully.
keyPoints: Children can form School Explorer Teams.
Each group picks a name for itself.
Before exploring, each group decides what to observe.
activities.explanation: Explorers plan first: pick a team, pick a name, pick what to watch.

activities.prompt: Two friends want to be School Explorers. One says: 'Let us just walk around and look at everything.' The other says: 'Wait, let us first decide what to observe.' Who will learn more, and why?
steps: If you look at everything, your eyes jump from one thing to another, so you may miss important things.
If you decide first what to observe, you know exactly what to watch for, so your notes become useful.
The Water Watchers watch only taps and tanks, so they find every leak because they are looking for leaks.
So the friend who decides what to observe first will learn more, because a plan makes watching sharp.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Your explorer team is ready to go. What must the team decide BEFORE it starts exploring?
options: Who will carry the bag
What the team will observe
Which game to play after
Where to sit in class
activities.explanation: Well done! Every group decides what to observe before exploring, so everyone knows what to look for.

activities.prompt: A tap in the corridor keeps dripping. Which team should note it down?
options: Water Watchers
Waste Warriors
Traffic Trackers
Green Guardians
activities.explanation: Water Watchers look for leaking taps around the school.

activities.prompt: Waste Warriors check where ______ is seen and what kinds of it are around the school.
activities.hint: Rubbish lying on the ground is called this.
activities.explanation: Waste Warriors look for litter and note the different kinds they see.

activities.prompt: Match each team to the thing it checks.
activities.explanation: Each team has its own special job: energy, water, traffic or waste.

activities.prompt: Green Guardians walk around during the day. Which check do they also do?
options: Which areas feel hottest and coolest
Which taps drip the most
Which bins are full of food waste
Which children cross the road
activities.explanation: Green Guardians find out which areas feel hottest and coolest during the day.

activities.prompt: Put the explorer steps in the right order.
items: Form your School Explorer Team
Choose a name for your group
Decide what your team will observe
Start exploring the school
activities.explanation: First form the team, then pick a name, then decide what to observe, and only then explore.

activities.prompt: A group checks lights and fans left on in empty rooms. They also check which rooms feel hottest at noon. Next week a new friend joins them. What should the group tell the friend to do first?
options: Decide what to observe before going to any room
Walk around the school and write down everything seen
Copy the notes from last week without looking again
Ask the teacher which group has the nicest name

why.Walk around the school and write down ev: This child thinks exploring means looking at everything, but then the eyes jump and important things get missed.
why.Copy the notes from last week without lo: This child thinks old notes are enough, but new checks may show something different now.
why.Ask the teacher which group has the nice: This child thinks the group name matters most, but a name does not tell you what to observe.

activities.explanation: Right. A group must first decide what to observe, so the new friend knows what to watch for.

activities.prompt: A Water Watcher team finds two water tanks. Tank A is open at the top. Tank B has a clean cover on top. Which tank should the team worry about more, and why?
options: Tank A, because Water Watchers check if tanks are clean and covered
Tank A, because an open tank always holds more water than a closed one
Tank B, because a cover stops children from seeing the water level
Tank B, because covered tanks are only used on hot days

why.Tank A, because an open tank always hold: This child guessed about water amount, but the team's job is checking covers, not measuring water.
why.Tank B, because a cover stops children f: This child made up a reason against covers, but covers are what Water Watchers want to see.
why.Tank B, because covered tanks are only u: This child invented a rule about hot days, but covers matter every day, not only hot days.

activities.explanation: Right. Water Watchers check if tanks are clean and covered, so an open tank fails that check.

activities.prompt: A Traffic Tracker says: 'The road outside our gate is safe for children because cars come at all times, so I can check it any single time I like.' What is the flaw in this claim?
options: Traffic changes during the day, so arrival and exit times must be checked
Traffic is the same all day, so one check at any time is enough
Traffic outside the gate does not matter, only litter inside matters
Traffic should be checked only on holidays, when roads are quiet

why.Traffic is the same all day, so one chec: This child believes traffic never changes, but arrival and exit times are exactly when it changes most.
why.Traffic outside the gate does not matter: This child mixed up groups, because litter is Waste Warrior work and traffic is Traffic Tracker work.
why.Traffic should be checked only on holida: This child wants the easiest time, but quiet holiday roads hide the busy times that need checking.

activities.explanation: Right. Traffic Trackers check the gate at arrival and exit times, because traffic is different then.

activities.prompt: A Waste Warrior sees banana peels near the canteen and paper bits near the library. The school has only one big bin for everything. What should the Waste Warrior check and report?
options: Where the litter is, what kinds are seen, and if separate bins are needed
Only the number of children, because more children always means more fun
Only the colour of the bin, because a bright bin collects all litter by itself
Only the weather, because litter appears only when it rains

why.Only the number of children, because mor: This child went off track, because counting children does not tell where litter is or its kinds.
why.Only the colour of the bin, because a br: This child believes a bin works by itself, but bins need separate ones for food and other waste.
why.Only the weather, because litter appears: This child made up a weather rule, but litter is found in all kinds of weather.

activities.explanation: Right. Waste Warriors check where litter is, what kinds are seen, and if there are separate bins.

lessons.sceneAlt: Children at the Indo-German School in Nelavoy, India, a free school built with Indian and German cooperation.
lessons.sceneCaption: The Indo-German School in Nelavoy, India, where Indian and German perspectives work together.

lessons.title: Waste Management and Segregation

activities.prompt: Where does your trash go after it leaves your bin?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Sorting Our Waste
activities.body: Every day we throw things away. We can reduce waste by using only what we need. We can reuse things instead of throwing away useful items. Still, some waste remains, like food peels, leftovers and paper. We separate this waste into dry and wet categories. This helps us manage it better.
keyPoints: Use only what you need to reduce waste.
Reuse useful things instead of throwing them away.
Separate waste into dry and wet to manage it better.
activities.explanation: Sorting waste the right way keeps our homes and streets clean.

activities.prompt: After a birthday party at home, the dustbin is full. What can the family do so that less waste is left?
steps: First, the family can use only what they need, so less waste is made in the first place.
They can reuse jars and boxes at home, so useful things are not thrown away.
Even then, food peels, leftovers and paper still remain, so waste cannot become zero.
So they separate waste into wet and dry, and check each item was put correctly, to manage it better.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: In the Segregation Game, which box do you use for wet waste?
options: The blue box
The green box
The red box
activities.explanation: Great job! The green box is for wet waste and the blue box is for dry waste.

activities.prompt: In the Segregation Game, dry waste goes into the ______ box.
activities.hint: Think of the colour of a clear sky.
activities.explanation: Well done! The blue box is for dry waste, and the green box is for wet waste.

activities.prompt: Match each item with where it should go.
activities.explanation: Super sorting! Wet waste, dry waste and recycler items each have their own place.

activities.prompt: Why do we separate waste into dry and wet categories?
options: To make the waste smell nice
To manage the waste better
To make the bins look colourful
activities.explanation: Yes! Separating dry and wet waste helps us manage it better.

activities.prompt: Put these steps of caring for waste in order.
items: Use only what you need
Reuse things instead of throwing them away
Separate the waste that still remains into dry and wet
activities.explanation: Perfect order! First reduce, then reuse, then sort what still remains.

activities.prompt: How can we play a better role in waste management?
options: Sort our waste well to make sanitation workers' work easier and safer
Ask sanitation workers to take away all our waste without sorting
Leave waste outside so sanitation workers can sort it for us
activities.explanation: Well done! Sorting our waste makes sanitation workers' work easier and safer. They can also share what they do and the challenges they face.

activities.prompt: A banana peel is wet waste. It should go in the green box. Ravi puts it in the blue box. What will happen to the waste?
options: The wet and dry waste will get mixed together.
The peel will turn into dry waste inside the box.
The peel will slowly disappear inside the blue box.
The green box will fill up faster than before.

why.The peel will turn into dry waste inside: Thinks the box can change the waste; a box cannot change wet into dry.
why.The peel will slowly disappear inside th: Thinks waste vanishes in a bin; waste does not disappear on its own.
why.The green box will fill up faster than b: Thinks boxes fill equally; the green box will actually get less waste.

activities.explanation: Right. Wet waste in the blue box mixes the two kinds, so sorting is spoiled.

activities.prompt: Old newspapers are kept aside in many homes. One recycler takes newspapers. Another recycler takes old plastic. Why do we keep newspapers aside?
options: Different recyclers collect different items, so each gets its own waste.
Newspapers are wet waste, so they cannot go with other waste.
Newspapers are very heavy, so they need a big truck.
Newspapers rot very fast, so they must be taken quickly.

why.Newspapers are wet waste, so they cannot: Confuses wet and dry; newspapers are dry waste, not wet waste.
why.Newspapers are very heavy, so they need: Thinks weight is the reason; the real reason is which recycler takes what.
why.Newspapers rot very fast, so they must b: Thinks newspapers rot like peels; the reason is about recyclers, not rotting.

activities.explanation: Right. Each recycler takes certain items, so newspapers wait for the right recycler.

activities.prompt: Dev puts all his waste in one big bin. He says this saves time. What is wrong with Dev's idea?
options: Mixed waste is hard to sort, so workers' work becomes harder.
One big bin costs more money than two small bins.
Big bins fill up much faster than small bins do.
Waste in one bin becomes wet after some time.

why.One big bin costs more money than two sm: Thinks the problem is money; the problem is mixed waste, not cost.
why.Big bins fill up much faster than small: Thinks bin size is the problem; size does not decide if waste is mixed.
why.Waste in one bin becomes wet after some: Thinks mixing changes waste; waste does not turn wet by sitting together.

activities.explanation: Right. Mixing wet and dry makes sorting hard, so workers' work is not easy and safe.

activities.prompt: An empty jar can still be used. Meena keeps her pencils in it. She does not throw it away. What happens to the waste?
options: Less waste remains, because the jar is used again.
The jar becomes wet waste after some days.
The jar makes more waste in the house.
The jar must now go into the green box.

why.The jar becomes wet waste after some day: Thinks jars change type; a jar does not become wet waste.
Thinks reusing creates waste; reusing actually stops waste.
Thinks all used things go in green; green is for wet waste only.

activities.explanation: Right. Reusing a useful item means it is not thrown, so less waste remains.

lessons.sceneAlt: Blue and green public waste segregation bins standing on a street in Amritsar, Punjab, India.
lessons.sceneCaption: Blue and green bins in Amritsar, part of the Swachh Bharat initiative, help people separate their waste.

lessons.title: Let Us Be Cool and Dripping Water

activities.prompt: Why does one tiny drip from a tap matter so much?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Why Do Some Rooms Feel Cooler?
activities.body: Have you noticed that some rooms feel warmer than others? Trees that give shade, windows that let the breeze in, and a white roof can all help a room stay cool. A black surface absorbs heat, so it gets hot. Small changes around us can make a big difference to how cool we feel.
keyPoints: Some rooms feel warmer than others.
Shade trees and breezy windows help a room stay cool.
A white roof stays cool, but a black surface absorbs heat.
activities.explanation: Clever choices like shade, windows and a white roof can keep a room cool.

activities.prompt: Ravi's new classroom has no windows. It feels very hot in summer. His friend's classroom has big windows and a shady tree outside. Why is one room cool and the other hot?
steps: Ravi's room has no windows, so no breeze can come in to cool it.
The friend's room has windows, so the moving breeze makes it cooler.
The shady tree blocks the hot sun, so less heat reaches the friend's room.
So windows for breeze and shade from trees make a room cooler.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Every Drop Counts
activities.body: Water is precious. Even a small leak can waste a lot of water over time, because drop by drop the water adds up. You can catch dripping water in a glass and measure the time to see it happen. The Jal Shakti Abhiyan asks us to plant trees, catch rainwater and use water wisely. In Ladakh, students help make ice stupas that melt in summer to water school gardens.
keyPoints: A small leak can waste a lot of water over time.
Catch drips in a glass and measure the time to see how water adds up.
Jal Shakti Abhiyan encourages planting trees, catching rainwater and using water wisely.
activities.explanation: Watching a drip teaches us how much water we can lose without noticing.

activities.prompt: Your school wants a cooler roof. Which colour roof should it choose?
options: A black roof
A blue roof
A white roof
A green roof
activities.explanation: A white roof can make the roof cool, while a black surface absorbs heat.

activities.prompt: Trees that give ______ can help a room feel cooler.
activities.hint: Think of standing under a tree on a hot day.
activities.explanation: Trees that give shade can make a real difference to how a room feels.

activities.prompt: A black surface absorbs heat.
activities.explanation: Yes! That is why a black surface feels hot in the sun.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what it does.
activities.explanation: Each of these helps in its own way to keep rooms cool.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in order to see how a dripping tap wastes water.
items: Put a glass under the dripping tap
Watch the drops fall into the glass
Measure the time with a clock
See how much water adds up
activities.explanation: First catch the drips, then watch and measure, and finally see how the water adds up.

activities.prompt: In Ladakh, students help make ice stupas. Why are they useful?
options: They keep the classroom cool in summer
They melt in summer to water school gardens
They catch rainwater for the whole town
They stop the wind from blowing
activities.explanation: Ice stupas are tall ice towers that slowly melt in summer to water school gardens.

activities.prompt: Meera paints her playhouse roof white. Her brother paints his black. The sun shines on both all day. Which roof feels cooler in the evening, and why?
options: The white roof, because white does not soak up as much heat.
The black roof, because black surfaces always stay cold.
Both roofs, because paint never changes how hot a roof gets.
The black roof, because black paint is thicker than white paint.

why.The black roof, because black surfaces a: Wrong: the child thinks black is cold, but black soaks up heat.
why.Both roofs, because paint never changes: Wrong: the child thinks surface colour makes no difference, but it does.
why.The black roof, because black paint is t: Wrong: the child blames paint thickness, but colour is what matters.

activities.explanation: Correct: white does not soak up heat the way black does, so it stays cooler.

activities.prompt: A tap drips all night while everyone sleeps. In the morning, a bucket under it is full. What does this show?
options: A small drip stops being a problem after a few hours.
Even a small drip adds up and wastes much water over time.
Drips only waste water when the tap is turned on fully.
Water drips faster at night than during the day.

why.A small drip stops being a problem after: Wrong: the child thinks small drips do not matter, but they add up.
why.Drips only waste water when the tap is t: Wrong: the child thinks only a strong flow wastes water, but drips do too.
why.Water drips faster at night than during: Wrong: the child invents a reason about night time, which is not the cause.

activities.explanation: Correct: drop by drop, the bucket filled, so much water was wasted.

activities.prompt: Two children test which classroom stays cooler. One sits in a closed room with a fan. The other sits in a room with open windows and a breeze. Both rooms are the same size. Why is this not a fair test of windows alone?
options: Because the rooms are the same size, so it is fair.
Because the fan also cools the first room, so two things changed.
Because children cannot test classrooms in the daytime.
Because windows should be kept shut for a fair test.

why.Because the rooms are the same size, so: Wrong: the child thinks same size makes it fair, but the cooling source differs.
why.Because children cannot test classrooms: Wrong: the child thinks timing is the problem, but it is not.
why.Because windows should be kept shut for: Wrong: the child thinks windows must be shut, which stops the test.

activities.explanation: Correct: a fair test changes only one thing, and here the fan adds a second thing.

activities.prompt: A boy says, 'Our school painted the roof white, so we never need to save water now.' His friend disagrees. What is wrong with the boy's claim?
options: A white roof keeps the room cool, but it does not save water.
A white roof saves water only in the winter months.
A white roof saves water only when the tap is dripping.
A white roof makes water pipes run faster in summer.

why.A white roof saves water only in the win: Wrong: the child thinks roof colour works only in one season.
why.A white roof saves water only when the t: Wrong: the child links roof colour to dripping taps, which is not connected.
why.A white roof makes water pipes run faste: Wrong: the child invents a false effect on pipes.

activities.explanation: Correct: a cool roof helps with heat, but saving water is a separate job.

lessons.title: Greenery Around Us and Traffic Signs

activities.prompt: Why do birds and butterflies love some trees more than others?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Trees Around Us and Staying Safe on Roads
activities.body: Trees are wonderful neighbours. They give birds and insects food and a home. They keep the air clean and give us cool shade. But roads can be unsafe. Many accidents happen when people do not follow traffic rules. That is why you should know the rules and follow them. You can also help, by designing a signboard for your school gate.
keyPoints: Trees give food, shade and homes to birds and insects.
Trees keep the air clean and the surroundings cool.
Many accidents happen when people do not follow traffic rules.
You can design a signboard that gives a clear message.
activities.explanation: Trees care for us, and traffic rules keep us safe.

activities.prompt: The sun is very hot. One side of the playground has a big tree. The other side has no tree. Where do the children want to play at break time, and why?
steps: The tree keeps the air clean, so the air under it feels fresh.
The tree gives shade, so the hot sun cannot fall on the children.
The tree keeps the ground cool, so that side is not hot to sit on.
So the children will play under the tree, because it is cool and shady there.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: You Can Help Too
activities.body: You can do two kind things this week. First, find the names of trees and plants that attract birds and butterflies. Then try to create a butterfly garden in your school. Second, design a signboard for your school gate. Make sure it gives a clear message to drivers, parents or students.
keyPoints: Find names of plants that attract birds and butterflies.
You can try to create a butterfly garden in school.
Design a signboard for the school gate.
The sign should give a clear message to drivers, parents or students.
activities.explanation: Small ideas from children can make school greener and safer.

activities.prompt: It is a hot sunny day. You sit under a big tree and feel cooler. Why?
options: The tree makes cold water
The tree gives shade and keeps surroundings cool
The tree blows cool wind from its leaves
activities.explanation: Well done! Trees give shade and help keep the surroundings cool.

activities.prompt: Trees keep the air ______ for everyone.
activities.hint: Think of what a tree does to the air we breathe.
activities.explanation: Great! Trees keep the air clean, so we can breathe easily.

activities.prompt: Trees are home to many living beings.
activities.explanation: Yes! Birds, insects and many other living beings live in trees.

activities.prompt: Match each problem with its helpful solution from the lesson.
activities.explanation: Super matching! Trees solve green problems, and rules solve road problems.

activities.prompt: You are designing a signboard for your school gate. What is the most important thing about it?
options: It should give a clear message to drivers, parents or students
It should be the biggest board on the road
It should use as few colours as possible
activities.explanation: Yes! A good sign gives a clear message to drivers, parents or students.

activities.prompt: A big tree near a house is cut down. In summer, the house gets more hot sun. What will happen to the rooms?
options: They will stay cool, because walls keep heat out.
They will become hotter, because the tree gave shade.
They will become cooler, because more wind comes in.
They will stay the same, because trees do not help houses.

why.They will stay cool, because walls keep: Walls help a little, but the child forgot the tree was blocking the hot sun.
why.They will become cooler, because more wi: Wind may come in, but the child forgot that shade was keeping the house cool.
why.They will stay the same, because trees d: Wrong. Trees do help houses by giving shade and keeping things cool.

activities.explanation: Right. Trees give shade and keep surroundings cool, so without the tree more heat comes in.

activities.prompt: A school garden has many plants. Birds and insects come there every day. Why do they keep coming?
options: The garden is quiet, so animals like quiet places only.
The plants give them food, and the trees give them a home.
The children play there, so the animals come to watch.
The garden is near the road, so animals rest there.

why.The garden is quiet, so animals like qui: Quiet may help, but the child missed the real reason: food and home.
why.The children play there, so the animals: Animals do not come to watch children; the child mixed up the reason.
why.The garden is near the road, so animals: Being near a road is not why they come; the child missed food and home.

activities.explanation: Right. Trees are homes to living beings and give food to birds and insects.

activities.prompt: Some children want a butterfly garden in school. Which plan will work best?
options: Plant any plants, because butterflies like every plant the same.
Find the names of plants that attract butterflies, then plant those.
Plant many trees far apart, so butterflies have space to fly.
Put a signboard in the garden, so butterflies can read it.

why.Plant any plants, because butterflies li: Butterflies do not like every plant the same; the child forgot to find the right plants.
why.Plant many trees far apart, so butterfli: Space to fly is not the main need; the child forgot butterflies need the right plants.
why.Put a signboard in the garden, so butter: Butterflies cannot read signs; the child mixed up signboards with gardens.

activities.explanation: Right. Children can find plant names that attract butterflies and make a butterfly garden.

activities.prompt: A driver is in a hurry. He does not stop at the crossing. A scooter comes and they crash. Why did this happen?
options: The road was too small for a car and a scooter.
The scooter was going too fast on the road.
The driver did not follow traffic rules at the crossing.
The crash happened because it was a hot sunny day.

why.The road was too small for a car and a s: Road size is not the reason here; the child missed the driver's mistake.
why.The scooter was going too fast on the ro: The prompt says nothing about the scooter's speed; the child blamed the wrong person.
why.The crash happened because it was a hot: Weather is not the reason here; the child missed the rule that was broken.

activities.explanation: Right. Many accidents happen because people do not follow traffic rules correctly.

activities.prompt: Children must design a signboard for the school gate. Which sign gives the clearest message to drivers?
options: A sign with a long story about the school's history.
A sign with many colours but no words or picture.
A sign that says 'Go slow, children crossing' in big letters.
A sign that says 'Welcome' with the school song below.

why.A sign with a long story about the schoo: A long story cannot be read fast by drivers; the child missed the need for a clear message.
why.A sign with many colours but no words or: Colours alone do not tell drivers what to do; the child forgot the message matters.
why.A sign that says 'Welcome' with the scho: A welcome sign is nice but does not tell drivers what to do at the gate.

activities.explanation: Right. The sign should give a clear message to drivers, parents or students.

activities.prompt: Mohit says, 'Some accidents happen even when rules are followed. So traffic rules do not help.' What is wrong with his claim?
options: He is right, because accidents can happen at any time.
He forgot that many accidents happen when rules are NOT followed.
He forgot that only drivers need to know the rules.
He is right, because rules are hard to learn and follow.

why.He is right, because accidents can happe: Accidents can happen, but that does not show rules do not help; the child agreed too fast.
why.He forgot that only drivers need to know: Everyone should know the rules, but that is not the flaw in Mohit's claim.
why.He is right, because rules are hard to l: Rules being hard does not prove they do not help; the child missed the real flaw.

activities.explanation: Right. Many accidents happen because people do not follow rules, so rules do help.

lessons.title: Fire Safety and What We Do Matters

activities.prompt: What should you do if you ever see smoke or fire?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Learning to Stay Safe
activities.body: Mohit's school arranged a session on fire safety. Learning how to stay safe from dangers like fire is very important. When you know what to do, being prepared helps everyone feel safer and more confident. In this lesson, you will learn the steps of a fire drill and how small kind actions make places peaceful and welcoming.
keyPoints: Mohit's school held a fire safety session.
Learning about fire keeps us safe from danger.
Being prepared makes us feel safer and more confident.
activities.explanation: Knowing what to do before danger comes is the best way to stay safe.

activities.prompt: Smoke fills the classroom during a fire drill. Ravi wants to hide under his desk. His friend Meera wants to run fast to the door. What should they really do, and why?
steps: Smoke rises up, so the air near the floor is cleaner to breathe.
Running fast can make someone fall, so staying calm keeps everyone safe.
Hiding under a desk means no one can see you and help you get out.
So Ravi and Meera should crawl low, stay calm, and walk to the exit together.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What We Do Matters
activities.body: Our behaviour can make places peaceful and welcoming. We show respect and kindness by waiting for our turn and using kind words. When we are kind and polite, everyone feels happy. Just like fire drills keep us safe, good behaviour keeps our school a happy place for all.
keyPoints: Good behaviour makes places peaceful and welcoming.
Wait for your turn and use kind words.
Kindness and politeness make everyone feel happy.
activities.explanation: Small kind actions, like waiting your turn, make everyone feel happy.

activities.prompt: During a fire drill, what should you do?
options: Move quickly and calmly to the nearest exit route
Wait inside the classroom until someone calls you
Run as fast as you can to the playground gate
Look for your bag before leaving the room
activities.explanation: In a fire drill, we move quickly and calmly to the nearest exit route. Calm and quick keeps everyone safe.

activities.prompt: After leaving the building, go to the ______ point and stay with your group.
activities.hint: It is the special place where everyone gathers.
activities.explanation: The assembly point is where the whole group gathers, so teachers know everyone is safe.

activities.prompt: During a fire drill, you should panic and run.
activities.explanation: We must not panic and not run. Staying calm helps you think clearly and reach safety.

activities.prompt: Why should you crawl low under smoke with your mouth covered?
options: To breathe cleaner air
To move faster than others
To hide from the teachers
To keep your clothes clean
activities.explanation: Crawling low with your mouth covered helps you breathe cleaner air under the smoke.

activities.prompt: Match each fire safety rule with what it means.
pairs: Move to the nearest exit route
Alert staff or teachers at once
activities.explanation: Each rule has a clear purpose: leave calmly, breathe safely, gather together, and tell a teacher at once.

activities.prompt: Put the fire drill steps in the right order.
items: Move quickly and calmly to the nearest exit route
Go to the assembly point and stay with your group
Alert staff or teachers if anyone is missing or injured
activities.explanation: First leave the building calmly, then gather at the assembly point, then tell a teacher if anyone is missing or hurt.

activities.prompt: A school has a fire drill. The bell rings loudly. Some children start shouting and pushing at the door. What is the best thing for the class to do?
options: Push harder so everyone gets out first.
Move calmly together along the exit route.
Sit down and wait for the smoke to go away.
Run in different directions to find a way out.

Pushing causes panic and someone may get hurt, so this is unsafe.
why.Sit down and wait for the smoke to go aw: Waiting inside during a fire keeps children near danger, so this is wrong.
why.Run in different directions to find a wa: Splitting up means teachers cannot keep the group together, so this is wrong.

activities.explanation: Right: moving calmly on the exit route is exactly what a fire drill teaches.

activities.prompt: There is smoke in a room. The air near the ceiling looks dark and thick. The air near the floor looks clearer. What should a child do to breathe better?
options: Stand tall and walk quickly through the smoke.
Cover the mouth and crawl low near the floor.
Open a window and stand near it to breathe.
Hold the breath and run out as fast as possible.

why.Stand tall and walk quickly through the: The cleaner air is low, not high, so standing tall means breathing bad smoke.
why.Open a window and stand near it to breat: The lesson does not say windows help, and standing up means breathing smoke.
why.Hold the breath and run out as fast as p: Running can cause falls, and holding the breath does not clean the air.

activities.explanation: Right: crawling low with the mouth covered gives cleaner air to breathe.

activities.prompt: During a fire drill, Anu feels scared. She slips into the big cupboard in the corner of the room. Why is hiding in the cupboard a bad idea?
options: Cupboards are too small for two children to hide in.
The cupboard door makes a loud noise when it shuts.
Nobody will know where she is, so nobody can help her.
Her clothes will get dusty inside the dark cupboard.

why.Cupboards are too small for two children: Size is not the real problem; even a big hiding place is unsafe.
why.The cupboard door makes a loud noise whe: Noise is not the danger; the danger is being hidden from helpers.
why.Her clothes will get dusty inside the da: Dust is a small worry, not the real reason hiding is unsafe.

activities.explanation: Right: hiding means teachers cannot find her or take her to safety.

activities.prompt: After a fire drill, the class stands at the assembly point. The teacher calls the names. Rima's friend Samir is not there. What should Rima do?
options: Run back inside the building to look for him.
Stay with her group and tell the teacher at once.
Wait quietly and hope he comes to the assembly point.
Shout his name very loudly across the playground.

why.Run back inside the building to look for: Going back inside puts Rima in danger too, so this is unsafe.
why.Wait quietly and hope he comes to the as: Hoping and waiting wastes time; adults must know at once.
why.Shout his name very loudly across the pl: Shouting may cause panic and does not alert the right person.

activities.explanation: Right: staying with the group and alerting the teacher gets help fast.

activities.prompt: Two classes learn fire safety. Class A only reads the rules once. Class B practises a fire drill many times. A fire drill happens one day. Why will Class B probably feel better during the drill?
options: Class B is cleverer than Class A at reading books.
Class B is lucky, and luck keeps children safe.
Class A did not want to feel safe in a fire.
Practice helps Class B feel prepared, calm and confident.

why.Class B is cleverer than Class A at read: Being clever at reading is not the reason; doing the drill is.
why.Class B is lucky, and luck keeps childre: Luck is not a plan; being prepared is what helps.
why.Class A did not want to feel safe in a f: Class A simply practised less; wanting safety is not the difference.

activities.explanation: Right: being prepared through practice makes people feel safer and confident.

activities.prompt: In the lunch line, Dev pushes ahead of everyone. Meena waits for her turn and speaks kindly. Later, children want to sit near Meena, not Dev. What does this show?
options: Kind behaviour makes others feel happy and welcome.
Pushing is fine if you reach the food faster.
Children only like others who are the fastest runners.
Waiting in a line is a rule only for young children.

why.Pushing is fine if you reach the food fa: Pushing is not kind, so this misses what really matters.
why.Children only like others who are the fa: Speed is not the point; kind and polite behaviour is.
why.Waiting in a line is a rule only for you: Waiting for your turn shows respect at every age, not just when young.

activities.explanation: Right: kindness and respect make places peaceful and people feel happy.
