activities.context: Mohit loves going to school because he meets his friends, plays games and learns new things, so he calls it his happy place. His classmate Aasha wants to make her school better like a green school. She suggests that the class should look closely at the school and decide what to do. She knows a green school manages waste, saves water, uses electricity carefully and plants more trees. The school also follows Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya, which keeps the campus clean and healthy for all.
activities.prompt: One day the students start throwing all the waste from their lunch into a single pile instead of sorting it. What will most likely happen to Aasha's green school plan?
options: The school will find it harder to keep the campus clean and manage the waste properly
The school will automatically get more trees planted on the campus
The students will start saving more water without doing anything else
The school will stop needing safe drinking water altogether

why.The school will automatically get more t: Wrong: planting trees is a separate step and does not happen because of waste piles.
why.The students will start saving more wate: Wrong: saving water is a different part of a green school and is not connected here.
why.The school will stop needing safe drinki: Wrong: safe drinking water is a facility, not something affected by lunch waste.

activities.explanation: Correct: a green school manages waste, so mixing all waste works against that plan.

activities.context: Mohit loves going to school because he meets his friends, plays games and learns new things, so he calls it his happy place. His classmate Aasha wants to make her school better like a green school. She suggests that the class should look closely at the school and decide what to do. She knows a green school manages waste, saves water, uses electricity carefully and plants more trees. The school also follows Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya, which keeps the campus clean and healthy for all.
activities.prompt: During the games period, Aasha notices taps left running in the corridor. Following her own suggestion, what should she and her class do first?
options: Look closely at where water is being wasted and decide what the class can do about it
Ask the school to stop giving the students any water during games
Plant more trees near the corridor so the water is used up
Tell everyone to use more electricity instead of water

why.Ask the school to stop giving the studen: Wrong: stopping water completely is not saving water; students still need safe drinking water.
why.Plant more trees near the corridor so th: Wrong: planting trees makes the campus green but does not fix running taps.
why.Tell everyone to use more electricity in: Wrong: using more electricity is the opposite of using electricity carefully.

activities.explanation: Correct: Aasha suggests looking closely at the school and deciding what to do, so observing the waste and planning comes first.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between what Mohit loves about school and what Aasha wants to change about her school?
activities.answer: Mohit loves school because he meets friends, plays games and learns new things, so he calls it his happy place. Aasha, however, wants to make her school better like a green school. She wants the school to manage waste, save water, use electricity carefully and plant more trees, and she suggests looking closely at the school first to decide what to do.
points: Mohit's reason: friends, games and learning new things make school his happy place
Aasha's goal: make the school better like a green school
A green school manages waste, saves water, uses electricity carefully and plants trees
Aasha's method: look closely at the school and decide what to do
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between what the Green Guardians observe and what the Waste Warriors observe? Explain with examples from the chapter.
activities.answer: Green Guardians observe how energy and heat are used, such as lights and fans left on when no one is using them, whether classrooms use natural light, and which areas feel hottest and coolest. Waste Warriors observe litter instead: where it is, what kinds are seen, and whether there are separate bins for food waste and other waste.
points: Green Guardians: lights and fans on when no one uses them
Green Guardians: natural light, and hottest and coolest areas
Waste Warriors: where litter is and what kinds are seen
Waste Warriors: separate bins for food waste and other waste
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera's family cleans the kitchen after dinner. Mother reminds everyone to take only as much food as they will eat, and an old jar is kept for storing spices instead of being thrown away. Still, vegetable peels, leftover rice and some paper remain. The family keeps two boxes in the kitchen, one green and one blue, and old newspapers are kept aside for the recycler who visits on weekends.
activities.prompt: Why does Meera's family keep old newspapers aside instead of putting them in the blue box?
options: Because a particular recycler comes to collect newspapers
Because newspapers are wet waste and cannot go in the blue box
Because newspapers rot quickly and smell bad if stored
Because newspapers must be thrown away with leftover food

why.Because newspapers are wet waste and can: Newspapers are a dry waste, so they would actually belong in the blue box if not given to a recycler.
why.Because newspapers rot quickly and smell: Newspapers do not rot like food peels or leftovers; this confuses dry waste with wet waste.
why.Because newspapers must be thrown away w: Newspapers are useful items that can be recycled, not thrown away with wet leftovers.

activities.explanation: Correct: different recyclers collect different items, so newspapers are kept for the recycler who takes them.

activities.prompt: Explain why we separate waste into dry and wet categories before giving it away.
activities.answer: We separate waste into dry and wet categories so that each kind can be managed in its own proper way. Wet waste like peels and leftovers is different from dry waste like paper. This separation also makes the work of sanitation workers easier and safer, and helps us play a better role in waste management.
points: States that waste is divided into dry and wet categories
Gives examples of each kind, such as peels/leftovers and paper
Links separation to managing waste better
Mentions making sanitation workers' work easier and safer
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Riya's new classroom feels very warm in the afternoon, while the room next door stays cooler. Her school has joined the Jal Shakti Abhiyan, so students are checking every tap. Riya finds a tap in the corridor dripping slowly. Her teacher asks the class to place a glass under it and note the time. The class also plans to ask the headmaster for changes to the building.
activities.prompt: Riya's classroom is warmer than the room next door. Which change to her classroom would most likely help it stay cooler?
options: Painting the classroom roof white and adding windows where the breeze can come in
Painting the classroom roof black and keeping the windows shut
Adding more lights inside the classroom and closing the door
Covering the windows with thick sheets so no air can enter

why.Painting the classroom roof black and ke: A black surface absorbs heat, and shut windows block the breeze, so this would make the room warmer, not cooler.
why.Adding more lights inside the classroom: More lights and a closed door do nothing to cool the room; nothing here reduces the heat.
why.Covering the windows with thick sheets s: Blocking the windows stops the breeze from coming in, so the room would stay warm.

activities.explanation: Correct: a white roof keeps the roof cool, and windows let the breeze in, so the room becomes cooler.

activities.context: Riya's new classroom feels very warm in the afternoon, while the room next door stays cooler. Her school has joined the Jal Shakti Abhiyan, so students are checking every tap. Riya finds a tap in the corridor dripping slowly. Her teacher asks the class to place a glass under it and note the time. The class also plans to ask the headmaster for changes to the building.
activities.prompt: The class places a glass under the dripping tap and measures the time. What will the class most likely discover after watching for a while?
options: The drips stop immediately, so there is no need to report the tap
The water keeps dripping, and the amount collected shows how much is wasted over time
The glass fills up in a few seconds because a leak pours out fast
The glass stays empty because dripping water cannot be collected

why.The drips stop immediately, so there is: A small leak keeps dripping; it does not stop on its own, so it cannot be ignored.
why.The glass fills up in a few seconds beca: A drip is slow, not a fast pour, so the glass will not fill in seconds.
why.The glass stays empty because dripping w: Dripping water can be collected in a glass; that is exactly why the glass is placed there.

activities.explanation: Correct: the drips add up in the glass, and measuring the time shows how much water is wasted.

activities.context: Riya's new classroom feels very warm in the afternoon, while the room next door stays cooler. Her school has joined the Jal Shakti Abhiyan, so students are checking every tap. Riya finds a tap in the corridor dripping slowly. Her teacher asks the class to place a glass under it and note the time. The class also plans to ask the headmaster for changes to the building.
activities.prompt: After finding the leak, what should Riya's class do that best matches what their school can help them learn?
options: Wait for summer so the leak freezes like the ice stupas in Ladakh
Learn to fix the leak and set up a way to collect rainwater for the school
Ask everyone to drink less water so the leak does not matter
Report the leak to another school and let them handle it

why.Wait for summer so the leak freezes like: Ice stupas are a Ladakh idea for gardens; a leaking tap here will not freeze, so waiting is wrong.
why.Ask everyone to drink less water so the: Using water wisely does not mean drinking less; ignoring a leak still wastes water over time.
why.Report the leak to another school and le: The leak is in their own school, so their school is the right place to fix and learn from it.

activities.explanation: Correct: schools can help students learn fixing leaks and collecting rainwater, which fits the Jal Shakti Abhiyan.

activities.prompt: Explain why a classroom with windows where the breeze can come in feels cooler than a closed room, and mention one more change to the building that can help.
activities.answer: Windows let the breeze come into the room, and moving air makes the room feel cooler than a closed room where hot air stays trapped. Another helpful change is painting the roof white, because a white roof stays cool while a black surface absorbs heat and makes the room warmer.
points: Windows allow the breeze to come in
Closed rooms trap warm air
White roof keeps the roof cool
Black surface absorbs heat
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Thomas and Mohit were walking to school. On the way, they saw a big peepal tree full of birds and butterflies, and some people resting in its cool shade. Near the school gate, they watched two vehicles nearly bump into each other because a driver was not following the rules of the road. Thomas said this happens too often. Mohit felt people simply ignore the rules. Their teacher asked the class to help: some students could plan a garden to attract butterflies, and others could make a signboard for the school gate.
activities.prompt: If the big peepal tree near the school were cut down, what would most likely happen to the birds and insects living there?
options: They would lose their home and the food and shade the tree gave them
They would move to the school gate and live near the signboard
They would start following traffic rules like the drivers
They would grow more trees by themselves in the playground

why.They would move to the school gate and l: Wrong: a signboard at a gate is not a home or food for birds and insects
why.They would start following traffic rules: Wrong: traffic rules are for people on the road, not for birds and insects
why.They would grow more trees by themselves: Wrong: trees cannot plant themselves; this does not follow from the case

activities.explanation: Correct: the tree was their home and gave them food and shade, so losing it takes all of that away

activities.context: Thomas and Mohit were walking to school. On the way, they saw a big peepal tree full of birds and butterflies, and some people resting in its cool shade. Near the school gate, they watched two vehicles nearly bump into each other because a driver was not following the rules of the road. Thomas said this happens too often. Mohit felt people simply ignore the rules. Their teacher asked the class to help: some students could plan a garden to attract butterflies, and others could make a signboard for the school gate.
activities.prompt: The class is designing the signboard for the school gate. Which signboard would best do the job?
options: A board with a long poem about trees and butterflies
A board with a short, clear message that drivers, parents and students can understand at once
A board with only colourful pictures of birds and no words at all
A board listing the names of every tree in the school garden

why.A board with a long poem about trees and: Wrong: a poem is not a clear message for people on the road
why.A board with only colourful pictures of: Wrong: pictures alone may not tell drivers what to do clearly
why.A board listing the names of every tree: Wrong: a list of tree names does not give any road message

activities.explanation: Correct: the sign must give a clear message that drivers, parents or students can quickly understand

activities.prompt: How does a tree help the living beings and people around it? Explain using what the students saw under the peepal tree.
activities.answer: The peepal tree was home to many birds and insects, giving them food and shade. It kept the air clean and its cool shade let people rest under it. So a tree gives living beings a home and food, and keeps the surroundings cool and the air clean for everyone.
points: Tree is a home for birds and insects
Gives food and shade to birds and insects
Keeps the air clean and surroundings cool
People can rest in its shade
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Mohit's school arranged a session on fire safety. During the session, the teacher explained that it is important to learn how to stay safe from dangers like fire, because being prepared can help everyone feel safer and more confident. The next day, during a fire drill, Mohit heard the bell and saw smoke coming from the corridor. He remembered what to do and helped his friends follow the right steps.
activities.prompt: Mohit's friend Rina gets frightened and wants to hide inside a cupboard in the classroom. What should Mohit tell her to do instead?
options: Hide quietly until the smoke goes away
Crawl low under the smoke with her mouth covered and move to the nearest exit
Run as fast as she can through the corridor
Wait inside the classroom for the teacher to come

why.Hide quietly until the smoke goes away: Hiding in closets is exactly what she should not do, so this is wrong
why.Run as fast as she can through the corri: Running is dangerous because one should not panic and not run
why.Wait inside the classroom for the teache: Staying in the classroom is like hiding and does not follow the exit route

activities.explanation: This is the correct safe action: crawl low, cover the mouth, use the nearest exit

activities.context: Mohit's school arranged a session on fire safety. During the session, the teacher explained that it is important to learn how to stay safe from dangers like fire, because being prepared can help everyone feel safer and more confident. The next day, during a fire drill, Mohit heard the bell and saw smoke coming from the corridor. He remembered what to do and helped his friends follow the right steps.
activities.prompt: After reaching the assembly point, Mohit notices that his friend Arjun is not with the group. What should Mohit do, and why?
options: Go back inside the building alone to search for Arjun
Stay with his group and alert the staff or teachers immediately
Wait quietly and hope Arjun joins the group soon
Shout loudly and run around looking for Arjun

why.Go back inside the building alone to sea: Going back alone is unsafe and not what a trained student should do
why.Wait quietly and hope Arjun joins the gr: Waiting and hoping wastes time when adults should be told immediately
why.Shout loudly and run around looking for: Running around would cause panic instead of staying calm with the group

activities.explanation: Correct: stay with the group and tell teachers or staff at once so they can help

activities.prompt: How does showing respect and kindness, like waiting for our turn and using kind words, change the way a place feels?
activities.answer: When we wait for our turn and use kind words, we show respect and kindness to others. Our behaviour can make places peaceful and welcoming. When we are kind and polite, everyone feels happy, so the classroom and school become nicer places for all.
points: Gives examples like waiting for turn and kind words
Links behaviour to making places peaceful and welcoming
Says everyone feels happy when people are kind and polite
Connects this to school or classroom life
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Our School — A Happy Place

activities.prompt: Mohit calls school his happy place. Why does he love school?
options: He meets friends, plays games and learns new things
He gets to stay away from his family all day
He does not have to study at home
He can sleep during his classes
activities.explanation: Mohit loves school because he meets friends, plays games and learns new things. That is why he calls it his happy place!

activities.prompt: A green school manages waste, saves water and uses electricity carefully.
activities.explanation: Well done! A green school also plants more trees to make the campus green.

activities.prompt: Match each School Explorer Team with what it checks.
pairs: The school gate at arrival time
activities.explanation: Each team looks closely at one thing in the school. That helps them decide what to do.

activities.prompt: In the Segregation Game, which waste goes into the green box?
options: Wet waste
Dry waste
Items for the recycler
Old newspapers
activities.explanation: The green box is for wet waste and the blue box is for dry waste. Old newspapers can go to a recycler.

activities.prompt: Put these fire drill steps in the right order.
items: Move quickly and calmly to the nearest exit route
Crawl low under smoke with your mouth covered
Go to the assembly point and stay with your group
Alert staff or teachers if anyone is missing
activities.explanation: First leave the building calmly, then gather at the assembly point. Teachers must know at once if anyone is missing.

activities.prompt: Painting a roof black will make the room below cooler.
activities.explanation: A black surface absorbs heat, so it gets hotter. A white roof can make the roof cool.

activities.prompt: In Ladakh, students help make ice ______ that melt slowly in summer to water school gardens.
activities.hint: They are tall ice towers.
activities.explanation: Ice stupas are tall ice towers. They melt slowly in summer and water the school gardens.

activities.prompt: Your class wants to attract more birds and butterflies to school. What could you try to create?
options: A butterfly garden
A car park
A new canteen
A bigger gate
activities.explanation: You can find names of trees and plants that attract birds and butterflies, then create a butterfly garden.

activities.prompt: Match each school problem with what you learned about it.
pairs: Wastes a lot of water over time
activities.explanation: Even a small leak wastes much water over time. Shade from trees and cool roofs can make rooms cooler.

chapters.title: Our Vibrant Country
chapters.summary: In this chapter: a special day in school; republic day and independence day; finding india in currency notes; symbols that speak.

lessons.title: A Special Day in School

activities.prompt: What happens when our flag rises high on Republic Day?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Our Republic Day Celebration
activities.body: It was 26 January, our Republic Day. We came to school early and stood in lines around the flagpole. The folded flag was tied at the top, and flowers decorated the ground. Our head teacher pulled the rope, and the tricolour flag unfurled to the rhythm of drums and claps. Together, we sang the National Anthem with pride and unity.
keyPoints: Republic Day is on 26 January.
The flag was tied folded at the top of the pole.
The head teacher pulled the rope to unfurl the tricolour.
Everyone sang the National Anthem together with pride.
activities.explanation: A special day at school begins with the flag hoisting ceremony.

activities.prompt: On Republic Day, Meena wants to come late and watch the flag from her classroom window. Her teacher says she will miss the best part. Why is Meena wrong?
steps: The folded flag stays tied at the top of the pole.
The flag only unfurls when the head teacher pulls the rope.
This unfurling happens once, with drums and claps, so it is special to watch.
Standing in lines near the flagpole lets everyone see it together, so Meena should come early.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What Our Flag Colours Mean
activities.body: Our tricolour flag has three bands and a wheel. Saffron at the top stands for strength and courage. The white middle band stands for peace and truth. The green band at the bottom stands for growth and prosperity. The blue Ashoka Chakra at the centre represents duty, or dharma.
keyPoints: Saffron means strength and courage.
White means peace and truth.
Green means growth and prosperity.
The blue Ashoka Chakra means duty, or dharma.
activities.explanation: Every colour on our flag teaches us something important.

activities.prompt: Which special day was celebrated at school?
options: 26 January, Republic Day
15 August, Independence Day
2 October, Gandhi Jayanti
1 May, Labour Day
activities.explanation: The lesson says it was 26 January, our Republic Day. Well done!

activities.prompt: Our head teacher pulled the ______ to unfurl the flag.
activities.hint: It is a long cord tied to the flag.
activities.explanation: The head teacher pulled the rope, and the flag rose up the pole.

activities.prompt: The ground around the flagpole was decorated with flowers.
activities.explanation: Yes! Flowers made the ground around the flagpole look bright and lovely.

activities.prompt: What does the saffron colour at the top of our National Flag stand for?
options: Strength and courage
Peace and truth
Growth and prosperity
Duty and dharma
activities.explanation: Saffron at the top stands for strength and courage. Great thinking!

activities.prompt: Match each part of the flag with what it stands for.
activities.explanation: Each colour and the chakra have a special meaning on our flag.

activities.prompt: Put the Republic Day events in the order they happened.
items: We gathered around the flagpole in lines.
The folded flag was tied at the top.
The head teacher pulled the rope.
The tricolour flag unfurled to drums and claps.
We sang the National Anthem together.
activities.explanation: First we gathered, then the flag was tied, the rope was pulled, the flag unfurled, and finally we sang together. Perfect order!

activities.prompt: The flag is folded and tied at the top of the pole. The head teacher pulls the rope. What will happen next?
options: The flag will unfurl with drums and claps.
The flag will stay folded at the top.
The flag will fall down from the pole.
The flag will change its colours slowly.

Thinks the rope does nothing to the flag.
Thinks pulling makes the flag come off the pole.
Thinks the flag changes by itself during hoisting.

activities.explanation: Right: pulling the rope makes the folded flag unfurl.

activities.prompt: On flag day, no one pulls the rope at all. What will the folded flag do?
options: It will stay folded and tied at the top.
It will unfurl slowly all by itself.
It will slide down and touch the ground.
It will fly high without any rope.

Thinks flags open on their own on special days.
Thinks the flag falls when no one pulls the rope.
Thinks flags fly up without anyone doing anything.

activities.explanation: Right: without pulling the rope, the flag cannot unfurl.

activities.prompt: Meera paints the top band of our National Flag blue. Her friend looks at it. What should the friend say?
options: The top is saffron; it means strength and courage.
The top is green; it means growth and prosperity.
The top is white; it means peace and truth.
The top is blue; it means duty, or dharma.

why.The top is green; it means growth and pr: Thinks green is the top band of the flag.
why.The top is white; it means peace and tru: Thinks white is the top band of the flag.
why.The top is blue; it means duty, or dharm: Thinks blue is at the top, not in the centre.

activities.explanation: Right: saffron is at the top and means strength and courage.

activities.prompt: Ravi says the white band and the blue Chakra both stand for peace. Find his mistake.
options: The Chakra means duty; only white means peace.
Both mean duty; neither one means peace at all.
The white band means courage; the Chakra means peace.
The Chakra means growth; the white band means duty.

why.Both mean duty; neither one means peace: Thinks both colours have the same meaning.
why.The white band means courage; the Chakra: Swaps the meanings of white and the Chakra.
why.The Chakra means growth; the white band: Mixes up the meanings of all the flag colours.

activities.explanation: Right: white means peace and the Chakra means duty.

activities.prompt: A farmer looks at the green band at the bottom of our flag and smiles. Why might he smile?
options: Green means growth and prosperity, good for his fields.
Green means peace and truth, good for his family.
Green means strength and courage, good for his work.
Green means duty and dharma, good for his village.

why.Green means peace and truth, good for hi: Thinks green means peace and truth, like white.
why.Green means strength and courage, good f: Thinks green means strength and courage, like saffron.
why.Green means duty and dharma, good for hi: Thinks green means duty, like the blue Chakra.

activities.explanation: Right: green stands for growth and prosperity, like growing crops.

lessons.title: Republic Day and Independence Day

activities.prompt: Why do we celebrate two special days for our country every year?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Two Special Days for India
activities.body: India became independent on 15 August 1947. Many brave people struggled hard to make India free. We remember them every year on Independence Day. On 26 January 1950, India decided to follow the Constitution. The Constitution is our plan and set of rules for the country. We celebrate 26 January as Republic Day with a grand parade in New Delhi.
keyPoints: India became independent on 15 August 1947.
On 26 January 1950, India decided to follow the Constitution.
We celebrate Republic Day every year on 26 January with a parade in New Delhi.
activities.explanation: Two big days, two big reasons: freedom in 1947 and our own rules in 1950.

activities.prompt: Our class plans a picnic with no rules at all. Everyone runs to eat first and nobody shares. Why does the picnic go wrong, and what fixes it?
steps: With no rules, everyone does only what they like, so the picnic becomes confusing.
A country is like the class, because many people must work together every day.
So a country also needs rules, because rules tell everyone how to act fairly.
That is why we made a plan and a set of rules for our country.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: The children watched the Republic Day parade. In which city did they watch it?
options: Mumbai
Chennai
New Delhi
Kolkata
activities.explanation: The Republic Day parade is held in New Delhi.

activities.prompt: India became independent on 15 August 1947.
activities.explanation: Yes! That is the day India became free, and we celebrate it every year.

activities.prompt: On 26 January ______, India decided to follow the Constitution.
activities.hint: Think of the year three years after 1947.
activities.explanation: That was the day we chose to follow our Constitution, so we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what it means.
pairs: We began to follow the Constitution
Our plan and set of rules
City of the Republic Day parade
activities.explanation: Each date and word tells part of the story of our two special days.

activities.prompt: What would happen if a country had no rules at all?
options: It would run faster than ever
It would not run smoothly
It would need more parades
It would win more prizes
activities.explanation: A country needs rules to run smoothly. That is why we made our Constitution.

activities.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened.
items: India became independent on 15 August 1947
India decided to follow the Constitution on 26 January 1950
Every year we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January
activities.explanation: First we became free in 1947, then we began following the Constitution in 1950, and now we celebrate every year.

activities.prompt: A cricket game starts with no rules. Everyone runs their own way. Nobody knows who is out. What will happen to the game?
options: It will become confusing and stop being fun.
It will become more fun with no rules.
The players will score many more runs.
The game will end much faster than before.

Wrong: thinks no rules means more freedom, but it really means confusion.
Wrong: thinks no rules help you win, but nobody can play fairly.
why.The game will end much faster than befor: Wrong: thinks games end faster with no rules, but they just break down.

activities.explanation: Right: without rules, people cannot work together, so things go wrong.

activities.prompt: The Republic Day parade shows soldiers marching. Boats and planes are shown too. Why does the parade show all of them together?
options: Each force protects India in its own different way.
Boats and planes look very pretty in a parade.
Only the Army is strong enough to protect India.
The forces come to the parade to sell tickets.

why.Boats and planes look very pretty in a p: Wrong: thinks the forces are only for show, not for protecting India.
why.Only the Army is strong enough to protec: Wrong: thinks only the Army matters, but the Navy and Airforce help too.
why.The forces come to the parade to sell ti: Wrong: thinks the parade is for money, but it honours the Defence Forces.

activities.explanation: Right: the Army, Navy and Airforce each protect India in their own way.

activities.prompt: India became free on 15 August 1947. Ravi says, 'We celebrate Republic Day because India became free that day.' What is wrong with Ravi's claim?
options: Republic Day is for the Constitution, not freedom day.
Republic Day and Independence Day are the same day.
India became free on 26 January, not August.
We should not celebrate Independence Day at all.

why.Republic Day and Independence Day are th: Wrong: mixes up the two days, because they celebrate different things.
why.India became free on 26 January, not Aug: Wrong: thinks the freedom date is 26 January, but it is 15 August.
why.We should not celebrate Independence Day: Wrong: thinks fixing one day means dropping the other, but both are celebrated.

activities.explanation: Right: Republic Day marks when we began to follow the Constitution.

activities.prompt: Meera watches the parade on TV in January. She sees dances and displays from many states. Why do states bring tableaux to the parade?
options: To show the culture of each different state.
To sell things from their states to people.
To show which state is the biggest one.
Because every state must send a gift.

why.To sell things from their states to peop: Wrong: thinks the parade is a market, but it is a celebration.
Wrong: thinks the parade is a contest about size, not culture.
Wrong: thinks tableaux are presents, but they show state culture.

activities.explanation: Right: tableaux and cultural programmes show each state's culture.

lessons.title: Finding India in Currency Notes

activities.prompt: What secrets about India are hiding inside the money in your pocket?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Note Full of Secrets
activities.body: Your teacher asked you to look at a currency note. Look at it carefully, like a detective! You will find Mahatma Gandhi's image on it. There are actually two images of Gandhi ji on each note. Hold the note up to the light, and a smaller image appears. The tiny round spectacles on the note are a symbol too. Every part of the note has a story to tell.
keyPoints: Mahatma Gandhi's image is on the currency note.
There are two images of Gandhi ji on each note.
Holding the note up to the light shows a smaller image.
activities.explanation: A currency note is like a treasure map. Look closely and you will find its secrets!

activities.prompt: Anu looks at her note. She sees only one picture of Gandhi ji. Her friend says there are two. Who is right, and how can Anu find out?
steps: Anu looked at the note flat on the table, so she saw only the big printed picture.
The second picture is hidden inside the paper, so flat looking cannot show it.
Light can pass through a note, so holding it up to light can show hidden things.
So both are partly right: Anu should hold the note up to light to see the smaller image.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Why the Spectacles Matter
activities.body: Why are Gandhi ji's spectacles on the note? The tiny round spectacles are the symbol of a nationwide mission, the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. Gandhi ji wanted everyone to keep their surroundings clean. In his ashram, people followed strict rules of cleanliness. So every time you see the spectacles, remember his big idea of a clean India.
keyPoints: The tiny round spectacles are the symbol of a nationwide mission.
Gandhi ji wanted everyone to keep their surroundings clean.
People in his ashram followed strict rules of cleanliness.
activities.explanation: The spectacles remind us of Gandhi ji's dream of a clean India.

activities.prompt: Whose image do you see on a currency note?
options: Your teacher
Mahatma Gandhi
A market seller
A cricket player
activities.explanation: Well done! Mahatma Gandhi's image is printed on the currency note.

activities.prompt: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan means ______ India Mission.
activities.hint: Swachh means free from dirt.
activities.explanation: Yes! Swachh Bharat Abhiyan means Clean India Mission.

activities.prompt: There is only one image of Gandhi ji on each note.
activities.explanation: Actually, there are two images of Gandhi ji on each note. Keep looking closely!

activities.prompt: What do you see when you hold the note up to the light?
options: A smaller image of Gandhi ji
A picture of a river
A map of India
A bigger image of Gandhi ji
activities.explanation: Great spotting! The light shows a smaller image of Gandhi ji hiding in the note.

activities.prompt: Match each thing on or about the note with what it does.
pairs: Help for people with visual impairment
activities.explanation: Super memory! Each part of the note helps someone in its own way.

activities.prompt: Put the steps for exploring a note in the right order.
items: Look at the currency note carefully
Find Mahatma Gandhi's image on the note
Hold the note up to the light
Spot the smaller image of Gandhi ji
activities.explanation: Perfect order! First look, then find the image, then use the light to spot the hidden one.

activities.prompt: Meena says, "There is only one Gandhi image on my note, because I can see only one." What is the flaw in her thinking?
options: She did not hold the note up to the light first.
She looked at the note for too long a time.
Her note is new, so it cannot have two images.
She held the note too far away from her eyes.

why.She looked at the note for too long a ti: Wrong: looking longer does not help; the way of looking is the problem.
why.Her note is new, so it cannot have two i: Wrong: every note has two images, new or old.
why.She held the note too far away from her: Wrong: distance does not hide the image; missing light does.

activities.explanation: Right: the smaller image only shows when the note is held up to light.

activities.prompt: Tiny round spectacles are printed on the note. Why did they put this symbol there?
options: It shows that Gandhi ji loved to read small books.
It is the symbol of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan mission.
It marks the place where the note was made by hand.
It reminds us to wear spectacles and check our eyes.

why.It shows that Gandhi ji loved to read sm: Wrong: the spectacles stand for a mission, not for reading books.
why.It marks the place where the note was ma: Wrong: the symbol is not a mark about where notes are made.
why.It reminds us to wear spectacles and che: Wrong: the spectacles are Gandhi ji's, not advice about our eyes.

activities.explanation: Right: the spectacles are the symbol of the Clean India Mission.

activities.prompt: In Gandhi ji's ashram, people followed strict rules of cleanliness. The playground near Riya's house is full of litter. What does Gandhi ji's teaching suggest Riya should do?
options: Wait for someone else to clean it up one day.
Stop going to the playground so she need not see it.
Help keep the playground clean, like the ashram people.
Ask the litter to go away by itself from the ground.

why.Wait for someone else to clean it up one: Wrong: waiting does not follow Gandhi ji's wish for everyone to help.
why.Stop going to the playground so she need: Wrong: running away does not keep surroundings clean.
why.Ask the litter to go away by itself from: Wrong: litter cannot clean itself; people must act.

activities.explanation: Right: Gandhi ji wanted everyone to keep their surroundings clean.

lessons.title: Symbols that Speak

activities.prompt: Why do lions and tigers appear on our country's important things?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Symbols that Speak
activities.body: Some pictures speak for our whole country. The National Emblem shows three lions standing on a circular platform, with the Ashoka Chakra below them. It stands for strength, courage and confidence, and you can see it on your Aadhaar card. Long ago, lions roamed all over India. Today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat. Our national symbols remind us of who we are.
keyPoints: The National Emblem has three lions on a circular platform, with the Ashoka Chakra below.
The Emblem stands for strength, courage and confidence.
Wild lions now live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat.
activities.explanation: National symbols are pictures and creatures that carry the story of our country.

activities.prompt: Aarav looks at his mother's Aadhaar card. He sees three lions on it. He asks, 'Why are lions printed on my mother's card?'
steps: The three lions are the National Emblem of India, so the card shows something that belongs to the whole country.
The Emblem stands for strength, courage and confidence, so it is not just a pretty picture.
National symbols remind us of who we are, so the card carries a message about being Indian.
So the lions are there because the Emblem shows who we are as a country.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where can you see the National Emblem at home?
options: On your Aadhaar card
On your school bag
On a bus ticket
On your pencil box
activities.explanation: Well spotted! The National Emblem is printed on the Aadhaar card.

activities.prompt: The lions on the National Emblem stand for strength, courage and ______.
activities.hint: It means believing in yourself.
activities.explanation: Yes! The Emblem represents strength, courage and confidence.

activities.prompt: Today, where in the wild can you find India's lions?
options: In the deserts of Rajasthan
In the Gir forests of Gujarat
In the hills of Kerala
In the valleys of Sikkim
activities.explanation: Correct! Long ago lions roamed all over India, but today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat.

activities.prompt: Match each symbol with what you know about it.
activities.explanation: Great matching! Each symbol has its own special look and place.

activities.prompt: Put the story of India's lions in order, from long ago to today.
items: Lions roamed freely over vast areas of India
Their numbers fell to only a few dozen about 150 years ago
Our country made great efforts to save the lions
Today India has several hundred lions in the wild
activities.explanation: Perfect order! From roaming everywhere, to nearly lost, to saved by great efforts.

activities.prompt: Why can we say India worked hard to save its lions?
options: Because lions moved to new forests on their own
Because lions grew from a few dozen to several hundred
Because lions were brought from another country
Because lions now live in every state of India
activities.explanation: Yes! From only a few dozen about 150 years ago, great efforts brought the numbers up to several hundred in the wild.

activities.prompt: Riya looks at her mother's Aadhaar card. She sees three lions on it. Why are the lions printed there?
options: They make the card look pretty.
They show lions live near Riya's house.
They are the National Emblem, which reminds us who we are.
They show the card is a toy.

The Emblem is not decoration; it has a meaning.
The Emblem is on the card for everyone, not for one place.
An Aadhaar card is a real paper, not a toy.

activities.explanation: Right. The Emblem on the card reminds us of who we are.

activities.prompt: About 150 years ago, only a few dozen lions were left. Today there are several hundred. What most likely changed?
options: Lions came from another country.
Our country made great efforts to save the lions.
People stopped caring about the lions.
The lions stopped having babies.

The lions were already in India; they did not come from outside.
If people stopped caring, the numbers would go down, not up.
If lions stopped having babies, the numbers would fall.

activities.explanation: Right. Great efforts to save the lions made their numbers grow.

activities.prompt: Dev says, 'Lions were always only in the Gir forests.' His book says lions roamed vast areas long ago. What is the flaw in Dev's claim?
options: Dev is right; lions never lived anywhere else.
Lions used to roam many places, not only Gir.
Lions came to Gir by aeroplane.
The Gir forests are very new.

why.Dev is right; lions never lived anywhere: This forgets that lions once roamed vast areas of India.
Lions did not travel by aeroplane; they already lived in India.
The forests are not new; the lions' home area shrank over time.

activities.explanation: Right. Long ago lions roamed freely over vast areas of India.

activities.prompt: Meera says, 'The peacock is our national animal because it has bright green and blue feathers.' What is wrong with her claim?
options: Peacock feathers are really grey.
Peacocks cannot be called animals at all.
The national animal wears orange with black stripes.
Peacocks are too small to be national animals.

The colours are not the problem; the animal is.
why.Peacocks cannot be called animals at all: The problem is not the word 'animal'; it is which animal.
why.Peacocks are too small to be national an: Size does not decide a national animal.

activities.explanation: Right. The national animal wears orange with black stripes, so it is not the peacock.

activities.prompt: A teacher asks, 'Why does our Emblem use lions and not rabbits?' What is the best reason?
options: Lions are louder than rabbits.
Lions show strength, courage and confidence.
Rabbits are faster than lions.
Lions live in zoos, rabbits do not.

Being loud is not what the Emblem is about.
Speed is not the message the Emblem carries.
Where animals live is not why they were chosen.

activities.explanation: Right. The Emblem stands for strength, courage and confidence.

lessons.title: Our Vibrant Culture and Diversity Everywhere

activities.prompt: Why do people in different places speak, dress, and eat so differently?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: So Many Languages, So Many Ways of Life
activities.body: India is full of variety. People speak more than a thousand languages across our country. Each language has its own history, songs and stories. People also eat food, wear clothes, and enjoy songs and dances special to their area. All this variety is called diversity. Diversity makes our country stronger and more self-sufficient.
keyPoints: More than a thousand languages are spoken in India.
Each language has its own history, songs and stories.
Food, clothes, songs and dances differ from area to area.
Diversity makes our country stronger and more self-sufficient.
activities.explanation: Our many languages and ways of life are a treasure that makes India strong.

activities.prompt: At a big fair, Aditi hears many languages, sees different clothes and headgear, and smells many foods. She asks, 'Why do people here look and speak so differently?'
steps: People in India speak more than a thousand languages, so Aditi hears many tongues at the fair.
Each language carries its own songs and stories, so every stall sounds different and special.
People eat food, wear clothes and enjoy dances of their area, so the fair looks colourful and varied.
Like a forest full of many plants and animals, this variety makes our country stronger, so Aditi sees a good thing.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: What Headgear Can Tell Us
activities.body: Have you noticed the different caps and turbans people wear? Headgear can tell us where someone is from. That is not its only job. Headgear is also worn for protection from heat or cold. And when you ride on a two wheeler, a helmet is compulsory. It must be worn to keep your head safe.
keyPoints: Headgear can tell us where someone is from.
Headgear protects us from heat or cold.
Helmets are compulsory on two wheelers.
activities.explanation: A cap or turban shows where a person is from and keeps them safe too.

activities.prompt: About how many languages are spoken across our country?
options: Only a few
Only the ones in your town
More than a thousand
activities.explanation: Well done! More than a thousand languages are spoken across India.

activities.prompt: Each language has its own history, songs and stories.
activities.explanation: Yes! Every language is rich with its own history, songs and stories.

activities.prompt: In Himachal Pradesh, people wear a ______ on their head.
activities.hint: It is a kind of cap.
activities.explanation: In Himachal Pradesh, people wear a topi.

activities.prompt: Match each place or thing with what people wear there.
activities.explanation: Different places have different headgear, and helmets keep riders safe.

activities.prompt: You meet someone who speaks a language you do not know. How can a mobile application help you?
options: It can translate one language to another
It can teach you to sing songs
It can tell you what food to eat
activities.explanation: Great thinking! Some apps can translate one language to another, so you can talk to more people.

activities.prompt: A man at the bus stop wears a colourful saafa on his head. Where may this man come from?
options: A place where men wear a saafa.
A place where people wear a topi.
A place where people wear helmets.
A place where people speak one language.

This mixes up the headgear. A topi is worn in Himachal Pradesh, not a saafa.
This confuses a helmet with a saafa. Helmets are for safety on two wheelers, not a place marker.
This thinks language decides headgear. The saafa shows the place, not the language spoken.

activities.explanation: Right. A colourful saafa is worn by men in Rajasthan, and headgear tells us where someone is from.

activities.prompt: Forest A has many kinds of trees, birds and insects. Forest B has only one kind of tree. A disease kills that one kind of tree. What may happen?
options: Forest B may lose all of its trees.
Forest A may lose all of its trees.
Both forests will lose every single tree.
Both forests will grow many new kinds fast.

This forgets how variety helps. Forest A has many kinds, so the disease kills only one kind there.
why.Both forests will lose every single tree: This thinks variety does not matter. Forest A's many kinds keep it safe from total loss.
why.Both forests will grow many new kinds fa: This thinks new kinds appear quickly. Variety already present is what protects a forest.

activities.explanation: Right. Forest B has only one kind, so the disease can kill every tree in it.

activities.prompt: Rohan says, 'Only one language is spoken in our whole country.' He asked only his five neighbours. What is wrong with his claim?
options: He asked too few people in one small place.
He asked his neighbours at the wrong time.
He should have asked only the grown-ups there.
He should have asked people wearing a topi.

why.He asked his neighbours at the wrong tim: This blames the time of day. The real flaw is the very small group he asked.
why.He should have asked only the grown-ups: This thinks grown-ups know all languages. Age does not fix the flaw of asking too few people.
why.He should have asked people wearing a to: This connects unrelated facts. A topi shows a place, not how many languages exist.

activities.explanation: Right. More than a thousand languages are spoken, so five neighbours cannot show the whole country.

activities.prompt: People in different areas eat different foods and wear different clothes. Each area has its own special things. Why does this make our country stronger?
options: The country can get many things from within itself.
The country must buy everything from far outside.
Everyone will slowly start wearing the same clothes.
Everyone will slowly start speaking the same language.

why.The country must buy everything from far: This is the opposite of the truth. Having many special things inside reduces the need from outside.
why.Everyone will slowly start wearing the s: This thinks diversity will end. The special clothes of each area are what make the country strong.
why.Everyone will slowly start speaking the: This thinks one language is the goal. Diversity itself, not sameness, makes the country strong.

activities.explanation: Right. Many areas with special foods and clothes make the country more self-sufficient and strong.

lessons.title: Indian Drums and Spirit of Togetherness

activities.prompt: How can a simple drum bring so many different people together?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: One Country, Many Rhythms
activities.body: Music and dance help us celebrate, pray, share stories and bring people together. A simple drum looks and sounds different in different parts of India. Each drum has its own rhythm and sound. India is a shining example of the spirit of togetherness. We speak many languages, follow many religions and wear many kinds of clothing. Yet we live together, helping and supporting each other, like threads woven into one strong fabric.
keyPoints: Music and dance bring people together.
Drums look and sound different in different parts of India.
Our many differences are woven together like one fabric.
activities.explanation: Our many differences make one beautiful, strong India.

activities.prompt: A new family moves next door. They speak a different language and wear different clothes. A festival comes. The new child stands alone watching the drum and dance. What should happen, and why?
steps: The new family looks different and speaks differently, because India has a rich variety of languages, clothing and traditions.
Music and dance bring people together, so the drum and dance are a chance to welcome them.
If we help and support the new child, we live the spirit of togetherness, because togetherness means caring for each other.
So the class should invite the new child to dance, because different threads woven together make one strong, vibrant fabric.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why do people play music and dance in India?
options: To celebrate and bring people together
To make the rain go away
To win a prize every time
activities.explanation: Music and dance help us celebrate, pray and share stories together.

activities.prompt: Which instrument is used in Carnatic music?
options: Sitar
Mridangam
Shehnai
activities.explanation: The mridangam is used in Carnatic music. The sitar and shehnai belong to Hindustani music.

activities.prompt: Different dance forms have originated from different ______ of India.
activities.hint: Think of the parts that make up our country.
activities.explanation: Each state has given India its own special dance form.

activities.prompt: What is adding new colours to old norms in India today?
options: Modern changes
Stopping all festivals
Forgetting our languages
activities.explanation: Modern changes add new colours to old norms, like scientists launching rockets and farmers using technology.

activities.prompt: Put these ideas in order to build the picture of togetherness, from first to last.
items: We have many languages, religions and traditions
We live together, helping each other
All the threads are woven into one strong fabric
India shines as an example of togetherness
activities.explanation: First come our many differences, then we help each other, they weave into one fabric, and India shines.

activities.prompt: Meera's drum comes from the south of India. Ravi's drum comes from the east. The two drums look different. They play them together at school. What will they hear?
options: One sound, because all drums are really the same
Two different rhythms and two different sounds
No sound, because drums only look different
One rhythm, because playing together changes the drums

why.One sound, because all drums are really: This thinks all drums are identical, but drums differ across the country.
why.No sound, because drums only look differ: This confuses how a drum looks with how a drum sounds.
why.One rhythm, because playing together cha: This thinks playing together erases differences, but each drum keeps its own sound.

activities.explanation: Right: each drum has its own rhythm and sound, and drums differ in different parts.

activities.prompt: It is festival time in a village. People beat a big drum. People dance together in a circle. Why do they do this?
options: To celebrate and to bring all the people together
To make the drum rest after a long day
To win a prize for the loudest drum beat
To stop people from talking to each other

why.To make the drum rest after a long day: This misses the purpose of music and thinks drums exist for resting.
why.To win a prize for the loudest drum beat: This thinks festivals are contests, but music and dance are for sharing and joining in.
why.To stop people from talking to each othe: This gets the purpose backwards; music and dance unite people, not separate them.

activities.explanation: Right: music and dance are ways of celebrating and bringing people together.

activities.prompt: Anil says every drum in India sounds the same. He wants to check his idea in a fair way. What should he do?
options: Listen to drums from many different parts of the country
Listen to one drum from his street many times
Ask his best friend whether his idea is right
Read one book that describes only one drum

why.Listen to one drum from his street many: This tests only one drum, so it cannot show what drums are like everywhere.
why.Ask his best friend whether his idea is: Asking a friend gives an opinion, not a fair test with real sounds.
why.Read one book that describes only one dr: One book about one drum cannot show drums from all parts of the country.

activities.explanation: Right: a fair test must compare drums from different parts, since drums differ across the country.

activities.prompt: Dev says, 'We speak many languages in India. So people here cannot live together.' What is wrong with Dev's claim?
options: Languages make people too tired to live together
Many languages mean everyone really speaks the same words
Different languages can still be woven into one strong fabric
Only one language can ever be spoken in a country

why.Languages make people too tired to live: This invents a tiredness problem; languages do not stop people from living together.
why.Many languages mean everyone really spea: This says languages are not really different, but we truly have a rich variety of languages.
why.Only one language can ever be spoken in: This says variety is impossible, but India has many languages, religions and traditions.

activities.explanation: Right: different threads like languages are woven together into one strong, vibrant fabric.

activities.prompt: A farmer uses new technology to grow better crops. At harvest time, he still plays the old drum and dances the old dance. What will happen?
options: He will forget the old dance because of technology
New ways and old traditions will both shine together
The drum sound will stop his crops from growing
He must pick between technology and the old dance

why.He will forget the old dance because of: This thinks new things erase old ones, but modern changes only add new colours to old norms.
why.The drum sound will stop his crops from: This thinks old traditions harm farming, but nothing in the situation says so.
why.He must pick between technology and the: This thinks a choice is forced, but old and new can go together.

activities.explanation: Right: modern changes add new colours to old norms, so both can live together.
