activities.context: On 26 January, Republic Day, Riya's class reached school before sunrise. Everyone stood in neat lines around the flagpole, which was surrounded by a ring of flowers. The folded flag waited at the top of the rope. The head teacher pulled the rope, drums began to beat, and the tricolour spread out in the morning breeze as everyone clapped.
activities.prompt: Just before the head teacher pulls the rope, a strong wind suddenly stops blowing. What will most likely happen when she pulls it anyway?
options: The flag will still come loose from its folded position and hang down from the top of the pole
The rope will break and the flag will stay tied at the top
The flowers around the flagpole will be blown away
The flag will rise but stay folded like a tight roll all day

why.The rope will break and the flag will st: Wrong: nothing in hoisting makes the rope snap; the rope is pulled gently by hand
why.The flowers around the flagpole will be: Wrong: flowers are decorations on the ground and are not affected by pulling the rope
why.The flag will rise but stay folded like: Wrong: pulling the rope is exactly what opens the fold; the flag cannot stay folded after being pulled

activities.explanation: Correct: pulling the rope unties the folded flag; without wind it unfurls only partly and hangs down, which is what really happens

activities.context: On 26 January, Republic Day, Riya's class reached school before sunrise. Everyone stood in neat lines around the flagpole, which was surrounded by a ring of flowers. The folded flag waited at the top of the rope. The head teacher pulled the rope, drums began to beat, and the tricolour spread out in the morning breeze as everyone clapped.
activities.prompt: During the ceremony, the drums stop for a moment and some students begin talking. What should the class monitor do so the moment keeps its meaning?
options: Quietly signal everyone to stand still and join the singing with pride and unity
Ask everyone to sit down until the drums start again
Tell students to run closer to the flagpole to see the colours better
Start picking up the flowers around the flagpole to keep students busy

why.Ask everyone to sit down until the drums: Wrong: sitting down during the anthem breaks the respect of the moment, not saves it
why.Tell students to run closer to the flagp: Wrong: moving out of line spoils the discipline of the lines formed around the flagpole
why.Start picking up the flowers around the: Wrong: tidying flowers is not the purpose of the ceremony and distracts from the anthem

activities.explanation: Correct: the anthem is sung together with pride and unity, so the monitor should restore silence and full participation

activities.prompt: What is the difference between what the saffron band and the green band of our National Flag stand for?
activities.answer: The saffron band is at the top and stands for strength and courage, qualities we need to face difficulties bravely. The green band is at the bottom and stands for growth and prosperity, which mean progress and well-being for the country. So one inspires bravery while the other hopes for a flourishing nation.
points: Saffron is at the top and stands for strength and courage
Green is at the bottom and stands for growth and prosperity
Brings out the contrast: bravery versus progress and well-being
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Riya's family visited New Delhi and watched the Republic Day parade. They saw colourful state tableaux, cultural programmes, and the Indian Defence Forces marching. Riya's grandfather told her that long ago, many brave people struggled hard to make India free, and later the country made a plan and a set of rules so it could run smoothly. Riya wondered why the parade is held every year.
activities.prompt: If Riya visits New Delhi again next year on the same national day, what will she most likely see?
options: The same parade with tableaux, cultural programmes and the Defence Forces
A parade only by the postal workers of India
A parade celebrating the day India became free in 1947
No parade, because it is held only once every few years

why.A parade only by the postal workers of I: Wrong: the postal network is large, but postal workers do not feature in this parade.
why.A parade celebrating the day India becam: Wrong: the freedom day is a different celebration in August, not this parade in January.
why.No parade, because it is held only once: Wrong: the celebration happens every year, not once in a while.

activities.explanation: Correct: Republic Day is celebrated every year, so the parade with tableaux, cultural programmes and the Defence Forces would be held again.

activities.context: Riya's family visited New Delhi and watched the Republic Day parade. They saw colourful state tableaux, cultural programmes, and the Indian Defence Forces marching. Riya's grandfather told her that long ago, many brave people struggled hard to make India free, and later the country made a plan and a set of rules so it could run smoothly. Riya wondered why the parade is held every year.
activities.prompt: Riya's grandfather says people struggled hard in the past. What should Riya do to honour what they did?
options: Remember their contributions and celebrate the country's freedom
Write new rules to replace the old set of rules
Ask the Army, Navy and Airforce to stop marching
Watch the parade only if the state tableaux are colourful

why.Write new rules to replace the old set o: Wrong: the plan and rules were already decided upon; replacing them is not how we honour the freedom fighters.
why.Ask the Army, Navy and Airforce to stop: Wrong: the Defence Forces are part of the parade; stopping them would not honour anyone.
why.Watch the parade only if the state table: Wrong: enjoying the parade is fine, but colourfulness is not the way to honour the brave people.

activities.explanation: Correct: we remember the contributions of the brave people and celebrate our freedom every year.

activities.prompt: Explain why 26 January is celebrated every year in India.
activities.answer: On 26 January 1950, India decided to follow the Constitution, which is the plan and set of rules the country made so it could run smoothly. To remember this important decision, we celebrate 26 January as Republic Day every year, with a parade in New Delhi.
points: Mentions 26 January 1950 and the decision to follow the Constitution
Links the Constitution to the plan and set of rules for running the country smoothly
States that the day is celebrated every year as Republic Day
May mention the parade in New Delhi
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.prompt: Explain why the tiny round spectacles are printed on the currency note.
activities.answer: The tiny round spectacles are the symbol of a nationwide mission called Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, which means Clean India Mission. Gandhi ji wanted everyone to keep their surroundings clean, and people in his ashram followed strict rules of cleanliness. The symbol on the note reminds us of his message.
points: Spectacles are the symbol of a nationwide mission
Names Swachh Bharat Abhiyan / Clean India Mission
Gandhi ji wanted everyone to keep surroundings clean
Mentions cleanliness rules followed in his ashram
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera's aunt shows her a new Aadhaar card. Meera spots three lions standing on a circular platform and, below them, a wheel. Her aunt says the card carries the National Emblem of India. Meera remembers that long ago lions roamed over vast areas of India, but today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat. She wonders why the country chose this animal for such an important symbol.
activities.prompt: Why do you think the National Emblem shows lions standing proudly instead of hiding or running?
options: Because the emblem should show strength, courage and confidence, and standing lions look like that
Because lions are the fastest animals in the Gir forests
Because lions on a platform show that they are tired and resting
Because the emblem is meant to scare people who see the card

why.Because lions are the fastest animals in: Speed is not a quality linked to the emblem in the lesson.
why.Because lions on a platform show that th: Resting or tired lions would not suggest the qualities the emblem carries.
why.Because the emblem is meant to scare peo: The emblem represents the country's qualities, not fear.

activities.explanation: Correct: standing lions match the qualities the emblem stands for.

activities.context: Meera's aunt shows her a new Aadhaar card. Meera spots three lions standing on a circular platform and, below them, a wheel. Her aunt says the card carries the National Emblem of India. Meera remembers that long ago lions roamed over vast areas of India, but today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat. She wonders why the country chose this animal for such an important symbol.
activities.prompt: About 150 years ago, lions had gone down to only a few dozen. If our country had NOT made great efforts to save them, what would most likely have happened?
options: The lions would have spread to new forests across India
The lions would have moved to the Gir forests on their own
The lions would have disappeared from the wild completely
The lions would have grown to several hundred by themselves

why.The lions would have spread to new fores: With only a few dozen left, spreading to new places would not happen without help.
why.The lions would have moved to the Gir fo: They were already in the Gir forests; moving there again does not solve the danger.
why.The lions would have grown to several hu: Numbers recover only because of effort and protection, not on their own.

activities.explanation: Correct: with so few left and no protection, they would have died out in the wild.

activities.context: Meera's aunt shows her a new Aadhaar card. Meera spots three lions standing on a circular platform and, below them, a wheel. Her aunt says the card carries the National Emblem of India. Meera remembers that long ago lions roamed over vast areas of India, but today they live only in the Gir forests of Gujarat. She wonders why the country chose this animal for such an important symbol.
activities.prompt: Meera draws a bird with orange feathers and black stripes and says she has drawn our national bird. What should her aunt tell her?
options: That the national bird has bright green and blue feathers, so her colours are wrong
That her drawing is perfect because the national bird is orange and black
That she should add three lions to the drawing to make it correct
That she should draw the Ashoka Chakra on the bird's wing

why.That her drawing is perfect because the: Orange with black stripes belongs to the national animal, not the bird.
why.That she should add three lions to the d: Lions belong on the National Emblem, not on a drawing of the national bird.
why.That she should draw the Ashoka Chakra o: The Ashoka Chakra is part of the National Emblem, not the national bird.

activities.explanation: Correct: the national bird's colours are bright green and blue, not orange and black.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between what the National Emblem shows and what the national animal and national bird look like?
activities.answer: The National Emblem shows three lions standing on a circular platform, with the Ashoka Chakra below them, and it stands for strength, courage and confidence. The national animal wears orange with black stripes, while the national bird has bright green and blue feathers. All of them remind us of who we are.
points: Describes the emblem: three lions on a circular platform with the Ashoka Chakra below
Gives the qualities the emblem represents: strength, courage and confidence
Says the national animal wears orange with black stripes
Says the national bird has bright green and blue feathers
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: During a school exchange week, students from different states visit Meera's class in Delhi. One boy from Rajasthan wears a colourful saafa, a girl from Himachal Pradesh wears a topi, and a new friend speaks a language Meera has never heard. Meera's teacher opens a mobile application on her tablet that converts the friend's words into a language the whole class understands, and soon everyone is sharing songs and stories from home.
activities.prompt: The new friend speaks a language Meera has never heard. What is the most likely reason so many languages like this exist across the country?
options: Every area has its own language, each with a long history, songs and stories
Languages were invented only a few years ago for school exchanges
All Indians are required to learn exactly one thousand languages
Languages spread only through mobile applications

why.Languages were invented only a few years: Wrong: languages developed over a long time, not recently for exchanges.
why.All Indians are required to learn exactl: Wrong: no rule fixes the number of languages a person must learn.
why.Languages spread only through mobile app: Wrong: applications only help translate; they did not create the languages.

activities.explanation: Correct: different areas have their own languages, each rich with its own history, songs and stories.

activities.context: During a school exchange week, students from different states visit Meera's class in Delhi. One boy from Rajasthan wears a colourful saafa, a girl from Himachal Pradesh wears a topi, and a new friend speaks a language Meera has never heard. Meera's teacher opens a mobile application on her tablet that converts the friend's words into a language the whole class understands, and soon everyone is sharing songs and stories from home.
activities.prompt: If the boy from Rajasthan stopped wearing his saafa and the girl from Himachal Pradesh stopped wearing her topi, what would become hardest for the visiting students?
options: Telling which state each visitor comes from by looking at their headgear
Eating the food special to their own areas
Using the translation application on the tablet
Riding two wheelers safely during the trip

why.Eating the food special to their own are: Wrong: food habits do not depend on the headgear they wear.
why.Using the translation application on the: Wrong: the application works on the tablet, not on anyone's headgear.
why.Riding two wheelers safely during the tr: Wrong: helmets on two wheelers are a separate rule and not linked to the saafa or topi.

activities.explanation: Correct: headgear can tell us where someone is from, so without it this clue is lost.

activities.context: During a school exchange week, students from different states visit Meera's class in Delhi. One boy from Rajasthan wears a colourful saafa, a girl from Himachal Pradesh wears a topi, and a new friend speaks a language Meera has never heard. Meera's teacher opens a mobile application on her tablet that converts the friend's words into a language the whole class understands, and soon everyone is sharing songs and stories from home.
activities.prompt: On the last day, the class plans a cultural programme. What should Meera suggest so the programme truly shows the strength of their diverse country?
options: Invite every visiting student to present a song, dance or story special to their own area
Ask everyone to perform only the same item so nothing looks different
Cancel the programme because different languages cannot be enjoyed together
Allow only students whose headgear looks colourful to perform

why.Ask everyone to perform only the same it: Wrong: making everything the same hides the very diversity being celebrated.
why.Cancel the programme because different l: Wrong: the translation application shows different languages need not divide people.
why.Allow only students whose headgear looks: Wrong: choosing performers by headgear is unfair and misses the point of diversity.

activities.explanation: Correct: sharing each area's special songs, dances and stories celebrates diversity, which makes the country stronger.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between headgear worn to show where someone is from and headgear worn for protection? Give one example of each kind from daily life.
activities.answer: Some headgear tells us where a person is from, like the colourful saafa or pagri worn by men in Rajasthan or the topi worn in Himachal Pradesh. Other headgear protects the body, like a helmet, which is compulsory and must be worn on two wheelers to keep the rider safe.
points: Says one kind of headgear shows where a person is from
Gives saafa or pagri (Rajasthan) or topi (Himachal Pradesh) as the example
Says the other kind protects from heat, cold or injury
Gives the helmet worn on two wheelers as the example
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera's school is holding a Unity Day function. Her group plans a Carnatic music item with the mridangam, a Hindustani item with the sitar and shehnai, dances from different states, and a display of the many languages, religions, clothing and traditions of India. Her friend Arjun says all this variety will look like a jumble. Meera is sure it will not.
activities.prompt: Why is Meera sure the programme will not look like a jumble?
options: Because the different items, like different threads, join to make one strong and lively whole
Because only the music items will be watched by the audience
Because every item will be performed in the same language
Because the dances from different states will be cancelled

why.Because only the music items will be wat: Wrong: the passage never says the audience watches only music.
why.Because every item will be performed in: Wrong: India has many languages, so items need not be in one language.
why.Because the dances from different states: Wrong: the dances are part of the plan, not cancelled.

activities.explanation: Correct: different threads coming together is how variety makes one strong whole.

activities.context: Meera's school is holding a Unity Day function. Her group plans a Carnatic music item with the mridangam, a Hindustani item with the sitar and shehnai, dances from different states, and a display of the many languages, religions, clothing and traditions of India. Her friend Arjun says all this variety will look like a jumble. Meera is sure it will not.
activities.prompt: What would most likely happen if the group swapped the mridangam for a drum from another part of the country?
options: The item would sound exactly the same, since all drums are alike
The rhythm and sound of the item would change, since every drum has its own
The drum would refuse to be played outside its home state
The audience would hear nothing at all from the drum

why.The item would sound exactly the same, s: Wrong: drums look and sound different in various parts of the country.
why.The drum would refuse to be played outsi: Wrong: a drum does not stop working in a new place.
why.The audience would hear nothing at all f: Wrong: the drum would still make sound, just a different one.

activities.explanation: Correct: each drum has its own rhythm and sound, so the item would change.

activities.prompt: Explain why India is called a shining example of the spirit of togetherness.
activities.answer: India has a rich variety of languages, religions, clothing and traditions, and a rich history, culture and practices. Yet we live together, helping and supporting each other. All these different threads are woven into one strong, vibrant fabric, so India shows the spirit of togetherness.
points: Mentions the rich variety of languages, religions, clothing and traditions
Says we live together, helping and supporting each other
Uses the idea of different threads woven into one strong fabric
Links this variety-with-unity to the spirit of togetherness
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Our Vibrant Country

activities.prompt: Why do we celebrate Republic Day on 26 January every year?
options: Because India became independent on that day
Because we started following the Constitution on that day in 1950
Because the National Flag was first made on that day
Because schools close for winter on that day
activities.explanation: On 26 January 1950, we decided to follow the Constitution. That is why we celebrate Republic Day each year.

activities.prompt: The white band of our National Flag stands for growth and prosperity.
activities.explanation: White stands for peace and truth. Growth and prosperity are shown by the green band at the bottom.

activities.prompt: The blue Ashoka Chakra at the centre of our flag represents duty, or ______.
activities.hint: It is an old word for doing what is right.
activities.explanation: The blue Chakra in the middle of the flag stands for duty, or dharma.

activities.prompt: Match each part of our National Flag with what it stands for.
activities.explanation: Each colour and the Chakra carry a special meaning on our tricolour.

activities.prompt: Put the flag hoisting events in the order they happened on Republic Day.
items: Everyone gathered in lines around the flagpole
The folded flag was tied at the top
The head teacher pulled the rope
The tricolour unfurled to the rhythm of drums
Everyone sang the National Anthem together
activities.explanation: First we gathered, then the flag was tied, the rope was pulled, the flag unfurled, and finally we sang together.

activities.prompt: You hold a currency note up to the light. What surprise can you see?
options: A smaller image of Gandhi ji appears
The note changes its colour
The spectacles on the note disappear
The raised prints become flat
activities.explanation: There are two images of Gandhi ji on each note. Holding it up to the light shows the smaller one.

activities.prompt: Today, Asiatic lions roam freely over vast areas of India.
activities.explanation: Long ago, lions roamed vast areas. Today they are found only in the Gir forests of Gujarat.

activities.prompt: The ______ app helps people identify different currency notes.
activities.hint: It is a four-letter name written in capital letters.
activities.explanation: The MANI app helps people, including those with visual impairment, identify different notes.

activities.prompt: Match each item with the place or music it belongs to.
activities.explanation: Headgear can tell us where someone is from, and each musical tradition has its own instruments.

activities.prompt: Why does diversity make our country stronger?
options: Because everyone in India speaks the same language
Because it makes us more self-sufficient
Because it means we never need rules
Because it stops modern changes from happening
activities.explanation: Our many languages, foods, clothes and traditions make India stronger and more self-sufficient. Different threads are woven into one vibrant fabric.

chapters.title: Some Unique Places
chapters.summary: In this chapter: a trip to the southernmost tip and the islands; island forests and safety at sea; marine life and north sentinel island; sundarbans: home of the mangroves.

lessons.title: A Trip to the Southernmost Tip and the Islands

activities.prompt: What would it feel like to stand at the very bottom tip of India?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.prompt: Shanti wants to see more of her country. Her parents are busy planning the summer vacation. Where should the trip begin so her wish comes true?
steps: Shanti wants to see more of her country, so the trip must show her new and special places.
Her parents are busy planning, so they must pick places that fit into one long trip.
The southernmost tip of India, Indira Point, is a special place at the very bottom of the map, so it is a good starting point.
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a long chain of islands near it, so the family can see many islands in one trip.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Ravi draws four pictures of land. His teacher asks for an island. Water must go all around it. Which picture is right?
options: Land with water on all four sides
Land with a river flowing through it
Land with a lake on one side only
Land joined to the big land by sand

why.Land with a river flowing through it: Wrong: he thinks any water near land makes an island, but a river does not go all around.
why.Land with a lake on one side only: Wrong: he thinks one side of water is enough, but an island needs water on every side.
why.Land joined to the big land by sand: Wrong: he thinks joined land can be an island, but joined land is not surrounded on all sides.

activities.explanation: Right: an island is land with water around it on all sides.

activities.prompt: Shanti looks down from a plane over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. What will she most likely see below?
options: Many islands in a long line
One very big island only
Dry land with no sea around
Islands spread in a big circle

why.One very big island only: Wrong: she thinks one island means the whole place, but a chain has many islands.
why.Dry land with no sea around: Wrong: she forgets islands are surrounded by sea on all sides.
why.Islands spread in a big circle: Wrong: she mixes up a chain with a circle; a chain is long, not round.

activities.explanation: Right: the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a long chain, so they look like a line.

activities.prompt: Shanti's trip starts at the southernmost tip of India. She opens a map of India. Where should she put her finger first?
options: At the very bottom of the map
At the very top of the map
On the left side of the map
Right in the middle of the map

why.At the very top of the map: Wrong: she mixes up south with north, which is at the top.
why.On the left side of the map: Wrong: she mixes up south with west, which is on the left.
why.Right in the middle of the map: Wrong: she thinks the middle is the tip, but a tip is at the edge.

activities.explanation: Right: southernmost means the farthest south, and south is at the bottom of a map.

activities.prompt: Arun says most of the world's wild tigers live outside India. Meera knows the facts. Why is Arun wrong?
options: India has most of the world's wild tigers
Tigers live only outside India
No one knows where tigers live
Tigers live equally in every country

why.Tigers live only outside India: Wrong: he flips it around; most tigers live inside India, not outside.
why.No one knows where tigers live: Wrong: he thinks we cannot know, but the tiger numbers are known.
why.Tigers live equally in every country: Wrong: he thinks tigers are spread evenly, but India has a very big share.

activities.explanation: Right: India has around 75 per cent of the world's wild tigers, so most live in India.

activities.prompt: Rina says Shanti's island trip started from a small village, not a big city. Shanti knows the facts. What is Rina's mistake?
options: The trip started from a capital city
Villages can never start any trips
The trip started in another country
Big cities cannot be trip starting points

why.Villages can never start any trips: Wrong: she blames villages, but the real reason is the trip began in a capital city.
why.The trip started in another country: Wrong: she thinks the trip went abroad, but it started inside the islands of India.
why.Big cities cannot be trip starting point: Wrong: she mixes up cities and villages; a capital city can start a trip.

activities.explanation: Right: the trip started from Sri Vijaya Puram, the capital city of the islands.

lessons.sceneCaption: Indira Point in the Andaman Islands is the southernmost tip of India.

lessons.title: Island Forests and Safety at Sea

activities.prompt: Why do some trees wear wide root 'skirts' to stand tall?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.prompt: Shanti saw a very big tree on the island. Its roots spread out wide, like a flat mat on the ground. She was curious and asked why the roots grow like that.
steps: The tree is very big and heavy, so it needs strong support.
The ground on the island can be soft, so a thin base may not hold it.
Wide roots hold the ground over a big area, so they support the tree.
So the roots spread out wide to keep the big tree standing safely.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: You must wear a life jacket on the ferry, even if you can swim.
activities.explanation: Yes! Everyone wears one, because it keeps you afloat if you fall into water.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what it does or means.
activities.explanation: Super matching! Each pair shows something useful from the lesson.

activities.prompt: Riya says life jackets are only for people who cannot swim. Her brother swims very well. He still wears one on the ferry. What is wrong with Riya's claim?
options: Jackets help good swimmers too if they fall in
Only children need to wear life jackets on boats
Swimmers should hold jackets instead of wearing them
Life jackets are needed only in deep rivers

why.Only children need to wear life jackets: The rule is for everyone, not just children.
why.Swimmers should hold jackets instead of: A jacket must be worn to work, not carried.
why.Life jackets are needed only in deep riv: Ferry water also needs jackets, not only rivers.

activities.explanation: A jacket keeps anyone afloat after a fall, so this is right.

activities.prompt: People want to cut part of an island forest. Its trees grow only on that island. Unique birds and butterflies live there. What may happen if the forest is cut?
options: The unique animals may lose their only home
The animals can easily move to any city
The animals will find the same trees nearby
Nothing will change for the animals at all

why.The animals can easily move to any city: City life is not their home, so they cannot just move there.
why.The animals will find the same trees nea: The same trees do not grow nearby, so this is wrong.
why.Nothing will change for the animals at a: Losing their only home is a big change, so this is wrong.

activities.explanation: The trees and animals are found only there, so this is right.

lessons.sceneAlt: Mangrove tree roots spreading out wide over the mud on Havelock Island in the Andaman Islands.
lessons.sceneCaption: Mangrove roots spread out wide to support the tree in unstable, oxygen-poor mud.

lessons.title: Marine Life and North Sentinel Island

activities.prompt: How can tiny sea creatures and a quiet island hold such big secrets?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Life under the sea, and a special island
activities.body: Rani took the children to the Marine Interpretation Centre. There they learned how tiny corals give shelter to many sea creatures. Marine life matters for the sea and for the whole Earth. Before leaving the island, they heard about North Sentinel Island. Its people live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors, so no one may go there.
keyPoints: Tiny corals give shelter to many creatures.
Marine life is important for the sea and for the whole Earth.
No one is allowed to visit North Sentinel Island.
activities.explanation: The sea is full of life that helps us all, and some peoples choose to live apart.

activities.prompt: Meera sees a picture of a coral. It looks like a small stone. She asks: why do so many fish live near it?
steps: A coral looks small and still, so Meera thinks it cannot help anyone.
But the coral makes shapes like little caves and rooms in the sea.
Tiny creatures need safe places to hide, and the coral gives them shelter.
So one small coral can be a home for many sea creatures.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Why is no one allowed to go to North Sentinel Island?
options: Its people do not want visitors
The island is too far away
There are no boats available
The island has no fresh water
activities.explanation: The people there live as they choose and do not want visitors, so we respect that.

activities.prompt: In ______, a tsunami hit the region near North Sentinel Island.
activities.hint: It was in the early 2000s.
activities.explanation: A tsunami struck the region in 2004. The island's people stayed safe.

activities.prompt: Match each idea with what goes with it.
activities.explanation: Corals shelter creatures, marine life helps the whole Earth, and the island's people were safe in 2004.

activities.prompt: What might have helped the people stay safe during the tsunami?
options: Signs they noticed in nature
A warning from a radio station
Boats that carried them away
A tall wall built of stone
activities.explanation: They possibly noticed signs in nature. Their deep connection with nature might have kept them safe.

activities.prompt: Put the events from your book in the right order.
items: Rani took them to the Marine Interpretation Centre
They learned how tiny corals give shelter to creatures
Before leaving, they heard about North Sentinel Island
They learned the people survived the 2004 tsunami
activities.explanation: That is the order of the story: first the centre, then corals, then the island, then how its people stayed safe.

activities.prompt: Some corals in a reef die. The small caves in them are gone. What will happen to the tiny sea creatures that lived there?
options: They will find new shelter somewhere else.
They will lose their shelter and may be in danger.
They will grow their own coral very fast.
They will move onto the beach to live.

why.They will find new shelter somewhere els: Wrong: the child thinks moving is easy, but creatures need the right shelter.
why.They will grow their own coral very fast: Wrong: the child thinks creatures can make coral, but corals are the shelter-givers.
Wrong: the child mixes up land and sea homes.

activities.explanation: Right: corals give shelter, so losing them means losing a safe home.

activities.prompt: A friend says the sea only needs fish, not corals. Why is this thinking not right?
options: Corals are pretty, so the sea needs them for looks.
Corals are big, so fish cannot live near them.
Corals give shelter, so many creatures need them to live.
Corals are stones, so they do nothing in the sea.

why.Corals are pretty, so the sea needs them: Wrong: the child thinks beauty is the reason corals matter.
why.Corals are big, so fish cannot live near: Wrong: the child thinks big things push creatures away.
why.Corals are stones, so they do nothing in: Wrong: the child thinks a still thing cannot help other living things.

activities.explanation: Right: corals give shelter to many creatures, so the sea needs them.

activities.prompt: A boat captain wants to land on North Sentinel Island to meet the people there. Why should he not go?
options: The island is too small for a boat to land.
The people do not want visitors, so no one may go.
The people are busy fishing every day of the year.
The sea near the island is too deep for boats.

why.The island is too small for a boat to la: Wrong: the child makes up a size problem that is not the reason.
why.The people are busy fishing every day of: Wrong: the child guesses a daily-life reason instead of the real rule.
why.The sea near the island is too deep for: Wrong: the child makes up a sea-depth problem that is not the reason.

activities.explanation: Right: the people do not want visitors, and no one is allowed to go.

lessons.title: Sundarbans: Home of the Mangroves

activities.prompt: How do trees survive in salty, muddy water where nothing else can grow?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Forest Where Rivers Meet the Sea
activities.body: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world. It is where the river Ganga meets the sea. The land there is muddy and salty, yet special trees called mangroves grow happily. Their roots help them breathe in the wet, salty mud. These roots also hold the soil together, so waves cannot wash the land away.
keyPoints: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
It is where the river Ganga meets the sea.
Mangrove roots breathe in muddy salt water and hold the soil together.
activities.explanation: Mangroves are special trees that can grow where most trees cannot.

activities.prompt: Meera sees a mangrove tree. Its roots stick up out of the mud like little knees. She asks: why do the roots grow up and not stay under the ground?
steps: The land there is muddy and full of salt water.
Roots under the mud cannot get enough air to breathe.
So the roots stick up above the mud to take in air.
That is why mangroves can live in wet, salty land where other trees cannot.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What is special about the Sundarbans forest?
options: It is the largest mangrove forest in the world.
It is the driest forest in the world.
It is the coldest forest in the world.
activities.explanation: Well done! The Sundarbans is the biggest mangrove forest anywhere on Earth.

activities.prompt: The Sundarbans is the place where the river Ganga meets the ______.
activities.hint: Think of the big, salty water beyond the beach.
activities.explanation: Yes! The river Ganga meets the sea here, so the land gets water from both.

activities.prompt: Why are the roots of mangroves special?
options: They help the trees breathe in muddy salt water.
They help the trees sleep through winter.
They help the trees float away in floods.
activities.explanation: Great thinking! The roots let mangroves breathe even in wet, salty mud.

activities.prompt: Match each thing with what the lesson says about it.
pairs: meets the sea in the Sundarbans
activities.explanation: Super! You remembered how the roots protect the land and where the river ends.

activities.prompt: In the Sundarbans, tigers may get confused by ______.
activities.hint: People wear something on their face that puzzles the tigers.
activities.explanation: Yes! Tigers may get confused by masks, which helps people stay safe.

activities.prompt: Why do many people live close to the Sundarbans forest?
options: They depend on the forest for what they need.
They want to move the forest to a city.
They are afraid of the wildlife there.
activities.explanation: Well done! People have depended on the forest and lived in harmony with nature for generations.

activities.prompt: Big waves hit two shores. One shore has many mangrove trees. One shore has no trees at all. What will happen?
options: Waves wash away soil on the shore with no trees
Waves wash away soil on the shore with mangroves
Both shores lose the same amount of soil
No waves can reach either of the two shores

why.Waves wash away soil on the shore with m: The mangrove shore is protected by the roots, not washed away.
why.Both shores lose the same amount of soil: The two shores are not the same; one has roots holding the soil.
why.No waves can reach either of the two sho: The waves are already hitting both shores in the situation.

activities.explanation: Right. Mangrove roots hold soil together and stop waves washing land away.

activities.prompt: A child wants to show that a mangrove seed grows best in salty mud. She has two pots and one kind of seed. What should she do?
options: Use salty mud in one pot and plain mud in the other, with same water and sun
Use two different kinds of seeds, one in each pot
Use salty mud in both pots and give them different water
Put one pot in the sun and one pot in a dark room

why.Use two different kinds of seeds, one in: Different seeds grow differently, so the test would not be fair.
why.Use salty mud in both pots and give them: If both pots have salty mud, there is nothing to compare with.
why.Put one pot in the sun and one pot in a: Light would change too, so the test would not be fair.

activities.explanation: Right. Only the salt should change; everything else must stay the same.

activities.prompt: Someone says: 'Cut down all the mangroves. The land near the sea will still be safe from waves.' What is wrong with this claim?
options: Without roots to hold the soil, waves will wash the land away
Cutting mangroves makes the waves much bigger and stronger
Mangrove trees eat the waves and stop them that way
The whole sea will dry up if the mangroves are cut

why.Cutting mangroves makes the waves much b: Waves do not get bigger without trees; the soil just loses its protection.
why.Mangrove trees eat the waves and stop th: Trees do not eat anything; roots hold the soil in place.
why.The whole sea will dry up if the mangrov: Cutting trees cannot make the sea dry up.

activities.explanation: Right. Mangrove roots hold soil together and stop waves washing land away.

lessons.sceneCaption: The Sundarbans is densely covered by mangrove forests on the Ganges Delta in West Bengal, India.

lessons.title: Northeast India: Green Hills and Great Traditions

activities.prompt: Could a tree's roots grow strong enough for people to walk on?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Welcome to the Northeast!
activities.body: After the Sundarbans, Shanti and her family travelled towards the Northeast of India. This part of our country has eight states: Sikkim and seven states called the Seven Sisters. The Northeast is full of colours, creativity and life. People there live closely with nature, in green hills and valleys.
keyPoints: Seven states are called the Seven Sisters.
Sikkim and the Seven Sisters make up Northeast India.
People in the Northeast live closely with nature.
activities.explanation: The Northeast is a special part of India with eight states and lots of green nature.

activities.prompt: Shanti sees a stream in the Northeast. The water is deep. There is no bridge. How can people cross without cutting trees?
steps: The stream is deep, so people cannot walk across the water.
Trees grow near the stream, and their roots can grow long and strong.
If roots grow across the stream, they can join both sides together.
So people can guide the roots, and one day the roots become a bridge to walk on.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Caring for Birds and Building with Roots
activities.body: In the Northeast, people help protect the Hargila bird, the Greater Adjutant Stork. Women are teaching children to help protect the bird's nests. People also grow living root bridges. Roots of trees are grown across streams. Slowly, the roots become strong enough to walk on!
keyPoints: The Hargila is the Greater Adjutant Stork.
Women teach children to protect its nests.
Living root bridges are made from tree roots across streams.
activities.explanation: People and nature work together in the Northeast.

activities.prompt: How many states are called the Seven Sisters?
options: Five
Seven
Nine
activities.explanation: Well done! Seven states together are called the Seven Sisters.

activities.prompt: Which states together make up Northeast India?
options: Only the Seven Sisters
Only Sikkim
Sikkim and the Seven Sisters
activities.explanation: Yes! Sikkim plus the Seven Sisters makes all of Northeast India.

activities.prompt: Bhut Jolokia, the ghost pepper, is one of the hottest chillies in the world.
activities.explanation: True! The ghost pepper is famous for being very, very hot.

activities.prompt: The ghost pepper is used in ______ and chutneys.
activities.hint: A spicy food kept in jars.
activities.explanation: Great! The hot ghost pepper adds fire to pickles and chutneys.

activities.prompt: Match each thing to what you learned about it.
activities.explanation: Super matching! You remembered the special treasures of the Northeast.

activities.prompt: Put the steps of growing a living root bridge in order.
items: Roots of trees are grown across a stream
The roots grow stronger day by day
The roots become strong enough to walk on
activities.explanation: Perfect order! The roots grow across the stream first, then get strong enough to walk on.

activities.prompt: Shanti's family travels from the Sundarbans towards the Northeast of India. They want to see the Seven Sisters and one more state. How many states will they visit in all?
options: Six states
Seven states
Eight states
Nine states

why.Six states: This counts only the Seven Sisters and forgets the extra state.
why.Seven states: This counts only the Seven Sisters and forgets the extra state.
why.Nine states: This adds one state too many by counting something twice.

activities.explanation: Right. Seven Sisters plus Sikkim makes eight states in the Northeast.

activities.prompt: Some children find a Hargila nest with eggs. The nest is low on a tree. The women of the village want the children to help. What should the children do to protect the nest?
options: Throw stones at the nest to move it
Learn from the women how to guard the nest
Climb the tree and take the eggs home
Shake the tree to see the bird fly

why.Throw stones at the nest to move it: Stones can break the eggs and hurt the bird, not protect it.
why.Climb the tree and take the eggs home: Taking eggs home stops the baby birds from ever hatching.
why.Shake the tree to see the bird fly: Shaking the tree can make the nest and eggs fall down.

activities.explanation: Right. Women teach children to help protect the nests of the Hargila.

activities.prompt: Two children cross a stream. One walks over a living root bridge. The other walks over a rope that was tied there last week. After one year, which crossing will be stronger?
options: The rope, because it was tied by people
The root bridge, because its roots keep growing stronger
Both are the same after one year
Neither, because water breaks both of them

why.The rope, because it was tied by people: A rope does not grow. It can get old and weak with time.
why.Both are the same after one year: They are not the same. Roots keep growing but a rope does not.
why.Neither, because water breaks both of th: The root bridge stands over water and still grows strong.

activities.explanation: Right. The roots of a living root bridge grow and become strong enough to walk on.

lessons.sceneCaption: Bhut jolokia, also called ghost pepper, is grown in Assam, Nagaland and Manipur in Northeast India.

lessons.title: Western Ghats and Silent Valley

activities.prompt: Why is a forest called 'silent', and why did people fight to save it?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Chain of Green Hills
activities.body: Far in the west of India runs a long chain of forested hills called the Western Ghats. These hills are a kind of nature's hotspot, because many plants and animals there are not found anywhere else. Tribal communities have lived in these forests for generations. Deep in Kerala lies Silent Valley, a wonderful rainforest with a special story.
keyPoints: The Western Ghats is a long chain of forested hills.
It is a nature's hotspot, full of plants and animals found nowhere else.
Silent Valley National Park is a wonderful rainforest in Kerala.
activities.explanation: These green hills are one of India's greatest treasures of nature.

activities.prompt: A lion-tailed macaque lives in the Western Ghats. Builders cut down its forest. Meera says it can just move to any other forest in India and be happy. Is Meera right?
steps: The Western Ghats is a long chain of forested hills, so this macaque grew up in that special home.
Lion-tailed macaques are only found in the Western Ghats, so other forests in India do not have them.
Because the macaque cannot live anywhere else, losing this forest means losing its only home.
So Meera is wrong; the macaque needs the Western Ghats to survive.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What is the Western Ghats?
options: A wide sandy desert
A group of snowy peaks
A long chain of forested hills
A deep blue lake
activities.explanation: The Western Ghats is a long chain of hills covered with forests. Well done!

activities.prompt: Which of these describes Silent Valley National Park?
options: A dry desert with no trees
A wonderful rainforest in Kerala
A tall snowy mountain
A busy city with tall towers
activities.explanation: Silent Valley is a wonderful rainforest in Kerala. Keep going!

activities.prompt: The Indian Giant ______ is also found in the Western Ghats.
activities.hint: A busy animal with a big bushy tail that loves trees.
activities.explanation: The Indian Giant Squirrel makes its home in these forested hills.

activities.prompt: Match each one to what you learned about it.
pairs: Found only in the Western Ghats
Also found in the Western Ghats
A long chain of forested hills
activities.explanation: You now know the special animals and places of the Western Ghats. Super!

activities.prompt: Why are the Western Ghats hills special for water?
options: They are made of salt
No rain ever falls there
Several rivers of India begin there
They are flat like a plate
activities.explanation: Several rivers of India begin from these hills, so they give water to many places.

activities.prompt: Put the story of Silent Valley's name in order.
items: The rainforest was silent
The valley got its name: Silent Valley
People joined the 'Save Silent Valley Movement'
activities.explanation: First the forest was silent, then came the name, and later people joined together to save it.

activities.prompt: Rescue workers catch a lion-tailed macaque. They want to leave it in a faraway forest in another part of India. What will most likely happen to it there?
options: It will find many friends of its own kind there.
It will not do well, because that is not its home.
It will quickly teach other animals its ways.
It will grow a new tail to match the new forest.

why.It will find many friends of its own kin: Wrong: thinks macaques live everywhere, but they are only found in the Western Ghats.
why.It will quickly teach other animals its: Wrong: thinks animals can just adjust anywhere, missing that this macaque needs its special home.
why.It will grow a new tail to match the new: Wrong: silly idea that animals change their bodies to fit new places.

activities.explanation: Right: lion-tailed macaques are only found in the Western Ghats, so it cannot live well elsewhere.

activities.prompt: A boy saw one lion-tailed macaque in a book. He tells his class that these macaques live in every forest of India. What is the flaw in his claim?
options: Books cannot show pictures of real animals at all.
One picture cannot prove where all the macaques live.
Macaques are too small to live in big forests.
His classmates did not see the picture he saw.

why.Books cannot show pictures of real anima: Wrong: thinks books are useless, but the problem is his jump to a big conclusion.
why.Macaques are too small to live in big fo: Wrong: talks about size, which has nothing to do with where macaques live.
why.His classmates did not see the picture h: Wrong: blames the classmates, not the boy's wrong conclusion.

activities.explanation: Right: lion-tailed macaques are only found in the Western Ghats, so one picture cannot prove they live everywhere.

activities.prompt: The Western Ghats is a long chain of forested hills. Several rivers of India begin from these hills. If many trees on these hills are cut down, what could happen to the rivers?
options: The rivers will get longer and reach more towns.
The rivers will turn salty like the sea.
The rivers may not flow as well as before.
The rivers will freeze because there is less shade.

why.The rivers will get longer and reach mor: Wrong: thinks cutting trees helps rivers grow, which makes no sense.
Wrong: mixes up rivers with the sea, where water is salty.
why.The rivers will freeze because there is: Wrong: thinks shade keeps rivers warm, missing that rivers start from these hills.

activities.explanation: Right: the rivers begin from these hills, so harming the hills can harm the rivers.

activities.prompt: Students surveyed the Western Ghats and recorded over 200 types of mangoes. A girl says this shows the Western Ghats is a special place for nature. Why is her thinking correct?
options: Because mangoes are the biggest fruits in the world.
Because so many kinds show the place is nature's hotspot.
Because students always find the best places for picnics.
Because 200 is a lucky number in many old stories.

why.Because mangoes are the biggest fruits i: Wrong: talks about mango size, which does not explain why the place is special.
why.Because students always find the best pl: Wrong: connects students and picnics, which has nothing to do with the finding.
why.Because 200 is a lucky number in many ol: Wrong: uses a lucky-number idea instead of thinking about many kinds of plants.

activities.explanation: Right: many kinds of living things in one place show it is nature's hotspot.

activities.prompt: Silent Valley is a wonderful rainforest in Kerala. People joined together in the 'Save Silent Valley Movement'. What was most likely the reason people did this?
options: They wanted the valley to stay safe and not be harmed.
They wanted to rename the valley after a famous leader.
They wanted to move all the animals to their homes.
They wanted to build a big school inside the valley.

why.They wanted to rename the valley after a: Wrong: thinks the movement was about names, not about saving the forest.
why.They wanted to move all the animals to t: Wrong: thinks saving means moving animals away, instead of protecting their home.
why.They wanted to build a big school inside: Wrong: thinks the movement was for building, which is the opposite of saving.

activities.explanation: Right: people join a 'save' movement to protect a special place from harm.

activities.context: Shanti's parents were busy planning their summer vacation. Shanti told them she wanted to see more of her country, and they said her wish might come true. They planned a trip to a few different places. The trip would start from the southernmost tip of India, Indira Point, and then move on to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, beginning at their capital city, Sri Vijaya Puram.
activities.prompt: The family lands in the islands and wants to begin sightseeing there. Why is Sri Vijaya Puram a sensible place for them to begin?
options: It is the main city of the island group they are visiting
It is the biggest island in the whole chain
It is the place closest to Indira Point
It is where most of India's wild tigers are found

why.It is the biggest island in the whole ch: Wrong: the passage never says anything about the size of islands.
why.It is the place closest to Indira Point: Wrong: the trip starts at Indira Point and then moves to the islands, so this is not the reason.
why.It is where most of India's wild tigers: Wrong: tigers are not linked to any one city in the facts given.

activities.explanation: Correct: Sri Vijaya Puram is the capital city of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, so it is the main city to start from.

activities.context: Shanti's parents were busy planning their summer vacation. Shanti told them she wanted to see more of her country, and they said her wish might come true. They planned a trip to a few different places. The trip would start from the southernmost tip of India, Indira Point, and then move on to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, beginning at their capital city, Sri Vijaya Puram.
activities.prompt: Shanti's cousin looks at a map and says, 'The Andaman and Nicobar Islands must be one single piece of land.' What should Shanti tell him?
options: It is actually a long chain made up of many separate islands
It is actually one island surrounded by water on all sides
It is actually part of the mainland and not surrounded by water
It is actually over a thousand islands joined to the mainland

why.It is actually one island surrounded by: Wrong: this treats the whole group as a single island, which is the cousin's mistake.
why.It is actually part of the mainland and: Wrong: islands are land surrounded by water on all sides, so they are not joined to the mainland.
why.It is actually over a thousand islands j: Wrong: the over-a-thousand islands fact is about all the seas around India, not islands joined to the mainland.

activities.explanation: Correct: the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a long chain of islands, so the cousin is wrong to call it one piece of land.

activities.prompt: Explain why Shanti's wish might come true.
activities.answer: Shanti wished to see more of her country. Her parents were busy planning their summer vacation, and they planned a trip to a few different places. Since the trip would cover several places, starting from the southernmost tip of India, her parents said her wish might come true.
points: States Shanti's wish to see more of her country
Mentions parents planning the summer vacation
Says the trip covers a few different places
Links the trip to the wish coming true
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Shanti and her family reached the jetty to catch a ferry to a nearby island. Before boarding, a guide gave everyone safety instructions. On the island, Shanti saw trees with big roots spreading out wide. She was curious about them. She also spotted birds found only on these islands, and heard that the forests are home to many unique animals, birds, butterflies and insects.
activities.prompt: Shanti's guide says one of the birds she saw cannot be seen anywhere else in the world. Which bird could it be?
options: The Andaman wood pigeon
The house sparrow
The peacock
The crow

why.The house sparrow: Sparrows are common everywhere, not unique to the islands.
why.The peacock: Peacocks are common mainland birds, not island-only.
why.The crow: Crows are found almost everywhere, so not unique.

activities.explanation: Correct: it is found only on these islands.

activities.context: Shanti and her family reached the jetty to catch a ferry to a nearby island. Before boarding, a guide gave everyone safety instructions. On the island, Shanti saw trees with big roots spreading out wide. She was curious about them. She also spotted birds found only on these islands, and heard that the forests are home to many unique animals, birds, butterflies and insects.
activities.prompt: Uncle Ravi says he swims very well, so he puts his life jacket aside while boarding the ferry. What is the most likely result if he follows the safety instructions wrongly?
options: If he falls into the water, nothing may keep him afloat
The ferry will not be able to start its journey
He will be asked to drive the ferry instead
The trees on the island will not grow properly

why.The ferry will not be able to start its: The ferry's journey does not depend on one passenger's jacket.
why.He will be asked to drive the ferry inst: Wearing or not wearing a jacket has nothing to do with driving the ferry.
why.The trees on the island will not grow pr: Tree growth on the island is unrelated to his jacket.

activities.explanation: Correct: without a life jacket, falling in is dangerous even for good swimmers.

activities.context: Shanti and her family reached the jetty to catch a ferry to a nearby island. Before boarding, a guide gave everyone safety instructions. On the island, Shanti saw trees with big roots spreading out wide. She was curious about them. She also spotted birds found only on these islands, and heard that the forests are home to many unique animals, birds, butterflies and insects.
activities.prompt: Shanti wonders what would happen to a tree if its big roots did NOT spread out wide. What should she conclude?
options: The tree may not be supported well and could lean or fall
The tree would grow taller than before
The tree would start catching a ferry to another island
The tree would attract more butterflies and insects

why.The tree would grow taller than before: Nothing in the roots' spreading makes a tree taller.
why.The tree would start catching a ferry to: Trees cannot travel on ferries; this is impossible.
why.The tree would attract more butterflies: Butterflies and insects live in the forests, not because of one tree's roots.

activities.explanation: Correct: wide-spreading roots are what support the tree.

activities.prompt: Explain why these island forests are special and important to protect.
activities.answer: These forests are special because many of their trees are unique and found only there. They are also home to many unique animals, birds, butterflies and insects, like the Andaman wood pigeon and Andaman hornbill, which are found only here. If the forests are harmed, these living things could be lost, so they must be protected.
points: Mentions trees unique to the islands
Mentions unique animals, birds, butterflies and insects
Names the Andaman wood pigeon and Andaman hornbill as found only here
Gives a reason for protection (losing them forever)
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: During her holiday on an island, Rani took her cousins to the Marine Interpretation Centre. There they saw how tiny corals give shelter to many creatures, and learned that marine life matters for the sea and the whole Earth. Before leaving, a guide spoke about North Sentinel Island, where people live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors. The cousins asked if their boat could sail close to it. The guide shook his head and shared how, in 2004, a tsunami hit the region, yet those people survived, possibly noticing signs in nature.
activities.prompt: The cousins' boat captain says he can take them near North Sentinel Island for a better view. What should the cousins do?
options: Ask the captain to sail closer but stay on the boat
Tell the captain they cannot go, because no one is allowed to go there
Go only if the people on the island wave at them
Take photographs from far away and later visit the island

why.Ask the captain to sail closer but stay: Staying on the boat still means going near, which the island people do not want
why.Go only if the people on the island wave: A wave cannot give permission; the people have said they do not want visitors
why.Take photographs from far away and later: Photographs do not change the rule, and visiting later is still forbidden

activities.explanation: Correct: the rule is that no one is allowed to go there, so the trip must be dropped

activities.context: During her holiday on an island, Rani took her cousins to the Marine Interpretation Centre. There they saw how tiny corals give shelter to many creatures, and learned that marine life matters for the sea and the whole Earth. Before leaving, a guide spoke about North Sentinel Island, where people live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors. The cousins asked if their boat could sail close to it. The guide shook his head and shared how, in 2004, a tsunami hit the region, yet those people survived, possibly noticing signs in nature.
activities.prompt: If the tiny corals near Rani's island were harmed, what would most likely happen next?
options: The many creatures that corals give shelter to would lose their shelter
The sea would become larger and cover the island
The people of North Sentinel Island would move to a new island
The Marine Interpretation Centre would close down

why.The sea would become larger and cover th: Corals sheltering creatures has nothing to do with the sea growing bigger
why.The people of North Sentinel Island woul: The island people keep to themselves and would not move because of corals elsewhere
why.The Marine Interpretation Centre would c: A centre closing is not a natural result of corals being harmed

activities.explanation: Correct: corals give shelter to many creatures, so harming corals takes that shelter away

activities.prompt: What is the difference between how the people of North Sentinel Island live and how the tourists around Rani live?
activities.answer: The people of North Sentinel Island live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors, so no one is allowed to go there. Tourists like Rani's group travel, visit centres, and move freely by boat. The island people live apart by choice, while tourists depend on outside places.
points: Says the island people live like ancient hunter-gatherers
Says they do not want visitors and no one is allowed to go there
Describes tourists as people who travel and visit places
Brings out the contrast between the two ways of living
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Last winter, Aarav's family flew to Kolkata, stopped there briefly, and then travelled on to the Sundarbans. He saw muddy, salty ground covered with mangrove trees whose roots stuck out to breathe. A guide explained that the roots also grip the soil so waves cannot drag it away, and that villagers wear masks near the tiger forest. Aarav felt he had entered a place where land, water and animals share one home.
activities.prompt: The guide says the roots 'grip the soil'. Why does this matter to the villagers whose homes stand near the water?
options: The roots give villagers wood for building their boats.
The roots keep the ground from being carried off by the water, so the homes stay safe.
The roots make the water salty enough for the fish to live in.
The roots soak up the mud so that boats can sail easily.

why.The roots give villagers wood for buildi: The guide described roots holding the land, not supplying wood.
why.The roots make the water salty enough fo: The water is salty because the river meets the sea, not because of the roots.
why.The roots soak up the mud so that boats: Roots do not remove mud; boats travel through water channels, not because of roots.

activities.explanation: Correct - by holding the soil, the roots protect the shore where people live.

activities.context: Last winter, Aarav's family flew to Kolkata, stopped there briefly, and then travelled on to the Sundarbans. He saw muddy, salty ground covered with mangrove trees whose roots stuck out to breathe. A guide explained that the roots also grip the soil so waves cannot drag it away, and that villagers wear masks near the tiger forest. Aarav felt he had entered a place where land, water and animals share one home.
activities.prompt: What would most likely happen to the ground in the Sundarbans if all the mangrove trees were cut down?
options: The ground would slowly become less salty.
The waves would gradually wash the ground away.
The ground would dry out and turn hard.
New mangrove trees would grow back faster than before.

why.The ground would slowly become less salt: The salt comes from the sea water, not from the trees, so cutting them changes nothing about salt.
The land is wet because of the river and sea around it; the trees are not what keep it wet.
why.New mangrove trees would grow back faste: Cutting trees down cannot make regrowth quicker; there would be no roots to protect the soil meanwhile.

activities.explanation: Correct - without roots holding it, nothing stops the waves from removing the soil.

activities.context: Last winter, Aarav's family flew to Kolkata, stopped there briefly, and then travelled on to the Sundarbans. He saw muddy, salty ground covered with mangrove trees whose roots stuck out to breathe. A guide explained that the roots also grip the soil so waves cannot drag it away, and that villagers wear masks near the tiger forest. Aarav felt he had entered a place where land, water and animals share one home.
activities.prompt: Why did the guide tell the villagers to wear masks when they go near the tiger forest?
options: A tiger cannot tell that a human is behind the mask.
A mask protects the face from mosquito bites in the muddy air.
A mask hides a villager from other villagers he does not know.
A mask keeps away the bad smell of the salt water.

why.A mask protects the face from mosquito b: Masks are advised because of tigers, not because of insects.
why.A mask hides a villager from other villa: Villagers know one another; a mask is not meant to hide people from people.
why.A mask keeps away the bad smell of the s: Smell is not the danger here; the mask is about what the tiger sees.

activities.explanation: Correct - the mask hides the human face, so the tiger is unsure what it is seeing.

activities.context: After leaving the Sundarbans, Shanti and her family travelled towards the Northeast of India. In a village, her aunt showed her a bridge made from the roots of trees growing across a stream. In the kitchen, a very spicy chilli was being made into pickles and chutneys. Near the village, women were teaching children how to help protect the nests of a large bird. Shanti saw that people here live closely with nature.
activities.prompt: The children in the village are being taught to protect the Hargila nests. What is most likely to happen if they keep doing this?
options: More Hargila chicks will grow up safely in their nests
The Hargila birds will move away to the Sundarbans
The nests will become too heavy for the trees
The children will have to build new nests themselves

why.The Hargila birds will move away to the: Wrong: nothing in the case suggests the birds would leave; protection keeps them safe where they are.
why.The nests will become too heavy for the: Wrong: protecting nests does not change their weight or harm the trees.
why.The children will have to build new nest: Wrong: the children are helping protect existing nests, not building new ones.

activities.explanation: Correct: when nests are protected, the young birds inside are safe and more chicks survive.

activities.context: After leaving the Sundarbans, Shanti and her family travelled towards the Northeast of India. In a village, her aunt showed her a bridge made from the roots of trees growing across a stream. In the kitchen, a very spicy chilli was being made into pickles and chutneys. Near the village, women were teaching children how to help protect the nests of a large bird. Shanti saw that people here live closely with nature.
activities.prompt: Shanti's aunt usually makes chutney with Bhut Jolokia. One day she uses a very mild chilli instead. What will change?
options: The chutney will taste much less spicy than before
The chutney will become one of the hottest in the world
The chutney will turn into a pickle instead of a chutney
The chutney will grow from the roots of trees

why.The chutney will become one of the hotte: Wrong: a mild chilli cannot make the chutney hotter; only a very hot chilli like Bhut Jolokia can.
why.The chutney will turn into a pickle inst: Wrong: changing the chilli does not change whether it is a chutney or a pickle.
why.The chutney will grow from the roots of: Wrong: chutney is made in a kitchen, not grown from roots.

activities.explanation: Correct: Bhut Jolokia is one of the hottest chillies, so a mild chilli will make the chutney far less spicy.

activities.context: After leaving the Sundarbans, Shanti and her family travelled towards the Northeast of India. In a village, her aunt showed her a bridge made from the roots of trees growing across a stream. In the kitchen, a very spicy chilli was being made into pickles and chutneys. Near the village, women were teaching children how to help protect the nests of a large bird. Shanti saw that people here live closely with nature.
activities.prompt: Another village nearby wants a way to cross a stream without cutting trees or using machines. Following the example in Shanti's village, what should they do?
options: Grow tree roots across the stream until they are strong enough to walk on
Cut down a tree and lay it across the stream
Ask the Hargila birds to carry people across the stream
Pick the hottest chillies and throw them into the stream

why.Cut down a tree and lay it across the st: Wrong: cutting a tree goes against the idea of living closely with nature.
why.Ask the Hargila birds to carry people ac: Wrong: birds cannot carry people across a stream.
why.Pick the hottest chillies and throw them: Wrong: chillies are used for pickles and chutneys, not for crossing streams.

activities.explanation: Correct: living root bridges are made by growing tree roots across streams until they can be walked on, which needs no cutting.

activities.prompt: What is the difference between the 'Seven Sisters' and Northeast India?
activities.answer: The 'Seven Sisters' is the name given to seven states of India. Northeast India is a bigger group because it is made up of the Seven Sisters together with one more state, Sikkim. So Northeast India has one more state than the Seven Sisters.
points: Says the Seven Sisters are seven states
Says Northeast India is made of the Seven Sisters plus Sikkim
Makes clear that Northeast India is the larger group
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: A school club visits a long chain of forested hills in Kerala. They spot a large squirrel with a bushy tail, hear macaques calling, and see a river flowing down. A guide says a rainforest valley nearby was once saved when people joined together to protect it. The club wonders why these hills are so special and what could happen if the forests were cut down.
activities.prompt: If the forests on these hills were cut down, which of the following would be the most serious loss?
options: Animals like the lion-tailed macaque would have nowhere to live anywhere in the world
The hills would become taller over time
The students would find fewer types of mangoes to eat at home
The tribal communities would move to a nearby city for a holiday

why.The hills would become taller over time: Wrong: cutting forests does not change the height of hills
why.The students would find fewer types of m: Wrong: mangoes were recorded by students, but the bigger loss is animals found nowhere else
why.The tribal communities would move to a n: Wrong: forest-dwelling people live there for generations; moving for a holiday is not a loss of the forest

activities.explanation: Correct: since macaques are found only here, losing the forest means losing them everywhere

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Some Unique Places

activities.prompt: Shanti's trip started from the southernmost tip of India. What is this place called?
options: Sri Vijaya Puram
Kolkata
Indira Point
Silent Valley
activities.explanation: Indira Point is the southernmost tip of India. That is where the family trip began!

activities.prompt: On the ferry, everyone had to wear a life jacket, even people who could swim.
activities.explanation: Life jackets keep you afloat if you fall into water. Safety rules are for everyone!

activities.prompt: Match each place to what it is famous for.
pairs: capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
largest mangrove forest in the world
a long chain of forested hills
activities.explanation: Each special place you visited has its own wonder. Well matched!

activities.prompt: Some people wear masks when they are near the Sundarbans forest. Why?
options: Tigers may get confused by masks
Masks keep the muddy water away
Masks help people walk on soft soil
activities.explanation: Tigers may get confused by masks. It is a clever way for people and tigers to stay out of each other's way.

activities.prompt: The people of North Sentinel Island warmly welcome visitors from outside.
activities.explanation: They live like ancient hunter-gatherers and do not want visitors. No one is allowed to go there, and we respect that.

activities.prompt: The land in the Sundarbans is muddy and salty. How do mangrove roots help the trees there?
options: They hold fresh rainwater for dry days
They help the trees breathe in muddy salt water
They make the salty land turn sweet
activities.explanation: Mangrove roots help the trees breathe in muddy salt water. They also hold the soil together against waves.

activities.prompt: Sikkim and the ______ Sisters together make up Northeast India.
activities.hint: Count the days in a week!
activities.explanation: Seven states are called the Seven Sisters. With Sikkim, they make up Northeast India.

activities.prompt: Match each thing to the special job it does.
pairs: spread out wide and support the tree
grow strong enough to walk on
keep you afloat if you fall in water
activities.explanation: Roots, bridges and jackets each do a life-saving job. You know them all now!

activities.prompt: Put the places of Shanti's trip in the order she visited them.
items: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Sundarbans
Northeast India
Western Ghats
activities.explanation: The trip began at the southernmost tip in the islands, then went to the Sundarbans, then the Northeast, and finally the Western Ghats. What a journey!
