activities.context: Meera's class saw a photograph of the Earth taken from high up in space. The Earth looked tiny and completely one, like a single blue ball. Meera tried hard to find her own village and her state on it, but she could not. Her teacher asked the class to say what they could actually see in the photograph and what it teaches us about our planet.
activities.prompt: Meera could not find her village in the photograph. Why did this happen?
options: Because her village was covered by clouds that day
Because from space we cannot see small details, only broad shapes of land masses and the sea
Because her village was too far away from the camera's country
Because villages do not appear in photographs taken from space at all

why.Because her village was covered by cloud: Wrong: clouds are not the reason given; the real reason is about how things look from space.
why.Because her village was too far away fro: Wrong: the camera's country has nothing to do with it; the view from space is the same for everyone.
why.Because villages do not appear in photog: Wrong: villages are not invisible in photos; they are simply too small a detail to be seen from space.

activities.explanation: Correct: from space only broad shapes of land masses and the sea can be seen, not small details like a village.

activities.context: Meera's class saw a photograph of the Earth taken from high up in space. The Earth looked tiny and completely one, like a single blue ball. Meera tried hard to find her own village and her state on it, but she could not. Her teacher asked the class to say what they could actually see in the photograph and what it teaches us about our planet.
activities.prompt: If an astronaut from a different country looked at the same Earth from space, what would that astronaut most likely see?
options: Lines dividing the Earth into different countries
Only the astronaut's own country clearly marked
The Earth looking completely one, with no borders visible
Names of states written across the land

why.Lines dividing the Earth into different: Wrong: no border can be seen from outside, so no dividing lines appear.
why.Only the astronaut's own country clearly: Wrong: from space no country stands out; small details cannot be seen.
why.Names of states written across the land: Wrong: names of states are things people draw on maps, not things visible from space.

activities.explanation: Correct: from outside the Earth looks completely one, and it seems that no borders, states or countries exist.

activities.context: Meera's class saw a photograph of the Earth taken from high up in space. The Earth looked tiny and completely one, like a single blue ball. Meera tried hard to find her own village and her state on it, but she could not. Her teacher asked the class to say what they could actually see in the photograph and what it teaches us about our planet.
activities.prompt: After seeing the photograph, what should Meera conclude about the Earth and the people living on it?
options: Only people of one country truly belong to the Earth
We all are part of humanity and the Earth is our one home
Each state on Earth is a separate home for its own people
The Earth belongs mainly to those who travel to space

why.Only people of one country truly belong: Wrong: the Earth looks completely one from outside, so it cannot belong to only one country's people.
why.Each state on Earth is a separate home f: Wrong: from space it seems that no states exist, so states cannot be separate homes.
why.The Earth belongs mainly to those who tr: Wrong: the Earth is the home of all humanity, not only of space travellers.

activities.explanation: Correct: since no borders are seen from space, everyone is part of humanity and shares the Earth as one home.

activities.prompt: Explain why no borders can be seen when the Earth is viewed from space.
activities.answer: From high up in space, the Earth looks tiny, so we cannot see small details like our city or village. We only see broad shapes of land masses and the sea. Since borders are small details drawn by people, they cannot be seen, and the Earth looks completely one.
points: Earth looks tiny from space
Small details like cities or villages cannot be seen
Only broad shapes of land masses and the sea are visible
So the Earth looks completely one with no borders
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera lives in Kochi with her family. Her school pencil was made in a factory far away, and the biscuits in her lunch box come from another state. Her cousin in Punjab sends mangoes every summer. Last week, rain clouds that formed over the sea watered her garden. Meera wonders how her small town is connected to so many places.
activities.prompt: Why did the rain clouds that formed over the sea water Meera's garden in Kochi?
options: Clouds drift with the wind and do not stop where people draw lines on a map
Clouds follow the roads and railway lines between states
Someone carried the clouds from the sea to Kochi in a truck
Clouds only form directly above the place where they fall

why.Clouds follow the roads and railway line: Wrong: clouds move in the sky, not along roads or tracks
why.Someone carried the clouds from the sea: Wrong: clouds cannot be transported by people; they move on their own
why.Clouds only form directly above the plac: Wrong: the case itself says the clouds formed over the sea but fell on the garden

activities.explanation: Correct: clouds, like air and water, travel naturally without regard to human-made borders

activities.context: Meera lives in Kochi with her family. Her school pencil was made in a factory far away, and the biscuits in her lunch box come from another state. Her cousin in Punjab sends mangoes every summer. Last week, rain clouds that formed over the sea watered her garden. Meera wonders how her small town is connected to so many places.
activities.prompt: Meera's cousin in Punjab can send mangoes to Kerala, and she can eat them happily. What does this show about people in different places?
options: They are joined together through sharing, so things grown in one place can reach another
They must live in the same house to share food
Mangoes can only grow in Punjab and nowhere else
People in Kerala cannot eat anything grown outside their own garden

why.They must live in the same house to shar: Wrong: people do not need to live together to share things across distances
why.Mangoes can only grow in Punjab and nowh: Wrong: nothing in the case says mangoes grow only in Punjab
why.People in Kerala cannot eat anything gro: Wrong: the case shows the opposite, since Meera eats things from other places

activities.explanation: Correct: sharing food and goods is one way people in different places are connected

activities.context: Meera lives in Kochi with her family. Her school pencil was made in a factory far away, and the biscuits in her lunch box come from another state. Her cousin in Punjab sends mangoes every summer. Last week, rain clouds that formed over the sea watered her garden. Meera wonders how her small town is connected to so many places.
activities.prompt: What would most likely happen if every country somehow built a wall that stopped air, water and seeds from crossing it?
options: It would fail, because these things keep moving naturally no matter what people do
The air inside each country would become sweeter and fresher
Rain would fall more evenly in every country
Seeds would grow into stronger plants behind the wall

why.The air inside each country would become: Wrong: blocking air would not make it fresher; air needs to move
why.Rain would fall more evenly in every cou: Wrong: stopping moving water and clouds would not make rain more even
why.Seeds would grow into stronger plants be: Wrong: seeds need to travel and spread; trapping them would not help plants

activities.explanation: Correct: air, water and seeds move freely by nature, so a human wall cannot stop them

activities.prompt: What is the difference between the lines people draw between countries and the way nature works?
activities.answer: People draw lines between countries on maps, but nature has no boundaries. Air, water, clouds, seeds and animals keep moving freely across the whole world, ignoring these lines. So the lines exist only on paper and in people's minds, while nature treats the whole Earth as one connected home.
points: Says people draw borders or lines between countries
Says nature has no boundaries
Gives examples like air, water, clouds, seeds or animals moving freely
Points out that the lines do not stop nature
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera's uncle owns a farm near Delhi. One winter morning, Meera sees huge flocks of pink and black birds landing on the fields. Her uncle smiles and says these visitors have flown a very long way from cold lands like southern Russia and Mongolia. He tells her that last year, when fewer birds came, his fields suffered more damage from locusts and grasshoppers.
activities.prompt: Why is Meera's uncle happy to see the flocks arrive on his farm?
options: The birds will eat the locusts and grasshoppers that damage his crops
The birds will build nests that make his crops grow taller
The birds will drink all the water so pests cannot survive
The birds will carry away his harvested grain to store it safely

why.The birds will build nests that make his: Wrong: the passage says nothing about nests helping crops grow
why.The birds will drink all the water so pe: Wrong: the birds help by eating pests, not by removing water
why.The birds will carry away his harvested: Wrong: the birds eat insects, they do not store grain for farmers

activities.explanation: Correct: the birds feed on locusts and grasshoppers, so they protect his crops

activities.context: Meera's uncle owns a farm near Delhi. One winter morning, Meera sees huge flocks of pink and black birds landing on the fields. Her uncle smiles and says these visitors have flown a very long way from cold lands like southern Russia and Mongolia. He tells her that last year, when fewer birds came, his fields suffered more damage from locusts and grasshoppers.
activities.prompt: If the birds could not fly safely to India one winter, what would most likely happen on Meera's uncle's farm?
options: More locusts and grasshoppers would attack his crops
The locusts and grasshoppers would all fly away to Russia
His crops would grow faster without the birds around
New birds would hatch from his fields to replace the flocks

why.The locusts and grasshoppers would all f: Wrong: pests do not fly off to Russia just because the birds are absent
why.His crops would grow faster without the: Wrong: fewer birds means more pests, not faster-growing crops
why.New birds would hatch from his fields to: Wrong: birds cannot simply hatch out of fields to take the flocks' place

activities.explanation: Correct: without the birds eating them, the pests would increase and harm crops

activities.context: Meera's uncle owns a farm near Delhi. One winter morning, Meera sees huge flocks of pink and black birds landing on the fields. Her uncle smiles and says these visitors have flown a very long way from cold lands like southern Russia and Mongolia. He tells her that last year, when fewer birds came, his fields suffered more damage from locusts and grasshoppers.
activities.prompt: The flocks fly thousands of kilometres from southern Russia and Mongolia to India every winter. What does this safe, free journey of the birds show us?
options: Nature is deeply connected, so animals can move freely and safely
Birds only travel to countries that have the biggest farms
Birds prefer cold countries and only visit India by mistake
Birds travel long distances only to escape other birds

why.Birds only travel to countries that have: Wrong: the birds come for food and warmth, not because of farm size
why.Birds prefer cold countries and only vis: Wrong: they leave cold lands in winter, so visiting India is not a mistake
why.Birds travel long distances only to esca: Wrong: nothing in the lesson says they travel to escape other birds

activities.explanation: Correct: free and safe movement of animals shows nature is deeply connected

activities.prompt: How does yoga connect a person with nature? Explain using what you have learnt.
activities.answer: Since ancient times, people in India practised yoga to keep their bodies healthy and their minds peaceful. Yoga was a way to live in harmony with oneself and with nature. Later, travellers, scholars and teachers from India shared yoga with the world, and today it is practised in almost every country.
points: Says yoga gives a healthy body and a peaceful mind
States yoga means living in harmony with oneself and nature
Mentions that people from India shared yoga with the world
Notes that yoga is now practised in almost every country
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera's grandfather tells her an old family story. Long ago, their ancestors used only black pepper to make food spicy. Then travellers from Portugal sailed from South America and brought chilli plants to India. The plants liked the new soil and climate, entered Indian kitchens, and soon everyone loved them. Meanwhile, sugarcane juice was turned into jaggery in India, and this method travelled abroad with traders, along with rice, mangoes and bananas.
activities.prompt: What would most likely have happened if the travellers from Portugal had never brought chilli plants to India?
options: Indian kitchens would have continued using black pepper as the main spice
Chilli plants would have grown in India on their own anyway
People in India would have stopped eating spicy food completely
South American farmers would have sailed to India to teach farming

why.Chilli plants would have grown in India: Wrong: the passage says chillies were found only in South America, so they could not reach India by themselves.
why.People in India would have stopped eatin: Wrong: people loved spicy food, so they would not give up spicing; they had black pepper.
why.South American farmers would have sailed: Wrong: the story only tells of travellers from Portugal bringing chillies, not farmers coming to teach.

activities.explanation: Correct: before chilli arrived, black pepper was the spice people used, so it would have stayed in use.

activities.context: Meera's grandfather tells her an old family story. Long ago, their ancestors used only black pepper to make food spicy. Then travellers from Portugal sailed from South America and brought chilli plants to India. The plants liked the new soil and climate, entered Indian kitchens, and soon everyone loved them. Meanwhile, sugarcane juice was turned into jaggery in India, and this method travelled abroad with traders, along with rice, mangoes and bananas.
activities.prompt: A trader from a faraway land visits India long ago. He tastes something sweet that his people have never known. What should he most sensibly do?
options: Learn the method of making jaggery from sugarcane juice and carry the knowledge home
Buy bags of black pepper instead, since that is the famous spice
Take chilli seeds home so his people can make their food spicy
Ask Indian traders to keep the sweet method secret from everyone else

why.Buy bags of black pepper instead, since: Wrong: black pepper is spicy, not sweet, so it is not what he tasted.
why.Take chilli seeds home so his people can: Wrong: chillies are spicy, not sweet, so they do not match what he tasted.
why.Ask Indian traders to keep the sweet met: Wrong: the story says the knowledge actually spread through trade and travel, not that it was kept secret.

activities.explanation: Correct: the sweet thing is jaggery, and its making was first discovered in India; traders carried such knowledge to other lands.

activities.prompt: Explain why people in India today cannot imagine food without chillies, even though chilli plants were not originally from India.
activities.answer: Chilli plants were found only in South America long ago. Travellers from Portugal brought them to India 400 to 500 years ago. They found suitable soil and climate, entered Indian kitchens, and people loved them so much that food without chillies now seems unthinkable.
points: States that chillies originally came only from South America
Mentions travellers from Portugal bringing them to India
Notes the new soil and climate suited the plants
Says people loved chillies so much they entered everyday food
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Meera helps her grandmother string bright orange and yellow marigolds for Diwali. She notices the same flowers at the temple, at a neighbour's wedding, and in market stalls everywhere. Her cousin Joao lives in Brazil. He tells her that most of his country's milk comes from cows whose ancestors came from India, and that these cows appear on Brazilian stamps and coins. Meera wonders how the two countries share so much.
activities.prompt: Joao's teacher asks the class why Brazil's milk depends so much on three Indian cow breeds. What should Joao say?
options: Because the Indian cows settled well in Brazil, gave plenty of milk, and their numbers grew over time.
Because Brazil has no other cows besides these three breeds.
Because the pictures on stamps and coins make people buy more milk.
Because the cows were brought to Brazil only a few years ago.

why.Because Brazil has no other cows besides: Wrong: Brazil has other cows; the point is that these three breeds give most of the milk.
why.Because the pictures on stamps and coins: Wrong: stamps and coins honour the cows; they do not cause the milk supply.
why.Because the cows were brought to Brazil: Wrong: the cows were taken to Brazil long ago, not recently.

activities.explanation: Correct: the cows were strong, gave good milk, did not mind the weather, and grew in number over time.

boss.title: Chapter challenge: Earth — Our Shared Home

activities.prompt: Astronauts look at the Earth from space. What does our planet look like to them?
options: Covered in border lines
Flat like a plate
Tiny, with broad shapes of land and sea
Hidden behind thick clouds
activities.explanation: From high up in space, the Earth looks tiny. We only see broad shapes of land and sea, not small details like our city.

activities.prompt: From space, you can clearly see the borders between countries.
activities.explanation: No border can be seen from outside. Nature has no boundaries, so the Earth looks completely one.

activities.prompt: When Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma saw India from space, he said 'Saare Jahaan Se ______'.
activities.hint: It means 'better than the whole world'.
activities.explanation: Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian to see the Earth from space. His words made everyone proud.

activities.prompt: Rosy starlings visit India every winter. How do they help farmers?
options: By eating locusts and grasshoppers
By carrying seeds on their feathers
By singing to the crops
By bringing rain with them
activities.explanation: These pink and black birds feed on locusts and grasshoppers. By eating pests on crops, they help farmers.

activities.prompt: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla was the first Indian to reach the International Space Station.
activities.explanation: Well remembered! He shared inspiring words with the then Prime Minister of India.

activities.prompt: Put the chilli's journey to India in the right order.
items: Chilli plants grew only in South America
Travellers from Portugal brought chillies to India
The chillies found new soil and a new climate
Chillies entered Indian kitchens
People loved chillies so much that food without them is hard to imagine
activities.explanation: The chilli travelled from South America with Portuguese travellers about 400 to 500 years ago. Before that, people used black pepper to spice food.

activities.prompt: The United Nations declared 21 ______ as International Day of Yoga.
activities.hint: It is the month when summer begins in India.
activities.explanation: Yoga has been practised in India for more than 3,000 years. Today it is practised in almost every country.

activities.prompt: There is a saying from ancient India: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'. What does it mean?
options: The world is a market
The world is one family
The world is a school
The world is a race
activities.explanation: It means the world is one family. All people, animals, trees, rivers, air and sky belong to this family.

activities.prompt: The Gir, Kankrej and Ongole cow breeds were taken from Brazil to India long ago.
activities.explanation: It was the other way round! Portuguese traders took Indian cows to Brazil, and today more than three-fourths of Brazil's milk comes from these breeds.
